articleTitle: Microwave Imaging with Modified Stack Type PIFA Antenna utilizing SAR Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper describes a Planer Inverted F Antenna (PIFA) that can be used as a microwave imaging transducer. The planned antenna has a peak gain of 4.6 dBi at 1.7 GHz and operates between 1.68 and 1.71 GHz. The shape and performance of the proposed antenna are first investigated. This study investigates its applicability for imaging two cylindrical metallic objects followed by a metallic beam veiled by a cotton material.

articleTitle: Penta-band Planar Inverted F Antenna for Wireless Communication Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this work, a multi band Planar Inverted F Antenna (PIFA) is introduced for wireless communication applications. Initially a basic PIFA is designed. This is followed by extensive modifications to obtain five different bands namely 0.76 - 0.81 GHz, 1.01 - 1.02 GHz, 1.59 - 1.61 GHz, 1.85 - 1.95 GHz and 2.56 - 2.76 GHz. The designed antenna is tested next on human head phantom by finding the specific absorption rate (SAR) value. The obtained SAR values complies both with the American and European standards proving that the proposed antenna can be utilized for communication applications.

articleTitle: Brain Tumor Detection with Compact Monopole Antennas using Microwave Medical Imaging
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this work, a star shaped patch with an outer ring structure is designed in the simulator for microwave head imaging applications. The designed antenna operatres from 1.47 GHz to 4.7 GHz with an impedance matching of greater than 10 dB. The antenna attains a peak gain of 3.8 dBi at 4.3 GHz. The Specific Absorption rate (SAR) of the designed antenna is checked to evaluate the effect of the antenna on the human head. This is done by separately designing a 7 layered head phantom. The antenna is also utilized to image brain tumor by introducing a cancerous tumor inside the brain phatom for imaging. Finally, brain tumor is obtained successfully after imaging using widely popular Delay and Sum (DAS) algorithm.

articleTitle: Wearable, Conformal, Compact and Flexible F-Slot Monopole Antenna on Textile For Non - Invasive Biomedical Imaging
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This work introduces a compact, flexible, and conformal F-slot monopole antenna for detecting cancer in human arm. This put forward antenna is composed of two flexible materials. One material is denim with a dimension 10 × 10 mm<sup>2</sup>and the other is felt with a dimension 10 × 15 mm<sup>2</sup>. The structure is integrated with six metamaterial unit cells to enhance its gain, directivity and bandwidth throughout the operating band. The proposed antenna operates over 5.6 - 58.6 GHz with return loss greater than 10 dB. The antenna attains maximum gain of 6 dBi at 43 GHz. The antenna is further attached to a human arm phantom developed in the simulator for obtaining the required signals for imaging a cancerous tissue embedded in the skin layer of the designed phantom.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Single Layer C/X-band Conformal Shared Aperture Antenna Array for Spaceborne SAR Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: SAR (Synthetic Aperture Radar) is a form of radar that generates two-dimensional images of a particular object. It employs microwave to collect RADAR images in all weather conditions. Spaceborne SAR systems are increasingly being employed to obtain high-quality images in Earth Observation missions. This article presents a unique conformal shared aperture antenna (SAA) that works in both the C and X bands on a single layer. The C band working frequency is 5.35 GHz, while the X-band working frequency is 9.65 GHz. For spaceborne SAR applications, a single layer C/X-band conformal SAA array with linear polarization of 4 elements (2x2) in C band and 4 elements (2x2) in X-band is proposed. The new technique is presented for simulating conformal Shared aperture antenna arrays. A corporate feeding technique is used in the designing of conformal shared aperture antennas. For the ±25° scan range criteria, the spacing between two patches is 0.7λ. The proposed SAA array size is 130 mm x 80 mm × 0.8 mm. According to simulations, the designed antenna array exhibits impedance bandwidths of 65 MHz and 354 MHz in the C and X bands respectively. The characteristics of the antenna array is simulated and also examined. The performance characteristics of the conformal arrays are compared with planar arrays.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of the $2\times 2$ Patch Antenna Array with Modified Fractal Antenna for 5G Communication and Wireless Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Modern communication demands wide bandwidth, high gain, and efficient reduced-size antennas to provide improved performance over a wide bandwidth range of the frequency spectrum. Here two antennas are taken, of which the first one is a fractal antenna and the second one is a <tex>$\mathbf{2}\times \mathbf{2}$</tex> array antenna. This paper compares the performances of the modified fractal antenna and <tex>$\mathbf{2}\times \mathbf{2}$</tex> patch array antenna. The modified fractal antenna has an FR-4 substrate with 2.4mm width and 2.4mm length and various rectangular slots through which the antenna has a wide bandwidth notch near 21 GHz with 2.77 GHz bandwidth, 25 GHz with 1.82 GHz bandwidth, 32 GHz with 4.23 GHz bandwidth, and 36.5 GHz with 2.94GHz bandwidth. It covers 5G applications in the range of 23.88-25.7GHz and 29.89-34.14GHz. On the other hand, the size of the <tex>$\mathbf{2}\times \mathbf{2}$</tex> array antenna is less compared to the fractal antenna with FR-4 substrate, i.e., 1.5mm X 1.5mm. The array antenna has bandwidth notches near 15.3GHz with a bandwidth of 0.38GHz, 22.6GHz with a bandwidth of 2.55GHz, and 27.3GHz with a bandwidth of 3.13GHz and covers 5G applications in the range of 25.01-28.14GHz. Both antennas have an n258 band that covers a 5G millimeter wave, implemented using CST.

articleTitle: Sensitivity Comparison of Common Microwave Feeds to be Useful in Angular Displacement Sensors
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this work, the authors analyze the performance of dielectric resonator (DR) based angular displacement sensor with different feeding methods. It is demonstrated that, sensor characteristics like resonant frequency, impedance matching, sensitivity, and dynamic range are highly dependent on the selected feeding technique. The common microwave feeds such as the coaxial probe, slot line, microstrip line, and conformal microstrip line are considered for reflection mode operation. Standard commercial EM simulation tool ANSYS HFSS is used for performing the simulations. Analysis of the simulation results lead to proposing the microstrip line feed for realizing fixed-frequency DR based angular sensor which is experimentally validated.

articleTitle: A Triple-Band mm-Wave SIW Antenna for 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This work proposes a triple-band SIW antenna design for millimeter wave (mm-wave) 5G applications. The proposed antenna is comprised of three rectangular slots of specific lengths, as well as a modified rectangular slot near the feed. For the sake of simulating and analyzing the proposed design, the Ansys HFSS 2021/ R2 software tool has been utilized. The working performance of the antenna is investigated using the parameters of reflection coefficient, radiation pattern, and gain. The proposed antenna offers resonant frequency at 24.37 GHz, 25.45 GHz, and 27.12 GHz with corresponding 10-dB impedance bandwidths of 91 MHz, 64 MHz, and 75 MHz. Moreover, the aforementioned SIW antenna features a maximum gain of 5.47 dBi, 5.3 dBi, and 5.2 dBi in each of the three respective operating frequency bands. These characteristics indicate that the proposed SIW antenna is indeed an excellent contender for operating in the frequency range of 24.25-27.5 GHz assigned by the International Telecommunication Union (ITV) for 5G applications.

articleTitle: Design of Dual-Band Pass FSS with Stable Oblique Incidence using Characteristics Mode Analysis
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this article, a novel and compact Frequency Selective Surface (FSS) with dual-band pass characteristics is proposed. The proposed design of the FSS unit cell is composed of two concentric rings with slotted stubs connected to the outer side of each. The proposed FSS structure provides a dual band-pass characteristic with operating frequencies of 7.5 GHz and 9.8 GHz having a bandwidth of 1.4 GHz for both bands. Both operating bands can be controlled independently by varying the design parameters of the structure. The structure is insensitive to oblique incidence angles up to 60 degree. Further, the geometry is low profile and angular stability and polarization are stable. The proposed design finds very promising applications in C and X bands.

articleTitle: Design of MMIC Ka Band Low Noise Amplifier
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A Ka-band monolithic low-noise amplifier (LNA) with high gain, low noise figure (NF), good input (output) return loss with high linearity has been designed for the operating frequency range of 33-37.4 GHz using 0.15um enhancement mode (E-mode) gallium arsenide (GaAs) pseudomorphic high electron mobility transistor (p-HEMT) process. The LNA employs FET feedback along with a source degeneration to achieve peak performance. The three-stage monolithic microwave integrated circuit (MMIC) LNA has attained a gain of 22.5 dB and a NF of 1.74 dB with good input return loss of 18dB and output return loss of 19dB at center frequency (35.61GHz). The output 1-dB compression point (P1dB) at 35.61 GHz is 17.3dBm. To our knowledge, this combination of NF, input/output return losses, gain, and linearity performance represents the state of the art in this frequency band.

articleTitle: GaN HEMT based Ku-band Power Amplifier MMIC
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents a Monolithic Microwave Integrated power amplifier circuit designed and fabricated with using 150nm Gallium Nitride on SiC process of UMS, France. This MMIC PA exhibits 39 dBm saturated output power in pulsed operating conditions with over 29 dB power gain and 35 percent power added efficiency (PAE). The chip area of this PA is 3.8 mm × 2 mm. This PA is suitable for integration in MMIC RF front-end chip for phased array radar applications.

articleTitle: In-band RCS Reduction of Microstrip Patch Antenna using Artificial Magnetic Conductors at X-Band for Stealth Technology
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this article two miniaturized artificial magnetic conductor(AMC) unit cells have been designed to reduce the RCS of microstrip patch antenna at X-band. The scattering performance of the patch antenna has been determined by using one checkerboard metasurface and one aperiodic metasurface to improve the scattering performance of the antenna. The antenna provides the wide impedance bandwidth of 26%. Because of the AMC metasurface's effectiveness in reducing surface waves, the antenna's radiating performance has been significantly enhanced as a result. While the results of the simulation show a remarkable RCS reduction of 14 dB throughout the X-band for both the polarizations, the results of the measurement show that they are in good agreement with simulated response. In order to facilitate a deeper comprehension of the scattering performance, 3D RCS plots have also been presented. The radiation performance of the antenna has been measured, and the results show a pattern that is almost identical to the one that was simulated.

articleTitle: On-Body V-Band Leaky-Wave Antenna for Navigation and Safety Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: The paper discusses an on-body V-band leaky-wave antenna for navigation and safety applications. The antenna is based on meandering microstrip line operating in V-Band with continuous beam scanning from backward-to-forward direction in the elevation plane. The width of the transverse line are alternatively varied to remove the open stop band (OSB) at the broadside frequency. The final antenna shows a scanning range in the elevation direction from -45° to 50° with no impact on performance at broadside direction. The antenna has a gain of more than 11 dB across the operating frequency range. The structure is simulated and the results and compared with the other leaky-wave antenna designs. The performance of the antenna is also verified for on-body conditions. The antenna is self matched at 50Ω hence removing the need for matching circuit. The requirements for an on-body antenna are also analysed for the designed structure.

articleTitle: Design of reflector based dipole antenna for sub-6GHz 5G applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A novel design of reflector based printed dual dipole antenna with enhanced radiating characteristics is proposed here for 5G sub-6 GHz applications. The proposed radiator resonates over 3.3 to 4.2 GHz. The dipoles are excited by 50 Ω co-axial feeding through microstrip line. The proposed antenna has hybrid geometry constructed using half circular ring and half square ring. The dipole antenna arms are fusion geometry and is constructed by employing a square, two circular and one triangular shaped sheet in each arm. The wide bandwidth of 0.9 GHz is achieved by introducing stepped V-shaped slot on the dipole arms. The slots and orientation of the crossed dipoles provide enhanced isolation and dual polarized radiating characteristics in the operational frequency band. Antenna numerical simulations indicate that the optimized antenna has wide bandwidth of 44.2% (3.3-4.2 GHz), power reflection co-efficient of < -10 dB, average gain of 7.23 dBi and radiation efficiency> 83 %.

articleTitle: Classification based DOA estimation using ANN and CNN Models
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: The Deep Learning Frameworks like ANN and CNN are employed in the area of DOA Estimation has been a recent trend. In this paper we propose Artificial Neural Network(ANN) and Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) which can estimate DOA of a single source with a Uniform Linear Array(ULA).The performance of proposed ANN and CNN which tries classify up to 21 angles with the help of 10 sensors of ULA configuration is evaluated by metrics like training loss, training accuracy etc.

articleTitle: A Polarization-Insensitive Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface for Beam Steering Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: With research being undertaken to develop supporting infrastructure for the 6G communication standard, the reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RIS) have garnered substantive interest due to their ability to dynamically alter the propagation characteristics of the transmitted and received signals. One of the key applications of RIS is to provide dynamic beam steering, which ensures that the signal is only received by the intended receiver. This helps in providing transmission paths for the signal even in the presence of obstacles as well as in differentiating the legitimate users from an eavesdropper. The key concerns in designing such a surface are its polarization sensitivity and angular stability behavior with respect to the incident signal. Further, the tunable phase range is limited in most of the existing RIS geometries. In this work, we present a polarization-insensitive passive surface design, which achieves wide tunability of the reflection angle (in the range -160° to +160° by using varactor diodes and exhibits angular stability upto 60° for TE polarized signal. The full wave simulation results of the proposed design are presented, with the operating frequency centered around 3.1 GHz. The proposed work will be helpful in the realization of goals envisioned by the 6G standard and beyond.

articleTitle: 1–18 GHz Ultra-broadband High Gain Distributed MMIC Amplifier
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents the design and measurement results of an ultra-broadband and high gain GaAs based compact monolithic microwave integrated circuit amplifier. The MMIC is designed using 150nm pseudomorphic high-electron-mobility transistor process in a compact size of 2.5mm x 1.5mm x 0.1mm. The amplifier is based on distributed amplifier topology where conventional distributed amplifier is used in conjunction with cascaded single-stage distributed amplifier stages to achieve large gain-bandwidth product of 374 GHz. Minimum gain of 22.5dB is achieved with low DC power consumption of only 240mW over the entire frequency band of 1–18 GHz.

articleTitle: GaN-based Class-F Power Amplifier for 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, the class F power amplifier is proposed and developed for 5G applications. The design methods include simulation followed by layout design and fabrication. Then, 1 tone Harmonic balance analysis of the fabricated structure of PA is performed to obtain the simulation and measurement results of PAE 79.251% and 12.194%, Gain of 16.54 dB and 13.03 dB, ACP of − 28.09 dBc and − 22.039 dBc, and 3<sup>rd</sup> and 5<sup>th</sup> order harmonics distortion of −20.5 dBc and −48.9 dBc and −18.4 dBc and −45.2 dBc respectively. Also, the study of MAE (in %) performance for Pout, gain, PAE, ACP, 3<sup>rd</sup> and 5<sup>th</sup> harmonic distortion having values 0.0064, 0.0023, 0.0072, 0.00605, 0.0021, and 0.0037 respectively is analyzed and verified.

articleTitle: Bidirectional Transmit-Reflect Array Antenna for 5G Millimeter-wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A high gain bidirectional reflect-transmit array antenna for millimeter wave applications is proposed which combines the properties of transmitarray and reflectarray antenna. The bidirectional antenna array is composed of phase and amplitude modulating digital metabits. The digital metabit consists of a dipole with end loading printed on the top layer of the substrate and a slotted end-loaded dipole on the bottom layer. A bidirectional transmit-reflect array of dimensions 5.6 λo × 5.6 Ao is designed and fed by an antipodal Vivaldi antenna. A maximum broadside gain of 13.1 dBi is obtained at 28 GHz in both transmission mode and reflection mode simultaneously. The designed 1-bit transmit-reflect array finds its application in the 5G communication system.

articleTitle: In-band Full-duplex Bistatic Antenna with reduced Mutual Coupling
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper describes a compact in-band full-duplex (IBFD) 2.4 GHz antenna with high isolation. One of the antennas is a conventional inset-fed microstrip antenna. The second antenna is a quarter-wavelength inset-fed microstrip antenna. The quarter-wave patch is achieved by placing cylindrical metal vias along one of its radiating edge. The two antennas are orthogonally placed with an inter-element spacing of 0.0032λ<inf>0</inf> making the proposed IBFD antenna structure compact than most reported structures. Inter-port isolation of 36 dB is achieved and the cross-polar components are 10 dB lower than the co-polar ones. A comparison of measured and simulated results serves to validate the proposed design concept.

articleTitle: Design of Membrane Based Unit Cell of Large Reflectarray Antenna for SAR System
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In the modern Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) applications, reflect array antenna (RFA) is the primary choice because of its simple planar structure, low profile, ability to stow following easy deployment. However, the structure has a narrow bandwidth, which is due to the unit-element bandwidth and spatial path delays. In this paper, the designed unit-element is a crossed loop having a square shape and a membrane-based unit-cell element. The electrical performance has been evaluated against half wavelength and sub-wavelength spacing's at the center frequency of 9.6 GHz. The antenna achieves approximately 7% bandwidth at the center frequency of 9.6 GHz respectively. To improve the reflection phase, foam-based structure is placed in between the dielectric layer and the ground plane. This helps reduce the overall weight of the RFA. The simulation results for the half wavelength element spacing show that the reflection phase variation happens up to 450°and the 90°phase difference. However, the phase error performance has been improved using sub-wavelength element spacing, which is ≤20° with the reflection phase variation of ≥380°. Moreover, incorporating the unit-cell in 1.2m large RFA gives 39dB gain with ±0.5 dB variation in a gain for desired band.

articleTitle: Far Field Radiation Pattern Synthesis of Circular Antenna Arrays Using NPSO
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A hybridized technique based on Novel Particle Swarm Optimization (NPSO) is used to solve a design challenge for non-uniform CAAs (circular antenna arrays) single ring with the best SLL (side lobe level) and improved FNBW (first null beamwidth) as well. An optimal combination of interelement spacing and current excitation for CAA that provides an array pattern with the greatest possible reduction in SLL and FNBW is determined using this technique. It is assumed that a CAA is placed on an x-y plane. An 8-, 10-, 12-, and 20-element circular array is subjected to NPSO. The performances of side lobe level and first null beam width are analyzed after various simulation results are shown. Experimental results show a significant improvement in SLL and FNBW both as compared to the uniform case in the PSO algorithm [11] used for the same problem.

articleTitle: Low Cost Polarization Insensitive L band FSS Absorber Based on Screen Printing Technique
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, a single-layer radar absorber (RA) design, simulation, and fabrication method based on the screen printing approach i.e resistive ink printed on FR-4 are presented. The proposed prototype has an absorption of more than 90% from 1.05 GHz to 2.14 GHz covering L band. The design is polarization insensitive and stable for oblique electromagnetic wave incidence up to 30 degree for both TE and TM polarization. The result of equivalent circuit model serves as confirmation for full wave simulation result. The fabricated prototype shows measured reflection coefficient below −10 dB from 1.05 GHz to 3 GHz (fractional bandwidth of 96%) with the thickness and periodicity of only 0.070λ<tex>$L$</tex> and 0.076λ<tex>$L$</tex> respectively. To understand the differences between the simulation and measurement results, further simulations with the variation of ink thickness and airgap have been performed. Based on these simulations, the RA with modified parameters (ink thickness of 0.02 mm and air gap of 22.5 mm) has a reflection coefficient below −10dB from 1.1 GHz to 2.74 GHz. The profile of the RA is only 0.086λ<tex>$L$</tex> with periodicity of 0.076λ<tex>$L$</tex>. Wide range of applications may be possible due to the structure's lightness and ease of fabrication.

articleTitle: A Defected Ground Comb Shape Microwave Sensor for Non Invasive Measurement of Blood Glucose
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents a miniaturized defected ground comb shape microwave sensor to detect blood glucose concentration in diabatic patients non-invasively. Proposed sensor works in the frequency range of 4.75-5.5 GHz at operating frequency of 5.25 GHz. The impedance bandwidth of 750 MHz (14.29<sup>%</sup>) is found with reflection coefficient <tex>$\vert \mathrm{S}11 \vert$</tex> of-45 dB. The proposed sensor shows compact volume of <tex>$\mathbf{20}\times \mathbf{20}\times \mathbf{0.8}\ \mathbf{mm}$</tex> 3 fabricated on FR4 substrate. The glucose detection is measured in terms of frequency shift and varying <tex>$\mathrm{S}_{11}$</tex> with respect to relative permittivity of human blood cells. The experimental validation is performed by interacting proposed sensor with human thumb. Observed frequency shift and corresponding sensitivity of sensor are 1.75 GHz and <tex>$6\ \text{MHz}/\varepsilon\mathrm{r}$</tex> respectively. The observed results of proposed sensor satisfied that it is useful for sensing of non-invasive blood glucose level in diabetic patients.

articleTitle: Performance comparison of DAS and BP algorithms for Synthetic Aperture Radar Imaging
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In the Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) research environment Imaging concept plays a very important role. However, many challenges and complexities to forming an image, and many algorithms were developed accordingly. Most of the algorithms were developed by approaching the conventional SAR imaging algorithms like Delay and Sum algorithm (DAS) and Back Projection Algorithm (BPA). This paper presents an overview of these two significant SAR imaging algorithms. The preliminary objective of this paper is to summarize the fundamentals, challenges, and latest advancements in SAR imaging by providing their mathematical framework. We briefly presented the state of the art of SAR imaging and implementations. Also, we compared the algorithms in metrics of noisy environments, execution time, and image resolution for the different algorithms used.

articleTitle: Highly Selective Filter Integrated UWB Monopole Antenna with Dual-Band Notch and Wide Stop Band Rejection Characteristics
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents a low-profile low pass filter integrated elliptical-shaped monopole filtering antenna for the UWB frequency range (3.1 GHz to 10.6 GHz) with dual band notch characteristics. Proposed filtering antenna fabricated on the FR-4 lossy substrate, which is cladded by copper on both sides of it. Rectangular with circular added slot is etched out from the ground to provide better impedance matching. A low pass filter with cut off frequency of 11 GHz has been integrated with the 50 Ohm microstrip line to incorporate selectivity at the higher frequency band of UWB. Two rectangular split ring resonators (R-SRR) have been incorporated to produce the notch at interfering bands. The simulated and measured results are in good agreement with the reflection loss above 10dB in the pass band and below 5dB at band notch frequencies. Wide stop band reported after 11GHz up to 20 GHz due to low pass filter. Similarly, reported gain and efficiencies are also suffice the requirement of RF front end system of the modern wireless communication system.

articleTitle: Digital Coding EM Metasurface to Reconfigurable the Radiation Beam Controlled by Light
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: this manuscript presents the digital coding metasurface control by light in remote mode to dynamically manipulate the EM (electromagnetic wave) in real-time. The varactor diode is embedded in the digital metasurface that changes the EM characteristics of the metasurface without altering its physical dimensions. The photodiode and voltage-driven module are connected to control the varactor diode loaded in the unit cell element, reducing the system”s overall volume and cross-talk between the D.C. signal and EM wave. The photodiode module converts the illuminating light intensity into voltage and tunes the unit cell's states in a non-contact way. These arrangements of digital coding Meta surface can manipulate the EM wave after applying the different coding sequences and generate beam splitting and deflection of the radiation pattern. The proposed digital coding Meta surface is 1-bit coding composed of “0” and “1” unit cell elements corresponding to 0 and 180-degree phase responses respectively. The design and simulation of the proposed unit cell element and digitally coded large array are carried out and observed the amplitude, phase response and beam splitting characteristics which may find promising applications in wireless communication, RCS Reduction, and OAM beam generation.

articleTitle: Dual Band Notch Antenna for Ultra Wide Band Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper is about monopole dual band notch antenna with a micro strip line fed. split ring resonators (split ring re-senators) and a 'T 'shape slot is etched on the surface of the structure to provide two band notches. The designed antenna has shown good performance over the UWB band (3.1 GHz - 10.6 GHz) with return loss of below -10dB and achieved a VSWR less than 2. This antenna provides flexible dual converting function between WLAN and Wi-MAX. UWB band notch antenna was designed and simulated on FR4 <tex>$\mathbf{(\epsilon \mathrm{r}=4.4)}$</tex> substrate with total size of <tex>$28\mathbf{mm}\times 20\mathbf{mm}\times 1.59\mathbf{mm}$</tex>. Simulated results are discussed in this paper.

articleTitle: A CSRR Loaded Triple-Band Microstrip Patch Antenna with Suppressed Higher Order Modes for Sub-6 GHz Phased Array Application
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, we design a CSRR loaded tripe band antenna with suppressed higher order modes. The CSRR loading is incorporated in a square microstrip antenna such that in addition to the triple band response at 3.52 GHz, 3.865 GHz, 4.39 GHz, antenna miniaturization is obtained yielding an overall footprint of <tex>$0.23\lambda_{0}\times 0.23\lambda_{0}$</tex>, where <tex>$\lambda_{0}$</tex> is the free space wavelength at 3.52 GHz. Further, the higher order mode suppression is achieved using a plated through hole (PTH) placed close to the CSRR loading position. The proposed antenna achieves satisfactory impedance matching <tex>$\leq -15$</tex> dB for all three operating frequencies. Further, the proposed antenna is arranged in <tex>$4\times 4$</tex> configuration with an inter-element spacing of <tex>$0.25\lambda_{0}$</tex> for phased array application. This <tex>$4\times 4$</tex> array configuration enables beam steering up to <tex>$80^{0}$</tex> without grating lobes, while maintaining lowest side lobe level <tex>$\geq 19\mathbf{dB}$</tex> and satisfactory array gains of 12 dBi, 13 dBi, 14 dBi at 3.52 GHz, 3.865 GHz, and 4.39 GHz respectively are achieved. The proposed concept is experimentally validated by S-parameter and pattern measurements on fabricated prototype.

articleTitle: SIW-based Circularly Polarized Slot Antenna Array for Millimeter-Wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, a substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) based circularly polarized slot antenna array is presented for millimeter-wave (mm-wave) wireless applications at 28 GHz. The proposed antenna geometry comprises two orthogonal slots engraved on the top layer of the SIW cavity. Upon optimization of slot dimensions and their positions inside the SIW cavity, one left-handed circularly polarized (LHCP) radiation has been obtained at 28 GHz with a decent maximum gain of 6.57 dBic in the broadside direction. To improve the gain of the antenna, a 1x2 antenna array with a SIW feed network has been designed and demonstrated. The array geometry exhibits the maximum gain of 9.25 dBic with an impedance bandwidth of 1.77 GHz (27.33 - 29.10 GHz) and an axial ratio bandwidth of 200 MHz (27.95 - 28.15 GHz). Furthermore, the structure features a simple topology, high efficiency, and low cross-polarization, which makes it suitable for mm-wave applications.

articleTitle: An FSS-based Conformal Band-stop Filter Design for Planar and Non-planar Surfaces
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents a frequency selective surface (FSS)-based conformal bandstop filter design for use in different types of planar and non-planar surfaces. The unit cell of the proposed geometry is based on a single metallic square loop printed on a dielectric substrate. The overall structure exhibits a bandstop response in the frequency range of 6.68 to 12.66 GHz, with a center frequency at 9.53 GHz. The topology is initially analyzed with respect to circuit modeling, surface current distribution, and parametric variation. Afterward, the structure is studied under different types of non-planar surfaces (x-axis curve, y-axis curve, xy- axis curve, hemispherical surface) using the finite element boundary integral (FEBI) method, and the bandstop filter response is observed across the operating band (with transmission coefficient < −10 dB) for all cases. The matching between the planar and non-planar responses confirms the conformal behavior of the proposed FSS structure.

articleTitle: Mutual coupling Compensation in Circular Dipole Array for FM Based Passive Coherent Location Radar
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Significant mutual coupling levels will be present in a minimal size circular array for passive radar, which will lower the array's performance. This work presents an electromagnetic (EM) simulation of mutual coupling compensation (MCC) in a circular dipole array. Additionally, after compensating for mutual coupling, measured beam formation from a realized circular array were also provided. Circular symmetry in the MCM data, computation of the mutual coupling matrix (MCM), and its impact are examined. This study also carries out the null depth verification and dynamic range verification in the field utilising the known sources at numerous positions.

articleTitle: Dual Band Microstrip Patch Antenna with U-shaped Slot and Parasitic Patches for Multiple Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: The paper presents a design of a single kite-shaped patch antenna with a U-shaped slot, parasitic elements, and a partial ground plane. The size of the antenna is 20mm*18mm*1.5mm. It uses annealed copper as the conductor for the patch and the ground plane and FR4 as the substrate, which has an electrical permittivity of 4.3 and a loss tangent of 0.025. The antenna operates in two different frequency bands, 3.6 GHz to 6.1 GHz and 9.4 GHz to 11.9 GHz. It has a peak gain of 3.08dBi and radiation efficiency of 83%. The antenna is suitable for applications in the portions of S-Band, which extends from 2 GHz to 4 GHz and C-Band which lies in the range of 4 GHz to 8 GHz, particularly for n79 5G band (4700 MHz) and 5GHz Wi-Fi. It also covers a portion of the X-Band (8 GHz – 12 GHz), generally helpful for radar applications. The article presents the simulation results of the obtained return loss plot, efficiencies, and radiation patterns.

articleTitle: Design and Testing of a Microstrip Patch Antenna for Vehicle-to-Vehicle Communication
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, a linearly polarized compact patch antenna for potential application to vehicle-to-vehicle communication is presented. This work focuses on the antenna's miniaturization for enhanced gain and wide half-power beamwidth. Two quarter-wavelength resonators are used as a part of the feeding network which leads to suppression of the unwanted out-of-band harmonics. As a result, the impedance bandwidth is slightly enhanced, and the patch size is also reduced by 25.4% as compared to the conventional patch. In addition, two semicircular slots are etched on radiating part in each direction to boast the symmetrical current distributions, thereby, enhancing the polarization purity of the antenna. Moreover, a circular slot is used at the center of the radiating patch to improve the proposed structure's front-to-back ratio. The antenna is fabricated and validated experimentally. The measured values of fractional impedance bandwidth of 4.0%, peak realized gain of 6.0 dBi, cross-polarization level of 40.7 dB, and front-to-back-lobe ratio of 20 dB is achieved at 5.9 GHz. Additionally, the simulated radiation efficiency of 95% is obtained. Such features are a potential for application to aerodynamic wireless devices in intelligent vehicles for blind spot detection.

articleTitle: Compact Tunable Non-Reciprocal Bandpass Filter with the aid of Combline Architecture
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Time-varying transmission lines (TVTL)-based non-reciprocal filters have lately grown in popularity. Their functionality is based on the use of sinusoids with progressive phase shifts to time-modulate spatially separated resonators. This work presents an EM simulated response of a non-reciprocal bandpass filter designed using combline architecture. The design methodology has been analyzed with the aid of coupling matrix and the circuit manifests a compact and tunable non-reciprocal bandpass response suitable for mobile communication frequency range. The variation of insertion loss, isolation, and return loss is 3.7 dB to 4.1 dB, approximately 20 dB, and 20 dB respectively, throughout the tunability range. The circuit possesses the potential for deployment in any monolithic integrations.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable Plasma Antenna Array for Beamsteering Application at S-band
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A beam forming circular Plasma Antenna Array has been designed for VHF and UHF range in CST. In this design a metal antenna which is omnidirectional acts an active element and plasma acts as passive element. Hence, omnidirectional metal antenna is surrounded by a blanket of plasma. The plasma blanket is realized with the use of commercially available fluorescent tubes in which plasma density can be varied with power applied for plasma production. Plasma behaves as a perfect reflector in the region where plasma frequency is greater than operating frequency of the antenna and appears to be transparent for plasma frequency below the operating frequency. A plasma window can be created by turning off or of low plasma density which is transparent to RF. These plasma tubes can be turned off and on in a sequence to provide 360° scanning of the RF signal. Hence, the antenna beam can be directed or steered into any plasma window electrically in all 360° direction which finds its application replacing mechanical steering. The angle of the plasma window can be changed varying the number of tubes used. The result is in terms of radiation pattern, reflection coefficient and VSWR.

articleTitle: Implementation of 3-Bit Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface (RIS) for Sub-6 GHz Range Based on Modified Square loop FSS and Tunable Varactors
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this article, a 3-bit Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface (RIS) based metasurface is implemented for 3.5 GHz sub-6 GHz applications. The unitcell consists of a modified square loop Frequency Selective Surface (FSS) printed on top of a 1 mm thin low-loss grounded dielectric substrate. Two vias are introduced at the centre of the square patch for the reflection phase optimization and HF tunable varactor diodes whose junction capacitance strongly influences the applied voltage. A total of eight different phase states were shown from -180° to 135° insteps of 45°, and the process behind the information encoding for 5G wireless applications is detailed. The angular stability of the reflection phase is investigated for different oblique incidences, and a considerably stable response is observed. Simulated surface current patterns are visualized at resonant frequency for understanding reflection phenomena. The design is compact with a periodicity of 0.058λ<inf>L</inf>×0.058λ<inf>L</inf>and possesses a low-profile thickness of 0.012λ<inf>L</inf>. Authors believe this design has many beneficial features like 3-bit information encoding, angular stability, and compact architecture that play key roles in the RIS design in real-time 5G wireless applications.

articleTitle: Performance Estimation of Continuous Class F−1 PA with Non-Ideal Harmonic Terminations
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In continuous class F-<sup>1</sup> (CCF-<sup>1</sup>) PA, loads at second and third harmonics are purely reactive and short-circuit, respectively. However, it is impossible to achieve these harmonic loads accurately. Therefore, this paper estimates the efficiency and output power of CCF-<sup>1</sup> PA with non-ideal second and third harmonic loads. The performance is estimated with the impedance space of CCF-<sup>1</sup>mode with resistive second and third harmonic loads. As a proof of concept, a CCF-<sup>1</sup> PA with non-ideal harmonic loads is implemented. The designed PA operates from 0.85 to 1.5 GHz with a 60-65% drain efficiency and output power of 37.6-40.8 dBm.

articleTitle: 22-Watts Power Amplifier Design Using GaN HEMT
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: GaN wide band gap semiconductor based devices has suitable material characteristics for higher power with higher frequency applications also. Which includes higher power densities, high breakdown voltages, high saturation velocity and mobility. Gallium Nitride (G <tex>$a$</tex> N) HEMT power amplifier (PA) accomplishing output power of 19.11-25.22 watts having frequency range of 1.18-1.88 GHz (47.13% fractional bandwidth) at center frequency 1.5 GHz is discussed in this paper. Presented amplifier module simulation results is providing maximum 58.64% power added efficiency and 59.95% drain efficiency at 27 dBm input power over the frequency range of 1.18-1.88 GHz at DC bias of VDS=32 V and VGS=-2.8 V. Devices based on GaN are a highly promising option for high power applications. Radar and L-band telecom applications both benefit greatly from this suggested PA.

articleTitle: Mode Purity Analysis of an Orbital Angular Momentum Antenna
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Orbital Angular Momentum (OAM) beams with a different topological charge are orthogonal to each other and hence can be multiplexed together on the same frequency. There are many techniques by which the OAM beams are being generated. However, the generated OAM beams are not always pure in nature which can influence the orthogonal nature of the OAM waves, and the cross-talk between adjacent modes may happen. So, it is very important to perform the mode purity analysis while designing the OAM antenna. This paper describes the mode purity analysis of the four-element Uniform Circular Array (UCA) generating first-order OAM beams. The UCA consists of circular patch antennas operating at 10 GHz. By properly exciting each antenna element with the corresponding phase values, the first order OAM beams with l = ±1 modes are generated. The mode purity analysis of the generated OAM beams is performed by the spectral analysis of the Fourier transform of its azimuth angular distribution. The variation of the mode purity with the sampling circle radius and with the transmission distance has been studied.

articleTitle: Indigenous State-of-the-Art Development of Wide Band and Wide Scan Active Phased Array Antennas
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper reviews the various state-of-the-art phased array antenna (PAAs) designs conceptualized and developed within Electronics and radar development establishment (LRDE) for wide band and wide scan applications for various radar applications. The paper describes the design techniques for these PAAs with the help of few case studies and discusses the various technological challenges faced during the development process.

articleTitle: Stepped Coplanar Waveguide Loaded with SRR Array for Detection of Cracks in Plastic Pipes
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents a stepped coplanar waveguide (CPW) based RF sensor loaded with 5 SRR elements for the detection of cracks in plastic pipes and other sensing applications. The proposed sensor resonates at 12.87 GHz and has good impedance matching in the specified frequency band. The stepping is used in the CPW topology to ensure <tex>$\mathbf{50}\mathbf{\Omega}$</tex> matching at the excitation port and requisite field localization over the coupling region. The number of SRRs is chosen to be five after an optimization process to attain higher Q and improved matching at the operating frequency. Each SRR couples with the central region of the stepped line and confines sufficient fields at its slits, forming an elongated sensing region to facilitate the detection of cracks and sensing of larger structures. The enhanced field confinement is demonstrated by analyzing the E-field plots of conventional and proposed topologies. The numerical simulation and measurement indicate that the proposed sensor provides an improved Q-factor and sharper response as compared to that of the sensor based on the conventional microstrip. Finally, the proposed sensor is fabricated and tested to detect invisible cracks in a typical plastic pipe, indicating its usage for numerous applications.

articleTitle: Broadband Tunable CMOS RF Bandpass filter using a Modified Active Inductor Topology
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, a modified active inductor based bandpass RF filter is proposed that achieves a broad tuning frequency range. A bandpass filter based on the proposed active inductor is shown be operated from 2 to 6.1 GHz. The filter's passband frequency and quality factor is tuned by changing the biasing voltage of PMOS current mirror. The second and higher order harmonic suppression is better than at least 19dB. The proposed active filter is designed using UMC 180 nm RF/MM process parameters and works with a 1.8V DC power supply. The filter also exhibits input port return losses up to 14dB over the range 2–6 GHz, making it fairly well matched over its functional bandwidth.

articleTitle: Synthesis of Conformal Phased Array Antenna with Improved SLL
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This article presents a methodology to synthesize a conformal cylindrical arc antenna array that can be controlled by both amplitude and phase Excitations. The proposed antenna array synthesizes directive lobe and multi-lobe patterns with beam steering capability. The phase excitation and amplitude coefficients are generated by using Taguchi's and Dolph-Chebyshev excitation methods, respectively. An 8- element cylindrical antenna array is designed using CST MW Studio and simulated various beam shapes.

articleTitle: Broad Band Polarization Insensitive Metamaterial Absorber for K Band Application
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this work, the design of broadband wide angle polarization insensitive metamaterial (MM) electromagnetic wave (EM) absorbers for K band frequency applications is investigated. The unit cell of the metamaterial absorber consists of four 90 degree rotated L shaped metallic patches imprinted on a dielectric substrate backed by a metallic sheet. The four fold symmetry of the design yields polarization insensitive characteristics. More than 90% absorptivity has been achieved from 22.56 GHz to 29.29 GHz having wide fractional bandwidth of 25.83 % (6.73 GHz). The unit cell structure has peak absorptivity of 98.75%, 99.12%, and 97.73% at frequencies 24.94 GHz, 26.66 GHz, and 28.29 GHz, respectively. The proposed design can effectively absorb more than 90% of Transverse Electric (TE) and Transverse Magnetic (TM) waves from any direction at normal incidence. For a wide angle of oblique incidence to TE wave, absorber has shown more than 75% absorption up to 0 = 60 degree while for TM wave, more than 50% absorption up to 0= 50 degree has been observed. Broadband response with good polarization insensitivity at normal and oblique incidence makes it commercially suitable for the applications of K band.

articleTitle: A 1–18 GHz Single Supply 5-Bit Low Power Consumption MMIC Digital Attenuator
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A broad band 1 to 18 GHz 5-bit Monolithic Microwave Integrated Circuit (MMIC) digital attenuator presented in this paper. The presented attenuator has high accuracy, low insertion loss, low insertion phase shift and low power consumption and is realized using enhancement/depletion (E/D) mode GaAs pseudomorphic high electron-mobility transistor (pHEMT) process. Attenuator fabricated in 0.25um GaAs PHEMT process. The digital attenuator achieves a 15.5dB dynamic attenuation range stepped by 0.5dB with better than 5.7dB insertion loss over the band and fewer than +/-0.5dB major state attenuation error in the band 8-18GHz. Major state linear phase variation less than 20deg realized in die size of 1.46x1.6 sq.mm.

articleTitle: A Metasurface-based Triple-band Polarization Insensitive Band-Stop Filter for S/C/X Band Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In the present work, a metasurface-based band-stop filter (BSF) has been designed and studied for applications in S, C and X bands. The single unit of the design comprises ring and plus-shaped metallic patterns made of copper layer on top of a FR-4 substrate while the backside is completely etched off. The proposed unit cell has a dimension on the order of <tex>$0.16\lambda \times 0.16\lambda$</tex>, making it compact in nature. When the electromagnetic (EM) wave is incident on the structure, band-stop characteristics have been observed at three distinct frequencies 2.67 GHz, 7.28 GHz and 9.71 GHz lying in S, C and X bands, respectively. The simulated results of the structure have been validated by the experimentally measured data. The design is ultrathin <tex>$(\lambda/68.67)$</tex> referred to the lowermost stopband frequency. The transmission response of the BSF is nearly stable up to 45° incident angle for both transverse magnetic and transverse electric polarization of the incident EM wave. The BSF further exhibits polarization insensitivity property owing to the four-fold symmetry. The structure has been fabricated and the experimentally measured results have been found to be good agreement with the simulated ones.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Multibeam Multi-Panel Antenna Array for Cellular mm-Wave 5G Vehicle-To-Everything (V2X) Communications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, a low-profile substrate integrated waveguide H-plane sectoral horn antenna with wide bandwidth and high gain is designed. An extended dielectric along with the extended bottom broadwall is utilized to improve the impedance matching between horn aperture and free space. To feed the antenna, a simple coaxial probe is used. The simulated results show that the horn antenna achieves a wide bandwidth of 20.6% (24.16 - 29.72 GHz) for |S<inf>11</inf>| < -10 dB with a compact size of only 18.3 mm × 20.6 mm. The extended bottom broadwall enhances the gain and acts as a reflector providing an inclined main beam. The antenna has a peak gain of 9.2 dBi with an inclination angle between 50-60°. These features of the designed horn antenna are suitable for implementing a multibeam antenna array with full azimuth coverage for application in cellular mm- Wave 5G vehicle-to-everything communications. By placing eight horn antenna panels in a sequentially rotated arrangement, a multibeam antenna array is implemented with a compact footprint. The antenna array has shown good inclined beam switching and omnidirectional capabilities over wide impedance bandwidth obtained with low profile and volume.

articleTitle: A Wideband Compact Polarization-Insensitive Absorber using Modified Resistive Jerusalem Cross FSS
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper proposes a Frequency Selective Surface (FSS) based Circuit Analog Absorber (CAA) using an array of modified, resistor loaded, Jerusalem cross geometry. The absorber consists of two FR4 dielectric layers separated by an air spacer. The top layer supports the FSS while the bottom layer supports the ground plane. The proposed absorber provides minimum 10 dB reflection reduction of the incoming electromagnetic wave starting from 2.167 GHz to 6.647 GHz, resulting in a fractional bandwidth of 101.657%. The overall footprint of the absorber is quite low. The unit cell size of the proposed design is 0.137 lambda x 0.137 lambda with thickness of 0.081 lambda (lambda being the wavelength corresponding to lower cut-off frequency of the absorption band). Being four fold symmetric geometry, the absorber is insensitive to incident polarization and shows stable response up to 30 degree angle of incidence. It is observed and additional Jerusalem cross at a rotated angle along with a slight modification in the form of a circular aperture at the center of the FSS improves overall absorption.

articleTitle: Novel Wideband Perfect Reflector with Linear-Cross Polarization Conversion Ability for X/Ku/Ka-Band Applications Including Bandwidth Adjustment
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This article proposes a novel wideband reflective type metasurface that performs linear-cross polarization conversion and perfect reflector operation in different bands. The polarizer unitcell primarily consists of a top Frequency Selective Surface (FSS) printed on the low-loss grounded substrate. It shows the minimum 90% Polarization Conversion Ratio (PCR) from 9.66- 14.72 GHz and almost zero PCR from 15–22 GHz for the linearly polarized Electromagnetic (EM) wave incidence. In addition to the linear-cross, the design also demonstrates the linear-circular conversion with a 3 dB Axial Ratio (AR) from 8.27 to 9 GHz (X-band) and 14.90 to 15.07 GHz (Ku-band). The performance is stable up to 45° for oblique incidences in the elevation plane. Multiple surface plasmonic resonances are the reason for the dual operation, and the near electric field patterns agree with the presented response. The operational bands are tunable mechanically by adjusting open-ended stub dimensions connected to the unitcell's inner loop. The design has volumetric architecture of 1.709(λ<inf>L</inf><sup>3</sup>/1000), λ<inf>L</inf> is the free-space wavelength of the lowest operational frequency. Due to the angular stable linear-cross polarizers and perfect reflectors at different frequency bands in a single design would be useful in real-time applications where dual-operation is the primary concern.

articleTitle: Inverted C shaped THz array antenna for wireless body area network applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Wireless communication is enhancing day by day. THz antennas play a major role to fulfill the demand of high speed and high bandwidth communication. In this paper 1 × 3 array antenna is designed with two different layers of substrates as RT5880 and Polyamide with more than 92 % radiation efficiency in the frequency band 1.6-1.87 THz and gain of 12.05 dBi at resonating frequency 1.69 THz. A C shaped slot is etched in the patch of square antenna of single element. The slot added results in improved return loss and further three elements are connected in series forming an array for enhancing gain and efficiency. It can be used in wireless body area networks.

articleTitle: A Wideband Quasi-Yagi Antenna Array at 24–28 GHz for 5G mmWave Mobile Terminals
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A wide-band quasi-Yagi antenna and its 4×1 array system proposed for mmWave 5G cellular terminal operating in the 24–28 GHz working band is presented. The antenna array is developed using a simple planar quasi-Yagi topology to fit into the 5G mobile terminals easily. A single antenna earnings a -10 dB impedance bandwidth for a reflection coefficient (S<inf>11</inf>) of 26% (23.28-30.29 GHz) and a gain of 7.65 and 8.37 dBi at 24 GHz and 28 GHz frequencies, respectively. Further, the two individual 4×1 linear quasi-Yagi antenna arrays are implemented at the top right corner of the mobile PCB. The array configurations can occupy an overall size of 66x46x0.254 mm<sup>3</sup>with 0.7λ<inf>0</inf>elemental spacing and having the -40 dB low mutual coupling obtained between the two 4×1 antenna arrays. The results show that the proposed two individual 4×1 linear quasi-Yagi antenna arrays have wide impedance bandwidth covering the 5G-n258 (24.25-27.5 GHz) frequency band and peak gains of 14 to 15 dBi at both 24 and 28 GHz frequencies respectively. With the broad hemispherical radiation characteristics and wider half power beam width, the proposed antenna arrays are a promising solution for 5G mmWave cellular terminals applications.

articleTitle: A Wideband Noise Cancelling Mixer in 130-nm BiCMOS Process
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents a low noise, high conversion gain mixer that is realized using the SiGe 130nm BiCMOS process. The propose mixer has adopted a noise-canceling technique for reducing noise by injecting a current at the common emitter of the RF transistors. The proposed mixer achieved a power consumption of 6.84 mW with an improvement in noise performance by 1dB. It achieved a 3 dB bandwidth of 10 GHz and a flat band noise figure variation of 0.2 dB over the 3dB bandwidth. The mixer has an OIP3 of 12.4dBm, a noise figure of 6.1dB, and a conversion gain of 23.1dB

articleTitle: A Partially Transparent GSM Band Loop RF-Solar Energy Harvester
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, a hybrid energy harvester consisting of a solar panel and a broadband loop rectenna in GSM 900 band is discussed. The RF energy harvester has a end-fire radiation pattern. This rectenna is useful to harvest energy from the cellular base-station at the same elevation plane. Most hybrid energy harvesters have a broadside radiation pattern for RF energy harvesting which have to be kept at an angle for energy harvesting limiting the solar irradiation of solar panel. The maximum gain of the antenna is 2.06 dBi and the maximum RF to DC efficiency of conversion of rectifier is 57.98 % at 0 dBm input power. The power management unit, consisting of rectifier and buck converter harvests 0.786 V voltage from the rectenna.

articleTitle: SIW Based Circularly Polarised Leaky Wave Antenna with Improved Scanning Rate and Scanning Range Using Hairpin-shaped Delay Lines
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, a substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) based circularly polarised (CP) leaky wave antenna (LWA) is designed to increase the scanning rate and the scanning range using hairpin-shaped delay lines. The proposed LWA has unit cells of H-shaped slots followed by hairpin-shaped delay lines placed periodically. This configuration has achieved CP along with frequency beam scanning. The hairpin-shaped delay lines introduce group delay and leakage constant suppression. This leads to an improvement in the scanning rate and scanning range of the LWA. The proposed antenna scans in the frequency range of 11GHz to 12.4GHz with percentage fractional bandwidth of 11.9%. It provides a scanning rate of 60.7 degree/GHz in the scanning range of -10 degree to 75 degree. In addition, a high gain of 14.53dBic at 11.5GHz is achieved.

articleTitle: Compact Triple Band Circularly Polarized Dielectric Resonator Antenna for Positioning and Navigational Application
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This article presents a compact dielectric resonator antenna for GPS and RNSS applications. Triple band circular polarization characteristic is obtained through a corner truncated modified rectangular DR along with three conformal strips. The parametric and simulated analysis is investigated by Ansys HFSS. The proposed antenna covers an L5 band of 1.164-1.188 GHz, an L1 band of 1.565-1.607 GHz, and an RNSS band of 2.484-2.50 GHz having RHCP in the lower two band whereas LHCP in the upper band. The gain of 4 dBic, 5.9 dBic, and 4 dBic across the first, second, and third operating frequency bands respectively.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Sparse Array Using Compressive Sensing in A Closed Multi-Path Environment
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Radars are primarily used to determine the velocity, range, and direction of arrival. Several methods have been developed in the literature to determine the target's direction of arrival. In this paper, we first examine how sparse array structures perform in a multi-path environment when the multi-path components are close to the target, and then we examine how these sparse array structures perform in multiple targets then extend it to targets close to each other. In addition, the high resolution subspace-based approach MUltiple-SIgnal Classification (MUSIC) is compared to the Compressive sensing-based recovery method Orthogonal Matching Pursuit (OMP). The results obtained, when compared to many state-of-the-art algorithms shows that the suggested approach in this paper works effectively.

articleTitle: An ultrathin polarization insensitive triple band microwave metamaterial absorber
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper proposes an ultrathin polarization-insensitive metamaterial absorber (MMA) with triple band performance at C-, X-, and Ku-band. The proposed structure has been optimized using its geometrical parameters and has an ultra-thin thickness of 0.8mm (0.114λ). The proposed structure has a maximum absorption peak of 98.7<sup>%</sup>, 94.6%, and 99.1% at 4.2GHz, 12.2GHz, and 16.5GHz, respectively. The structure's absorption mechanism has been thoroughly investigated, and its surface current distribution has been examined. The structure has been analyzed for its constitutive electromagnetic parameters. Applications for the proposed MMA include multiband antenna radar cross section (RCS) reduction, sensors, and radar absorbing structures.

articleTitle: Metasurfaces Antennas for Biological Imaging
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Since metasurface antennas are composed of ensembles of electrically-small resonators, they have a tendency to be frequency band-limited. While this may be a significant challenge in wireless communications, for biomedical applications, such inherent limitation may be an advantage. In this work, we present an application of a metasurface antenna where the antenna is used to capture an impression-image of a human female breast, thereby acting as an electronic film. The impression basically captures the electromagnetic near field arising from the re-radiation of the breast. We Show that such use of metasurfaces antennas, when used as receivers, can provide a potentially powerful diagnostic tool for breast cancer detection.

articleTitle: Multibeam Pattern Reconfigurable Antenna Using SP3T Switching Network and RRS
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This article discusses a new idea of radiation pattern and multibeam reconfiguration. Two different types of antennas have used along with two sets of reconfigurable reflecting surfaces (RRS). All these arranged so, it may provide the radiation pattern reconfiguration from broadside to backside and end-fire to back-fire direction. Two sets of traditional printed dipole antennas are used to provide end-fire to back-fire radiations. At the center, a slot-based antenna with two sets of RRS on top and bottom has been designed to provide broadside to backside radiation. To make all these possible, a reconfigurable single-pole three throw (SP3T) switching network has been provided. So, the proposed design is capable to provide four single beams as well as two bi-directional beams.

articleTitle: Array Arrangement of Octagonal Chipless RFID Tag for Read Range Enhancement
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, the concept of array configurations of chipless RFID tags is presented. The proposed tag consists of eleven concentric octagonal resonators. The symmetrical structure of the tag makes it orientation-independent. The tag also has a high coding capacity of 1 0 bits. The tag resonator is placed in 2 x 2 array configuration to enhance RCS response and hence,achieved a long-read range.

articleTitle: S-Band Dual Circularly Polarized Multi-Beam Shared Aperture Phase Array Antenna for Ground Reception System
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A dual circularly polarized S-band multi-beam shared aperture phase array antenna for ground based communication and data acquisition system has been discussed in this manuscript. The objective is to simultaneously produce multiple beams--using the same antenna aperture. Each beam is independently assigned to separate airborne flying objects for tracking and health data analysis purpose. The antenna system is capable of producing simultaneous dual circular polarization, namely left hand and right hand circular polarization. Each beam is independently steered electronically over ±45° without much degradation of the gain and beamwidth at scan edge. Side lobe level is reduced below 30 dB using Taylor distributed amplitude tapering. The overall array antenna produces a 3dB beamwidth of about 14°with boresight gain of is 20dBi over the entire operating band. However, the gain decreases by ~ 3dB at scan edge of <tex>$\pm 45^{\circ}$</tex> The system has been realized and experimentally validated. The realized impedance bandwidth is wider than 10% at each of the ports with inter-port isolation <tex>$\geq 18$</tex> dB. Measured axial ratio is better than 3 dB over the entire operating band.

articleTitle: Improved Sensitivity of Zero Bias Diode Power Detectors using Impedance Tuners
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This work proposes the use of an impedance tuner to increase the sensitivity of a diode detector. A zero bias Schottky diode is used as a power detector with a Chebyshev-based impedance tuner. The system is implemented with lumped components and is investigated over a wide frequency range from 0.433 GHz to 1 GHz. The measured results show a minimum increase of 1.2x at 0.433 GHz and a maximum of 2.8x at 0.9 GHz in the detector's sensitivity when the tuner is used.

articleTitle: Design A 1Bit High Gain 21×21 Reconfigurable Reflectarray Antenna for X-Band Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presented the design of a high gain electronically reflectarray antenna with a 21×21 element operating at 11.8GHz. It consists of a rectangular microstrip patch with a semicircle slot, a stack of substrate, ground plane, and two copper vias. A Pin diode is biased with a quarter wave dc line by using via. The Reflectarray element has a phase difference of 180+13.4°in operating bands 11.29-12.03 GHz. Based on the performance of the reflectarray element design and optimization of a 21×21 element RRA for +50° beam scanning in the xoy plane at 11.8 GHz. The 441-pin diode is used for steering beams.

articleTitle: A Compact Ultrawideband Planar Patch Antenna for UWB/X/Ku Band Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents an ultrawideband (UWB) planar patch antenna covering a wide frequency range that can perform in UWB, X, and Ku bands. The ultrawideband frequency range is achieved by using defected ground structure (DGS) technique. The compact volume of presented antenna is 32×32×1.6 mm3, designed using a cost-effective FR-4 substrate. The measured impedance bandwidth is observed from 3.02 GHz to 19.82 GHz. The Antenna's impedance bandwidth is enhanced by using a half-plane semicircular-shaped ground structure. The percentage impedance bandwidth of antenna is 146.2%. The antenna's peak gain is found to be in the range of 2 dB to 6.8 dB throughout the operational frequency range. The proposed antenna radiates with more than 85% of radiation efficiency within the range of operational frequency. The antenna parameters are optimized by using appropriate design techniques. The measured results are found to be in concurrence with the simulated one.

articleTitle: Beam-Forming Antenna Based on Electrically Reconfigurable Frequency Selective Surface
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A linearly polarized two-dimensional beam-forming antenna using electrically reconfigurable frequency selective surface (FSS) has been proposed in this manuscript. The antenna structure incorporates a coaxial fed patch antenna and a recon-figurable FSS layer, kept above the patch radiator at a height of 0.41λ<inf>0</inf> (λ<inf>0</inf> represents the free space wavelength at the resonant frequency). The reconfigurable superstrate FSS layer consists of 6× 6 unit cells. The dimension of each unit cell is 0.24λ<inf>0</inf> ×0.24λ<inf>0</inf>. To make the FSS layer electrically reconfigurable, each unit cell consists of two PIN diodes. The FSS superstate is further divided in four sections and each section contains 3 × 3 unit cells. Each sections are connected to the individual biasing pads for the purpose of biasing. The overall dimension of the proposed structure is 1.6λ<inf>0</inf> ×1.6λ<inf>0</inf> × 0.44λ<inf>0</inf>. When the reconfigurable FSS is illuminated by the coaxial fed patch, the composite system can generate thirteen individual radiating modes, which interms radiating in thirteen individual direction in 3D space. The antenna operates at a resonant frequency of 4 GHz and a maximum gain of 8.06 dBi is achieved with a maximum of 34° tilting of the beam.

articleTitle: Dual-Band Substrate Integrated Waveguide (SIW) Cavity Slot Antenna for C-Band Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents a dual-band substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) cavity slot antenna with improved performance in terms of impedance matching, radiation efficiency, gain, and reduced cross-polarization level for C-band application. A pair of diagonal corner truncated L-shape slots on the SIW cavity generates circular polarization (CP) and linear polarization (LP). Two shorting pins are placed near a feed line to realize better impedance matching. A square patch antenna with truncated corners is designed on a SIW for circular polarization, and two shorting pins are used near the feed line for better impedance matching. The radiation pattern of the proposed antenna is LP at 5.43 GHz and CP at 5.98 GHz. The impedance bandwidth for reflection coefficient below -10 dB is between 5.35 to 5.55 GHz and 5.85-6.05 GHz for the lower and the upper band, respectively. In addition, a 3-dB axial ratio bandwidth of 0.375 GHz is observed at the upper band owing to the CP radiation. The measured peak realized gains of the LP mode and the CP mode are 8.13 dBi and 8.9 dBic. The radiation efficiencies at the lower and upper bands are above 89% and 88%, respectively. The measured results are in good agreement with the simulation data.

articleTitle: A Dual Circularly Polarized Substrate Integrated Waveguide Antenna for X-band Application
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This manuscript presents a substrate integrated cavity-backed dual circularly polarized microstrip antenna. Based on substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) technology a cylindrical shaped substrate integrated cavity-based antenna design is considered. The top wall of the cavity consists of a cross slot. The antenna is excited by two orthogonally placed microstrip lines. The slot is oriented at an angle 45° with respect to the feed lines. Enforcing two different phase differences (90° and -90°) between the two input ports the antenna, left- and right-hand circular polarizations have been produced. The antenna resonates at an identical frequency (9.98 GHz) for each of the polarizations with a consistent gain of 6.2 dBiC and impedance bandwidths of 2.87% (9.89 - 10.17 GHz) at port-1 and 3.35% (9.9 - 10.23 GHz) at port-2. In both <tex>$\boldsymbol{E}$</tex> - and <tex>$\boldsymbol{H}$</tex> -plane, the antenna exhibits an approximate cardioid shape pattern and an excellent pattern symmetry.

articleTitle: MTM-EBG Loaded Circular Patch Antenna for ISM Band Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A dual frequency circular microstrip patch antenna is designed with transmission line metamaterial based electromagnetic bandgap (MTM-EBG) structures in this article. The two frequencies of interest are chosen as 2.4 GHz and 5.75 GHz covering industrial, scientific, and medical (ISM) band applications. The MTM-EBG unit cell is designed with the combination of interdigital capacitance and rectangular apertures. Twelve MTM- EBG unit cells are placed together to form a periodiccircular EBG surface around a low profile small circular microstrip patch resonating at 5.75 GHz. The arrangement is placed in such a way that the overall effective radius of the patch can be manipulated to get the resonances at both the operational frequencies by utilizing the bandgap of the EBG cells.

articleTitle: Modified Sierpinski and its use in Fractal Patch Antenna for Miniaturization and Multiband Behavior
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: The characteristics like self-similarity and space filling are the unique properties of Fractal geometries. The geometries associated with fractal designs have been exploited, by the researchers for designing an antenna to have the mentioned properties. The article proposes a modified Sierpinski fractal design to give better miniaturization as equated to the conventional Sierpinski geometry. The advised design miniaturizes the triangular patch antenna by more than 50%. The two geometries are compared for a microstrip patch antenna. The comparison is done for the planar antenna on Roggers RO4003 lossy substrate with permittivity of 4.3 and the fractalization has been done up to fourth iteration. The calculations and simulations of S11(dB) and radiation pattern have been completed and mentioned in this communication.

articleTitle: Design of Monolithic 5–18 GHz Digital Attenuator with Low Attenuation and Phase Error
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A 6-bit MMIC digital attenuator with multi octave bandwidth of 5-18GHz is reported in this article. The attenuator is fabricated on 0.13µm GaAs pHEMT process technology of GAETEC Hyderabad, India. Low phase variation is achieved over attenuation states by optimizing the phase balance between signal paths making it suitable for EW applications. The circuit performance is measured on-wafer and a dynamic range of 31.5dB is achieved with incremental steps of 0.5dB; phase variation of ±4° over wideband. The reference state insertion loss of <-6.2dB and input/output return loss better than 8 dB are measured over 5-18GHz across all states. A compact chip size of 2.5mm×1.5mm makes it appropriate for use in multifunction MMICs.

articleTitle: A Dual-Band Circularly Polarized Microstrip Antenna for Navigation System Terminals
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A dual-band circularly polarized microstrip antenna is proposed to realize the reception of multi-band navigation signals by satellite navigation system terminals. The proposed antenna adopts a double-layer structure to achieve dual-band. The top layer adopts a crown-like fractal structure and the bottom one is a rectangular patch. The top and bottom are fed simultaneously by a single coaxial probe to achieve circular polarization. The proposed antenna can work in the B1 (1.561 GHz) and B3 (1.268 GHz) bands of the BeiDou Navigation Satellite System (BDS) and the L1 (1.575 GHz) band of the Global Positioning System (GPS) with right-handed circular polarization (RHCP). The proposed antenna has a low profile and compact structure, and can be applied as the terminal antenna of a satellite navigation system.

articleTitle: A Compact Flexible Crown Rectangular Fractal Antenna on low-cost PET substrate
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Textile substrates and paper-based substrates are generally used to design the flexible antennas. However, these substrates have the issue of moisture absorbance which effect the antenna working. In the present work, a compact flexible crown rectangular fractal antenna has been fabricated and tested using copper tape (conducting material) and PET sheet (substrate). The proposed antenna is simulated and fabricated and the results are found in good agreement. Further, the results for prototype antenna are obtained in bent form. Also, the proposed antenna is compared with similar shaped antenna fabricated on RT-Duroid.
