The proposed PET substrate based antenna shows 53.17 % miniaturization capability with an advantage of flexibility compared to the earlier published antenna.

articleTitle: GaAs MMICs based High Power Ku-band T/R chain using in-house processed PCB and Assembly
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A Ku-band high power Transmit-Receive (T/R) Module chain with a transmit chain output power of 4.6 watt and a receive chain Noise Figure (NF) less than 5 dB is developed using an in-house PCB processing and MMICs assembly. All the COTs based MMICs except circulator used in T/R module are based on Gallium Arsenide (GaAs) technology. The integrated version of this T/R module can have wide applications in high-performance space based phased array system for surveillance, Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR), Active Electronically Scanned Array (AESA) radar for aircraft, missiles etc.

articleTitle: Bi-Directional True Time Delay Core Chip for Phased Array Radars
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Due to less usage of the area and small power, Phased arrays are used extensively. To classify the direction of propagation and attain decent gain, beam steering is needed. Therefore, the main threat is the expanded size of the array for high power. To clarify the issues, the rising technology of True Time Delay can be used. In this paper, here research is being done to configure a unidirectional True Time Delay Core Chip in bidirectional mode by using SPDT switches such that it can be used in both Transmit and receive paths. The entire proposal is being supported by ADS (EM-co Simulation) and Cadence Allegro. As the Core Chip is unidirectional, two separate chips are to be needed for the transmitter and receiver differently. Therefore, this unidirectional Core Chip is configured into bidirectional so that with the help of one Core Chip only, one can achieve desired results. Moreover, this will result in more cost-saving and reliability.

articleTitle: Polarization independent meta-structure absorber using array of embedded gelated deep eutectic solvent for X-band applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A polarization independent meta-structure absorber is proposed using cylindrical embedded subwavelength structures of gelated deep eutectic solvent (DES) in silicone rubber (SR) substrate with aluminium back. The absorber is designed and developed with thickness of 3 mm <tex>$(=\lambda/10)$</tex> for X-band applications. Measured absorption performance of the absorber shows a -10 dB bandwidth of 3.45 GHz and - 26.23 dB reflection loss (>99% absorption) at 9.76 GHz. The absorber shows wide angle polarization insensitivity upto <tex>$\pm 90^{\circ}$</tex>. The absorber performance is retained upto 20 mm of bending curvature. The absorption mechanism in the proposed absorber is investigated and discussed through field analysis at the resonant frequency.

articleTitle: RF communication using salt water standing column
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: RF communication (transmission and reception) is tried using salt water standing column in very high frequency range. RF power is coupled to salt water column using a coaxial connector. This antenna has large bandwidth unlike metallic antenna. This type of antenna is preferred due to its low cost, simple configuration, re-configurability, easy availability of salt water and large bandwidth. Good communication is achieved with salt water standing column over (60–400) MHz frequency range.

articleTitle: SIW Cavity Backed High-Gain Slot Antenna using Metamaterial for 5G mmWave Communications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper proposes a low-profile high-gain SIW-cavity backed slot antenna using metamaterial slab in the superstrate of the reference antenna for 5G mmWave communications. The proposed antenna operates at the frequency band of 27.7 - 29.2 GHz with realized gain greater than 9.8 dBi throughout the entire operating frequency band whereas the reference antenna gain is 4.6 dBi and the antenna profile is 0.2 λ<inf>0</inf> at the frequency of 28 GHz. The superstrate slab is working as a low-impedance metamaterial and the front-to-back ratio is improved by 5.2 dB at 28 GHz due to the application of the metamaterial. The radiation efficiency of the proposed antenna is greater than 92 % throughout the entire operating frequency band of the antenna. This low-profile high-gain antenna can be used in mmWave communications.

articleTitle: A Wide-band SWaP System for VSWR and Power Measurement with Temperature Compensation Technique
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Modern high-power systems like Radars and communication need very accurate and temperature invariant systems to measure the transmitted power and VSWR to insure the proper operation of these equipment. This paper discusses the design of a wide-band SWaP (size, weight, and power) system for VSWR and power measurement with very high accuracy and dynamic range with different duty cycles of operation. Measurement accuracy is achieved using digital RF signal processing and voltage mapping techniques. This paper also discusses the temperature compensation technique for a wide band temperature of operation (-10°C to +70°C) with less than or equal to ±0.3 dB of measurement of accuracy. Finally, the results of L & S - Bands with various power levels and temperatures are presented.

articleTitle: A Polarization-Insensitive Dual-Transmission Band Frequency Selective Rasorber
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A polarization-insensitive frequency selective rasorber (FSR) geometry with dual-transmission and dual-absorption band has been presented in this paper. Two passbands appear inside a wide absorption band, thereby resulting in multiple absorption regions surrounding the transmission peaks. The proposed FSR comprises of one absorptive layer and one transmissive layer, separated by an air spacer, and each of them is realized by patterning geometries in a periodic arrangement. The transmission bands are obtained at 5.30 GHz and 8.10 GHz with insertion losses of 0.79 dB and 0.46 dB, respectively. A wide absorption band, originally realized between 2.26 GHz and 8.79 GHz, gets divided into multiple absorption regions due to the presence of in-band transmission peaks and shows two discrete absorption bands from 2.01 GHz to 4.95 GHz and 5.81 GHz to 7.45 GHz. The structure achieves an overall fractional bandwidth of 118.20% with respect to its centre frequency. Polarization-insensitivity as well as angular stability for different polarizations (till 30 angle of incidence) are also observed in the structure. As compared to the existing dual-transmission band rasorber geometries, the proposed FSR offers a simpler design topology, lower footprint, and larger operating bandwidth. Proposed structure has been fabricated and measured to verify proposed design.

articleTitle: High Gain Dual Broadband Antenna Array Using Substrate Integrated Waveguide at X/Ku Bands
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, a new high gain dual band antenna array is proposed using substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) for X and Ku band satellite communication applications. Two major parts of the SIW array are pair of cavity backed slot antenna and a 1 to 2 way SIW based Y-junction divider. The multimode high order resonances are excited within the cavity resonator to obtain dual broadband performance. Impedance bandwidth (BW) of the array exists between frequency ranges of 11.47-11.74 GHz (2.3 %) and 12.79-14.15 GHz (10.1 %) in the lower and higher bands. The simulated peak gain and efficiency of the array are 10.6 dBi and 94.4 % at the lower resonance and 11 dBi and 95.4 % at the higher resonance.

articleTitle: EM Modeling Considerations on Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces for System Design
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RIS) are passive, controllable reflective surfaces, that are able to direct radio waves toward or away from target nodes. In the last two years, RIS structures have attracted a huge amount of attention in the wireless communication community. The design of reflective surfaces in the antenna community also has a long history. This paper is written to be accessible to both communities, describing the general design principles and the underlying reasons for some RF design choices and outcomes, whose roots may not be transparent to the wireless community, resulting in some baseband wireless models and system designs that are inconsistent with RF practical characteristics. In particular, this paper addresses the role and the impact of the ground plane and phase shifts in RIS, as well as the underlying reason for the resonant properties of RIS elements and its implications at 2.4 GHz using Ansys HFSS.

articleTitle: Non-destructive Testing and Evaluation of Surface-Breaking Cracks using Microwave Planar Resonator Probe
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Metallic structures are commonly employed for innumerable applications across various industries. However, stress, fatigue and corrosion can lead to manifestation of surface-breaking cracks. Non-destructive testing (NDT) of such anomalies is incumbent to maintain integrity and health of metal structures. Apart from well-known and standard NDT techniques, microwave -based inspection of cracks dates back to 1960s and has been demonstrated as a reliable modality for detection and characterization of cracks. In this paper, we present the utility of an ultra-high frequency (UHF) probe towards detection and characterization of crack on metal surface. Simulation analysis of resonance frequency shift as a function of crack width is corroborated with experimental results rendering a close match. In addition to this, the higher sensitivity of one the resonances of the probe against the other is also explained herein with the aid of field distributions and surface current maps rendered by simulations. The effect of change in magnitude with crack width is also studied. Lastly, the imaging capability of the probe towards detection of fine micro crack of width 0.07 mm is also illustrated. Overall, the potential of the probe as a reliable inspection tool for detection and characterization of micro cracks is demonstrated.

articleTitle: Design of Electronically Tunable Narrow Band Coaxial Cavity Bandpass Filter With Tunable Transmission Zero
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A novel tunable coaxial cavity narrow band filter with a tunable transmission zero is presented in this paper. A two-pole coaxial cavity designed using inductively coupled direct feed shorted quarter wavelength resonator. Electrical length of coaxial resonator is tuned using varactor loaded printed coaxial cavity at the open end of the resonator. A varactor loaded stepped impedance microstrip line capacitive cross coupling between source and load is introduced at the bottom of printed coaxial cavity to independently tune the transmission zero location. A prototype tunable filter operating from 1.8GHz to 2.6GHz with 3dB fractional bandwidth of 2.5±0.5% is designed and measured to validate the tunable filter design. Experimental tunabilty of transmission zero is also verified in this article. The measured performance of tunable filter shows good agreement with the simulation results.

articleTitle: Optimal Phase Angle Rounding-Off for Forming Closely Spaced Beams for On-board Active Phased Array System
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Modern on-board active Phased Array Antenna System (PAAS) uses Digital Phase Shifters (DPS) to perform electronic scanning. The DPS has limitation of phase angle quantization, which when employed in PAAS lead to quantization of beam scanning steps. When closely spaced beam are needed for target tracking, the quantization of phase angles due to DPS leads to rounding-off of phase angles, which causes errors in beam pointing. This paper proposes an optimal Rounding-Off approach, to form closely spaced beams with low beam pointing errors. The paper formulates an optimization problem of minimizing the beam pointing errors, and obtain the rounding-off of the required phase angles to achieve this minimization objective. The proposed method has been integrated with primitive scanning trajectories for the performance evaluation.

articleTitle: MIMO Synthetic Impulse and Aperture Radar(SIAR) for Anti-Stealth Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Anti-Stealth radar using meter wave frequency such as VHF and UHF is found to be effective against stealth targets. However, meter wave radar suffers from low angular and range resolution which does not meet the detection and tracking performance of modern microwave radar. In this paper, a new class of MIMO radar which is known as Synthetic Impulse Aperture Radar (SIAR) which uses multi-carrier orthogonal waveforms has been studied. The MIMO-SIAR uses Multiple transmitters and Multiple receivers to mitigate the angular and range resolution problem of meter wave radar such as HF, VHF and UHF radar. The study is about the use of SIAR to improve the range and angular resolution using narrow band waveforms from multiple transmitters due to scarcity of continuous gap free frequency band for radiation in meter wave and sparse Tx and Rx arrays to obtain synthetic aperture using the MIMO orthogonality principle for improved angular accuracy. We have studied multi-carrier LFM waveform with de-chirping techniques for spatial domain bandwidth synthesis. From our analysis, it is evident that the MIMO-SIAR will be the solution for anti-stealth applications in meter wave frequency with sufficient resolution in angle and range for surveillance and tracking comparable to microwave radar.

Author Keywords: Frequency Modulated Continuous Wave (FMCW) and Spatial Domain Synthetic Band-width(SDSB)

articleTitle: Space Qualified Q/V Band Receiver for High Throughput Communication Satellites
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper describes the design and realisation of a space qualified low noise, high gain receiver at Q/V band frequency, which is a part of Technology Demonstration Q/V- Band payload. The receiver is used in the front-end of Q/V payload to down-convert the high frequency radio signal (RF) at 43.1745GHz to an intermediate frequency (IF) signal of 38.075GHz. A noise figure of 4.5dB and gain more than 50dB has been achieved due to compact & novel packaging technique and indigenously designed MMIC chips. The receiver is fully space qualified & operates in temperature range of -5°C to +60°C. Details of design, fabrication, and packaging along with measured results have been discussed in the paper.

articleTitle: Tunable HM-CSIW based Self-Diplexing Antenna using Liquid Dielectric for Wireless Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents a frequency switchable sub-strate integrated self-diplexing antenna (SDA) using liquid dielectric. The antenna comprises of shielded half-mode circular substrate integrated waveguide (S-HM-CSIW) cavity, radiating slot, and feeding network. The proposed SDA can be frequency tuned by filling pockets with air or liquid. Based on the simulation results, the proposed model can be switched from 3.6 GHz to 3.94 GHz in lower band and from 4.8 GHz to 5.56 GHz in higher frequency bands, respectively. The proposed antenna has peak gains of 3.75 dBi and 4.42 dBi at 3.6 GHz and 4.8 GHz respectively, with distilled water-filled pockets. The HM-CSIW based SDA is designed on a 1.6 mm thick Rogers 5880 substrate (∊r = 2.2 and tan δ = 0.0012). This antenna has frequency reconfigurability, a simple design, and good isolation (> 29.3 dB) compared to previous designs.

articleTitle: Initial Results of Ground based SAR Experiment in an Opencast Coal Mine for Slope Stability Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Slope stability monitoring in opencast mines is very important for the safety of workers and the equipment close to the overburden dump. Ground based Synthetic Aperture Radar (GBSAR) system is widely used due to its high accuracy in measurement and all weather capability. We developed FMCW GBSAR system first time in India and operated at Dudhichua, Northern Coal Ltd. This paper presents the initial results of its performance. GBSAR images are acquired over the mining area with a corner reflector placed at different locations. The raw data were processed for single look complex images so that radar interferometry technique can be used for monitoring the slopes. The backscattered power images show the benches in the mines very clearly with the SNR of 22 dB in VV polarization, A MATLAB tool was developed for processing the raw data. The validation of the system for phase stability, interferometric coherence, and time series real time monitoring is in progress.

articleTitle: Novel 5G patch antenna designs for FR1 and FR2 frequency bands with radio network planning
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents two novel patch antennae operating in 5G sub 6GHz (FR1) and millimeter-wave (FR2) frequency bands. The FR1 patch antenna is designed to operate in sub 6GHz with VSWR < 2 from 2 to 4 GHz, peak gain of 1.8 dBi and 2.7 dBi for 2.4 and 2.7 GHz respectively. The FR2 patch antenna is designed to operate with a VSWR < 2 from 24 to 29 GHz and peak gain of 7.4 dBi at 25 GHz. A linear antenna array with <tex>$\mathbf{1}\times \mathbf{4}$</tex> configuration is designed to operate for both FR1 and FR2 patch antennae. The antenna simulations are performed in Altair Feko. Altair WinProp is utilized for practical deployment to analyze detailed radio network planning. The antenna radiation patterns are imported from Feko to WinProp and deployed as a macro and micro base station antennae for FR1 and FR2 respectively. In WinProp, data rates, throughput, signal strength, and reference signal parameters representing signal quality are evaluated. From the simulation results, with different carriers assigned to the macro and micro base stations, a maximum achievable data rate and throughput of 1.07 Mbit/s, 26.78 Mbit/s and 1.146 Mbit/s, 28.65 Mbit/s for uplink and downlink frequencies respectively are achieved.

articleTitle: Simulation of Direction of Arrival Using MUSIC Algorithm and Beamforming using Variable Step Size LMS Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In signal processing applications smart antenna arrays are used to locate sources of various signals and for beamforming. Various algorithms have been developed to determine or estimate the Direction Of Arrival (DOA). Direction Of Arrival estimation is utilized in a number of applications, including radar, navigation, communication, etc. Beamforming is a technique used for directive signal transmission and reception. In a smart antenna system antenna arrays adjusts the main lobe towards the desire user and generates null in the direction of interfering users to provide suppression. Objective of this paper is to analyze the performance of Multiple Signal Classification (MUSIC) algorithm a subspace method to estimate DOA and compare with classical Bartlett method of DOA. Beamforming algorithms like LMS and NVSSLMS are studied,analyzed and its performance parameters compared.

articleTitle: Design and simulation of a Parasitic Patch loaded Novel Broadband Antipodal Vivaldi Antenna for GPR Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: The simulation model of an Antipodal Vivaldi antenna which can operate from 470 MHz to 2.8 GHz is presented for GPR applications. The overall size of proposed antipodal Vivaldi antenna is 450 × 600 × 1.57 mm3. The analysis of the model is presented in the form of reflection coefficients, VSWR, radiation patterns, and gain in the desired range of frequencies. The simulation was carried out using FEM -based 3D EM simulator (ANSYS HFSS V. 17.0). In this proposed model impedance bandwidth of 142.5 % (from 0.47 to 2.8 GHz) and gain of a minimum of 3 dB (with maximum of 7 dB) throughout the band without any dissipative loads is achieved. The designed antenna can find its potential advantage for a UWB GPR system applications to detect items buried underneath.

articleTitle: Performance Characterization of High-Accuracy Direction-Finding in Electronic-Warfare Systems
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, performance characterization of high accuracy direction finding (HADF) of threat radars in airborne Electronic Warfare (EW) Systems is presented. HADF is an operationally critical functionality in airborne EW systems, since, for undertaking any defensive/offensive/evasive actions, direction information of adversary is fundamental. Accurate and instantaneous direction finding of threat emitters in real time is an EW force multiplier, facilitating effective battlefield cognition and mission execution with a host of tactical and strategic advantages. In the current work, the estimation method considered for the study is multi-baseline Phase Interferometry (PI). Analytical computations and MATLAB simulations form the reference framework for PI delta-phase profiling and corresponding HADF Estimation, over spectral and spatial ranges of interest, under noise-free and noisy conditions. The proposed PI prototype array has been extensively studied in an anechoic environment in far- field conditions. The paper focuses on detailed characterization of signal delta-phase measurements carried out in radiation mode with typical radar signatures, quantifying and compensating various errors in the process and quantifying the achievable measurement accuracies. Demonstrated performance sets achievability bounds at the design stage and is an important error-apportioning activity in the overall EW system design and subsequent validation.

articleTitle: Design of Aperture Sharing Thick Patch Antenna Array for Dual-band 5G Communications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This study proposes an aperture sharing thick patch antenna (TPA) for dual-band applications. A TPA is utilized to construct a Ka-band Circular Substrate Integrated Waveguide (SIW) cavity with a double slot elements acting as radiators. A Circular SIW cavity-backed antenna array elements are excited with the 1 to 4 SIW power divider. The entire thick patch antenna consist of Ka-band elements is fed with an aperture coupled feeding network. Mutual interference between two different band antenna elements is avoided by using SIW structure. The proposed antenna's peak gain value obtaining in broadside direction is 7.7 dBi at 3.7 GHz and 7.2 dBi at 28 GHz. By sharing the same aperture the antenna is intended to apply for large frequency ratio applications like 5G and satellite communications.

articleTitle: Quality Assessment of Apple Cider Vinegar and Acetic Acid Using IDC based RF Planar Sensor
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A highly sensitive tapered microstrip line-based RF sensor is proposed for quality assessment of vinegar and other standard acetic acid products. The proposed RF sensors is based on the IDC integrated SRR coupled with the tapered microstrip line to attain higher sensitivity. The tapering of the 50-ohm microstrip line to 100-ohm impedance basically improves the electric field intensity and provides better coupling with the corresponding SRR element. The integration of IDC with the SRR improves the field confinement in the sensing region, which basically improves the overall sensitivity of the designed sensor. For detecting the purity of acetic acid and vinegar specimens, the corresponding analyte is injected through 0.5mm thick glass tube into the sensing region. The acetic acid concentration in DI water is first determined here by varying the acetic acid concentration from 0 to 100%. In the later part of this work, the proposed sensor is used to establish the quality assessment of the Apple Cider Vinegar (ACV) and to distinguish between ACV and the Synthetic Vinegar (SV).

articleTitle: Circular Slot loaded ultrawideband circularly polarized Antenna
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, a circular slot loaded circular monopole antenna for ultrawideband circularly polarized applications is presented. The antenna consists of a circular radiator fed by a modified feedline and multiple slots loaded modified coplanar waveguide (CPW) ground plane. The ground plane is also loaded with quarter elliptical slot and semicircular stub to achieve circular polarization. The overall dimensions of the proposed antenna are 17×20 mm<sup>2</sup>. The antenna has an impedance bandwidth of 4.41-14.0 GHz (104.2%) and axial ratio bandwidth (ARBW) of 5.87-13.66 GHz (79.77%). It has a peak gain of 5.34 dBi. The proposed antenna provides right hand circularly polarized (RHCP) radiation patterns along +z axis. It has advantages of compact dimensions, wide impedance bandwidth and wide axial ratio bandwidth over previously reported structures.

articleTitle: Wideband Printed Dipole Antenna Array for Beam Steering
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: We propose a wideband printed dipole antenna array with beam steering for ISM band application in this paper. The proposed printed dipole antenna with balun feeding achieves a wide impedance bandwidth of 34.16% (2.07 GHz – 2.89GHz). The gain of single antenna element is found to be 8.34 dB at 2.4 GHz. To implement the beam steering, a three-element antenna array is proposed with single balun feeding. The simulation results show a fractional bandwidth of 49.58%. The gain in the bandwidth is observed to be 9 dB – 10.9 dB and a beam steering of −22° to +14°.

articleTitle: InP Based Hybrid Plasmonic Inset Fed Rectangular Patch Nanoantenna
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In the proposed structure, we designed the InP-based hybrid plasmonic patch nanoantenna at the optical wavelength of 1550. InP-based hybrid plasmonic nanoantenna is one of the alternative approaches of silicon on insulator-based hybrid plasmonic nanoantenna. This optical nanoantenna is used to transmit and receive optical signals. This proposed nanoantenna achieved a gain of 6.78dB at a frequency of 193.4THz. We achieved the reflection coefficient -15dB at 1550nm (193.4THz). At optical communication wavelengths, the InP based HP nanoantenna can be monolithically integrated with a laser and a photodetector.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Traditional Band Pass/Band Stop Frequency Selective Surfaces for Distinct Frequency Domains of Electromagnetic Spectrum
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Conventional square loop (SL) and complementary square loop (CSL) based frequency selective surfaces (FSSs) for distinct frequency range are designed, analyzed and compared in this paper. The SL and CSL type FSSs are designed to demonstrate band stop and band pass characteristics for S-band, Ku-Band, Ka-Band, G-band, Terahertz (THz) and Infrared (IR) frequency range respectively. The influence of dielectric substrate and metallic layer on FSS transmission characteristics are also studied for a purpose to identify the appropriate dielectric substrate and metallic layer to design the FSSs to obtain desired operating frequency, bandwidth of stop band and pass band and signal isolation/transmission. It is found that the signal transmission characteristics of FSSs at THz and IR frequencies deteriorates. Also, low lossy substrate materials are desired to improve the signal transmission and isolation levels at THz and IR frequency domains.

articleTitle: A NRI-TL Metamaterial Based Dual-band Phase Shifter
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents a new reconfigurable phase-shifter based upon the theory of negative refractive index transmission line (NRI-TL) metamaterial unit cells. The lumped elements are inter-switchable among them with biased polarities of two pin diodes. The design layout of the proposed phase-shifter has been studied in Keysight ADS and consequently modeled using the equivalent microstrip configuration in CST Microwave Studio solver. A compact parallel phase-shifter has been designed on the RO4003C substrate covering an area of 46.40 mm × 45 mm. The dual-band characteristics has been realized in two distinct frequency bands of 1.26 GHz and 2.4 GHz enhancing its efficiency and operating range over the respective bandwidths of 120 MHz and 200 MHz. A nearly constant of average phase differences of 110° and 60° have been achieved in the respective bands of operation. The slope of the differential phase shift has been achieved close to 5° making this device a unique one. The high return losses in the two bands of operation result in better performance of the phase-shifter. The proposed prototype can find applications in phased-array antennas, military applications and aerospace industries.

articleTitle: Development of RF Rotary Joint for IFF RADAR Application
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents a non-contacting, bidirectional, half wave cavity based RF rotary joint. It is a through bore rotary joint, where two cavities (rotor cavity and stator cavity) placed at a distance and having hole (bore) at their centers are coupled though a coupling path formed by inner walls of the cavities and wall of the through bore. Quarter wave chokes are implemented between rotor and stator cavities at middle and top parts of cavities to make them short for RF and mechanically separate. Concept is implemented in the frequency band of 1025MHz-1095MHz using HFSS. Designed rotary joints have been realized and tested. Measured results are showing close agreement with simulation results.

articleTitle: A Short Half-Cosine Slot Waveguide Leaky-Wave Antenna with Quasi Omni-Directional Beamwidth
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents a short, conformal, half-cosine slot waveguide leaky-wave antenna at Ku-band. Antenna is flush mounted onto the cylindrical airframe. There are two antennas mounted onto the cylindrical airframe with a 180-degree angular separation. Omni directional coverage through this configuration needs to be achieved by designing each antenna for a 180-degree HPBW. Antenna design is also aimed for a beam tilt of 50 degrees from antenna broadside direction and sidelobe level of less than -20 dB. Low sidelobes are achieved by designing a half-cosine shaped longitudinal slot cut on the broad wall of the waveguide. HPBW of 180 degrees is achieved by designing an extended flange in the direction of E-plane. Length of the antenna is <tex>$\mathbf{2.75}{\lambda}$</tex> at the center frequency. A short length of less than <tex>$\mathbf{3}{\lambda}$</tex>, E-plane coverage of 180 degrees, half-cosine shaped slot to achieve low sidelobe levels are the novelties of this work. Design, simulation and measurement results are presented. Measurement results are in correlation with the simulation results and met the aimed specifications.

articleTitle: Compact Coplanar-waveguide based Bandpass to Bandstop Switchable Filter with Distinct Inductive and Capacitive coupling
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A compact coplanar-waveguide (CPW) based switchable bandpass to bandstop filter has been presented in this manuscript. The bandpass consists of open-loop resonator which is centrally connected to the ground plane of CPW. The inductive and capacitive couplings are realized using grounding at the center and open ends of resonator respectively. These two couplings lead to two transmission zeros across the passband which improves the selectivity of the filter. These two paths has been analyzed using even and odd-mode stydy. A coupled-feed scheme has been implemented to couple RF energy to the resonator. A PIN diode has been integrated between input and output feed line to achieve bandpass (BP) to bandstop (BS) responses. An example filter has been fabricated for 1.1 G Hz. The filter has a power handling capacity upto 26 dBm.

articleTitle: CPW Fed SLDSL FSS Inspired Jerusalem Cross Shaped Antenna for mm-Wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper introduces a swastika-loaded double square loop (SDSL) shape-inspired frequency-selective surface (FSS)-based Jerusalem cross structure antenna (JSA) for mm-wave 5G applications. The dimensions of the antenna and unit cell of FSS are 20mm x 13mm x 0.6mm and 5mm x 5mm x 0.127mm, respectively. The FR4(Flame retardant 4 ) with an epsilon value of 4.4 is used as the substrate for the antenna Similarly, the dielectric constant value of substrate RL5880LZ is 2.001, which is used to construct the FSS structure. Jerusalem-shaped antenna (JSA) resonates at a frequency 24GHz, and the gain is 3.2dBi. Jerusalem structure antenna (JSA) resonates at a frequency of 24GHz, and its gain is 3.2dBi. The swastika-shaped frequency selective surface-inspired Jerusalem-shaped antenna provides a directivity of 7.5dBi and bandwidth of 9200MHz, respectively. The simulation results show that the frequency-selective surface-inspired antennas are the prime candidate for millimeter-wave applications in the 5G spectrum.

articleTitle: Antenna-Platform Interaction Study in Phased Array Antennas
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Phased array antenna systems (PAAS) for radars need to consider the effect of the surrounding environment and the platform for mounting to correctly assess its performance in the field scenario. This paper discusses these aspects of the design and development of PAAS. A substrate integrated waveguide technology (SIW) based U-slot microstrip patch antenna (SIW_MPA) is designed with wide beam width and wide band performance and used for realizing the antenna array for PAAS. The design cycle of PAAS includes the single element design (isolated), element performance in array environment, followed by the effect of platform and surrounding structures on array performance. A hybridization of finite element method (FEM) and shooting bouncing ray (SBR) modules in electromagnetic (EM) solver, Ansys HFSS are utilized to carry out the various simulations. The results are quite informative and useful for mast mounted phased array antenna systems.

articleTitle: Design of an S-Band Transmit-Mode Active Integrated Antenna for Low Power IoT Application
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, we present the design of a transmit-mode active integrated antenna (AIA) operating in the S-band. The proposed design consists of a radiating structure with an integrated transistor (HBT: Heterojunction Bipolar Transistor) based Negative Impedance Converter(NIC) which collectively forms the transmit-mode AIA. Here, a quasi-yagi antenna operating in S-Band is designed to be the radiating structure. The proposed AIA is designed on an FR4 substrate, which is subsequently fabricated and measured. The measured quasi-yagi antenna operates in the frequency band of 2.04 – 3.29 GHz having a gain of 4.86 dBi in the broadside direction at 2.16 GHz. The proposed antenna-NIC integrated AIA operates at a frequency of 2.16 GHz, with 5.04 dBm transmitter power, suitable for low-power IoT applications.

articleTitle: Development of High Performance Dual-Band Millimeter Wave Elliptic Patch-based Antenna
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents an implementation of a compact high-gain millimeter-wave dual-band antenna. It is worthwhile noting that the meandering approach was employed to reduce the antenna area by 40%. The designed antenna has a great potential to support the wireless body area networks that are useful in monitoring human health conditions. Particularly, the dual-band property of the antenna aids in catering to the full-duplex data exchange. The geometry of the proposed elliptic patch was analyzed to determine the highest gain which, subsequently, resulted in the achieved gain of 10.2 dBi. Finally, the design validation was obtained through the experimental measurements.

articleTitle: Design and PIC Simulation of Millimeter Wave Stagger Tuned Gyro-twystron
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this article, the design of a staggered-tuned millimeter wave gyro-twystron amplifier and its PIC simulation are presented. The stagger tuning method increases the amplifier's bandwidth, which is beneficial for radar applications. The entire amplifier RF structure has been modeled in the “CST Particle Studio” to analyze an interaction between electron beam and wave. The present simulation predicted ~340 kW RF power with ~48% efficiency, ~61 dB gain, and ~2.8 GHz bandwidth for the beam characteristics of 70 kV, 10 A.

articleTitle: A Novel Design Approach for Concurrent Dual Band Complex to Complex Matching Network
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents a novel and simple technique to match two arbitrary Frequency Dependent Complex Loads (FDCLs) to two arbitrary Frequency Dependent Complex Sources (FDCSs) at any two un-correlated frequencies. The structure allows concurrent operability. It has the versatility to transform all combinations of loads and sources. In the proposed scheme, the complex loads/sources are transformed to the same constant g-circle using single section transmission lines. The combined susceptances at the two frequencies appearing in between those two transmission lines are then cancelled through a T-section stub. The concept has been validated by designing matching networks to match load impedances ZL1 <tex>$=80-\mathrm{j}50$</tex> and ZL2 <tex>$=10+\mathrm{j}80$</tex> with source impedances ZS1 <tex>$=30-\mathrm{j}40$</tex> and ZS2 <tex>$=70+\mathrm{j}10$</tex> at frequency ratio, <tex>$\mathrm{m}=\mathrm{f}2/\mathrm{f}1=1.8,2.3,3.4,5.7$</tex> and 7.3. The simulations have been done through Keysight Advanced Design System (ADS) using ideal transmission lines.

articleTitle: Design of Hexagonal RF Surface coil for 3T MRI Scanner by Characteristic Mode Analysis
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: MRI Systems are used for diagnosis of decease in humans which provide results in the form of images. MRI images provide details of deceases in human body. For better quality of images RF coils are used in MRI system. RF coils receive the signals of interest. RF coils can be of different shapes. This paper presents the design of hexagonal RF surface coil of 3T using Characteristic mode analysis. Simulations are carried out using EM package Altair Feko 2021.2

articleTitle: Rasorber With Wide Absorption Band Before Transmission Band (A-T Type FSR)
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents a polarization-insensitive frequency selective rasorber (FSR) with wide absorption band before the transmission band. The FSR consists of two layers, the top layer is lossy layer which contains lumped resistors, while the bottom layer is a frequency selective surface (FSS) based filter layer. The proposed structure achieves a reflection coefficient less than -10 dB in the range from 3.22 GHz to 13.80 GHz (124.2%). The absorption band (80%) extends from 2.86 GHz - 10 GHz (fractional absorption bandwidth of 111%) which covers C-band fully and S- and X-band partially. Additionally, the transmission band with minimum insertion loss of 0.33 dB occurs at 12.89 GHz. The structure has a thickness of 0.09λ with respect to the lowest frequency. The surface current distribution as well as some parametric variations are studied to develop an understanding of the working principle of the proposed rasorber. Equivalent Circuit Model (ECM) is used to guide the formation of structure. The prototype has been fabricated and measured and the measured results are in accordance with the simulated results.

articleTitle: Capacitively Coupled Spoof Surface Plasmon Unit Cells Based Transmission Line with Band Rejection Capability
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, a method to achieve band rejection within the operating band of the spoof surface plasmon polariton (SSPP) transmission line is reported. Capacitive coupled unit cells are incorporated at a definite interval in the realization of the spoof surface plasmon polariton transmission line. The surface matching of spoof surface plasmon line is disturbed at some frequencies by introducing the capacitively coupled unit cells which creates a rejection band. The proposed structure exhibits a rejection band in the frequency range 8.7-9.9 GHz while maintaining the low pass characteristic of the SSPP line at other frequencies up to cut-off frequency of the line. The measured transmission coefficient is less than -20 dB over the rejection band, which proves that the signal having frequencies in the range 8.7-9.8 GHz gets rejected.

articleTitle: Design and Verification of a Novel Anchor Shaped Double Negative Metamaterial Unit Cell
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this manuscript, a novel anchor-shaped double negative metamaterial is proposed. The structure is designed to resonate at 2.45 GHz. The unit cell is designed on a 1.6 mm thick FR4 substrate having a dielectric constant of 4.4, and simulated using Ansys HFSS. The unit cell exhibits a double negative behavior and negative refractive index behavior. The robust and popularly used Nicolson-Ross-Weir and Transmission-Reflection methods were implemented on MATLAB to extract and validate the metamaterial characteristics. This novel metamaterial unit cell covers 1 GHz to 4.8 GHz which is one of the most extensively researched and employed bands of the electromagnetic spectrum. The bandwidth performance of this new structure for double negative behavior is compared to other unit cells. It shows better performance with comparable size and outperforms the other geometries. This metamaterial is well-suited for a wide range of applications like wireless communication, biomedical applications in ISM (2.4 GHz) band and <tex>$\mathbf{5}\mathbf{G}$</tex> communication services in the sub-6 GHz range.

articleTitle: Fractal Based 8-Element Multiple Input Multiple Output (MIMO) Antenna for 5G Sub: 6 GHz and WLAN Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A Novel Multiple Input Multiple Output Antenna (MIMO) with eight-element antennas is proposed. The MIMO system covers the frequency range 3.3 GHz to 6 GHz, making the antenna suitable for 5G sub: 6 GHz applications. The 5G bands covered by the antenna are N77 (3.3 to 4.2 GHz), N78 (3.3 to 3.8 GHz), N79 (4.4 to 5.0 GHz), and WLAN (5.15 to 5.85 GHz). The developed antenna works in these bands with a reduced mutual coupling of -15 dB between the adjacent elements of the MIMO system. The maximum isolation of 60 dB is obtained among the diagonal elements with a gain of 6 dBi and radiation efficiency of 97%. The proposed antenna is very compact with a low profile with dimensions of <tex>$\mathbf{72}\ \mathbf{mm} \times \mathbf{72}\ \mathbf{mm} \times \mathbf{1.6}\ \mathbf{mm}$</tex> and eight antenna elements. The important MIMO parameters like CCL (Channel Capacity Loss), TARC (Total Active Reflection Coefficient), and ECC (Envelope Correlation Coefficient) are also presented to validate the performance of the proposed eight-element antenna system under the MIMO environment.

articleTitle: Estimation of Hydrometeor Fall Velocity from ST Radar Spectrum using Bi-Gaussian Fitting and its Validation with Micro Rain Radar
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A novel approach using Hybrid Bi-Gaussian fitting is developed and applied to ST Radar raw spectrum for the identification of clear air and rain echoes. The algorithm proved efficient in separating the echoes for all classes of rainfall which enables further computation of clear air vertical velocity and hydrometeor fall velocity from multi-peaked power spectra. The validity of this novel algorithm is established by comparing the profiles derived from adaptive fitting with that obtained using fall velocity directly obtained from Micro Rain Radar (MRR). In this study, the hydrometeor fall velocity derived from ST Radar rain echo after applying the adaptive hybrid fitting is validated against the fall velocity obtained from Micro Rain Radar(MRR) operating at 24.23 GHz. The vertical profiles of fall velocity derived from ST Radar spectrum compares well with that obtained from MRR during heavy and light rainfall intensities.

articleTitle: High Reliability Wide Band Temperature Compensated Ku Band Transmit Module for BFN
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents a design, development and realization of hermetically sealed, wide band MMIC based Ku Band Transmit Module. The design incorporates ease of industry fabrication, advance gain and power control technique as well as its testability. A wide band, medium power Transmit Module having low amplitude and phase error with RS422 serial interface for onboard control. It has one input and four outputs with individual phase and gain control. A rugged and reliable gain and power compensated Transmit Module is designed for stable performance over temperature range with minimum commanding required for temperature variation over wide temperature range.

articleTitle: Intermediate Frequency Circuit Design for Ka-band Superheterodyne FMCW Reflectometer
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents the design detail of intermediate frequency (IF) circuit used in Ka-band superheterodyne frequency modulated continuous wave (FMCW) reflectometer. A complete circuit of superheterodyne consists of two or more down conversions in which the first stage uses the high radio frequency (RF) as a local oscillator (LO) frequency; further in the next stage a low-frequency reference signal is used as a LO frequency. In this work, a 200 MHz low frequency stage of receiver is designed for plasma density measurement. The circuit includes a crystal oscillator, frequency doubler, low noise amplifier, band pass filter and IQ demodulator stage. The circuit design details are presented and the experimental results of the prototyping system are given.

articleTitle: Radiation Characteristic Analysis of V/UHF Band Antennas Integrated on Aircraft using EM Tool
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, V/UHF band blade monopole and circularly polarised UHF band cross dipole antennas are mounted on the aircraft. The radiation characteristic analysis of antennas placed on aircraft carried out using full wave and asymptotic hybrid solver. The two blade monopole antennas are placed on top & bottom and cross dipole antenna on top of the aircraft. The radiation patterns are getting distorted along length of aircraft, the nulls are observed in various cuts. The nulls are around 25dB, 20dB, and 22dB for top, bottom blade monopole antennas and a cross-dipole antenna placed on the aircraft respectively.

articleTitle: Wideband Endfire Circularly Polarized Antenna using Magnetoelectric Dipole
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A wideband endfire circularly polarized (CP) antenna using magnetoelectric dipole (magnetic and electric dipoles) is proposed and investigated. The vertically polarized magnetic dipole is formed using a three-sided closed cavity and opened at one side. A feed line connects a vertically polarized magnetic dipole and a horizontally polarized electric dipole to create a CP wave in the endfire direction. A two-layer profile system is used to increase the impedance bandwidth (IBW) of the CP antenna. To validate the simulation results, measurements of the antenna parameters of the proposed structure are performed. The proposed endfire CP antenna provides (5.56-6.3 GHz) 12.47% IBW and (5.59-6.11 GHz) 8.88% axial ratio bandwidth (ARBW). The proposed endfire CP antenna has a measured maximum gain of 5.47 dBic and an endfire polarization purity of 18 dB at the centre frequency. The complete dimension of this antenna is 0.907λ<inf>L</inf> x 0.498λ<inf>L</inf> × 0.064λ<inf>L</inf>, where λ<inf>L</inf> is the lowest frequency of the IBW.

articleTitle: Design of a Microstrip Line to CPS Transition With 1:300 Bandwidth for the HF and VHF Bands
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A PCB based planar back-to-back microstrip line to coplanar strip line (CPS) transition is presented for the HF and VHF band applications. A metallic via and a slot is used to convert the unbalanced microstrip line mode to the balanced CPS mode. The measured results show a return loss better than 10 dB over 1–300 MHz. Over the band, measured insertion loss is less than 0.7 dB. Removal of any frequency dependent physical parameter helps to achieve 1:300 bandwidth. The dimension of a single transition fabricated on a RO4003C substrate with a dielectric constant of 3.55 is just 105 mm × 40 mm.

articleTitle: Design and Development of Carbon Nanofiber based Lightweight Flexible Nanocomposite Structure for EMI Shielding Application
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: The present work deals with design and development of nanocomposite structure of carbon nanofiber CNF (5 to 20 wt%) encapsulated in polyurethane using the solution casting technique. CNF15 nanocomposite (15 wt% CNF in PU) having low density ~0.112g/cm<sup>3</sup>shows the optimized value for conductivity and dielectric properties in the X-band of frequency. The total EMI shielding effectiveness (SET) of the CNF15 nanocomposite structure is above 30 dB covering the entire X-band with its maximum value of ~42.01 dB at 12.4 GHz at just 0.7 mm thick sample. The capacity to handle the complex environment and ability to work for conformal electronic devices is investigated by the measurement SET values after 1 hour of sonication in water, bending at direction and manually bending for 500 mechanical cycles. The EMI shielding mechanism is explained on the basis of dielectric properties and morphology of the fabricated nanocomposite structure, The SET is analyzed by performing the simulation using the CST microwave studio in 1–18 GHz to ensure the usage of fabricated structure for the wideband application. The high EMI shielding is achieved for the fabricated thin, flexible, nanocomposite structures, making them appropriate thin coating of conformal electronic devices in military and space applications.

articleTitle: On the study of fundamental modes of spherical dielectric resonator at millimeter-wave frequency
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: The information-rich canonical problem of electromagnetic wave interaction with dielectric spheres has been explored for over a century. This has revolutionized several state-of-art technologies in the optical frequency regime. However, such principles have not been extensively scaled down to frequencies of operation in electrical circuits. With the futuristic demand for consumer electronics subservient to millimeter-waves, the large-scale use of dielectric-based circuit elements is self-evident. As far as mass production of dielectric bodies is concerned, a spherical geometry will provide the most accessible fabrication with minimum tolerance and cost compared to other generic shapes of dielectric bodies. Hence, in this context, the current paper explores electromagnetics involving homogeneous dielectric spheres from the perspective of its potential application to millimeter-wave circuit design. Its fundamental resonance modes are analyzed in the light of Rayleigh scattering and Mie theory, followed by its testing and evaluation in the Ka-band (26.5 GHz to 40 GHz). Finally, the concept of an on-chip resonator based on the spherical magnetic dipole mode is demonstrated.

articleTitle: T/R Module Technologies for Radar EW and Communication Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper brings out the state-of-the-art technologies related to the design and development of transmit-receive (T/R) modules conceptualized and realized within Electronics and Radar Development Establishment (LRDE) for various applications such as radar, EW and Communication. The article discusses the state-of-the art T/R modules developed highlighting the associated technological challenges and indigenization approach to increase the self-reliance of DRDO in T/R module development supported with detailed case studies.

articleTitle: Millimeter-wave Polymer Rod Based Leaky-Wave Antenna Design with Open Stopband Suppression
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this work, a dielectric waveguide-based leaky-wave antenna for operation in millimeter-wave frequency is presented. The proposed antenna design features a periodic array of annular metal rings realized on a thin substrate that is wrapped around a low-permittivity Teflon rod waveguide, thereby leading to a frequency-based scan of its directive main lobe of radiation. A novel architecture of capacitive compensation in the perturbation elements is proposed, which resolves the generic limitation of open-stopband suppression of radiation from the dielectric rod-based leaky-wave antenna. The presented experimental prototype of the antenna design shows a measured gain in excess of 10 dBi over a wide operational bandwidth from 28 GHz to 40 GHz along with an input matching better than 15 dB. Simultaneously, measurements show the directive beam scanning over more than 25 degrees from the broadside axis along both the forward and backward directions. Necessary theoretical analysis is presented to support these observations and the working principle of the antenna along with the dielectric waveguide in the Ka-band. The proposed antenna design can be scaled to higher frequencies owing to its robust geometry, relaxed low-cost assembly, and ease of manufacturing.

articleTitle: Investigation of Microwave Induced Local Gas Heating in HPM Switching and Protection Using Two-dimensional Computations
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: HPM-induced plasma plays a significant role in applications such as fast high-power handling switches and power limiters to protect electronic components from HPM attacks. The efficient design requires a lower cutoff time and desired plasma formation. The presence of initial seed electrons and the strength of microwave E-field decide the cutoff time. Localized gas heating can act as a source of breakdown initiation. The work presents a 2D simulation of gas-heating effects on the HPM breakdown-induced plasma. The simulations reveal that gas-heating can result in the plasma bulk having higher effective ionization and a higher effective reduced field to sustain a higher plasma density. Gas heating lowers the neutral count in bulk together, with a high plasma density can provide a better limiter action over a wide frequency range of 1 to 40 GHz. The study highlights a significant reduction in the cutoff time in the order of 100 ns. Thus, providing a faster switching action.

articleTitle: Target Direction Agnostic Maximum SNR Beamformer: An Improved Interference Suppression Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Adaptive beamforming has become an important signal processing technique for suppression of interference/unwanted signals. Robust Adaptive beamforming (RAB) is a class of techniques that achieve interference suppression without distorting the beam in the region of interest. RAB techniques generally define a spatial sector of interest within which the target signal is expected. Further, it is assumed that no interference is present in the sector of interest. Such assumptions give rise to two main problems: 1) A mismatch in the assumption (or estimate) of target direction gives sub-optimal SNR improvement and 2) poor suppression of In-band interference (within the sector of interest). We address these issues in this work. We propose a novel RAB called Target Direction Agnostic Maximum Signal-to-Noise Ratio (TDA-MSNR) beamformer. We show that TDA-MSNR requires no prior knowledge of the target direction. Further, we demonstrate an improved in-band suppression performance compared to the other RAB techniques. We also show that algorithm is computationally efficient. Further, TDA-MSNR finds direct application to Space Time Adaptive Processing (STAP-Clutter suppression).

articleTitle: Multiband Compact MIMO Antenna for sub-6 GHz Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A multiband compact multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) antenna system is proposed for sub-6 GHz 5G new radio, LTE, RFID and internet-of-things (IoT). The proposed design has two modified truncated tetrahedron MIMO elements on top of substrate and a slotted tapered ground plane on the bottom of the substrate. This entire system covers multiple bands like 854–958 MHz, 1.38-1.56 GHz, 1.75-1.87 GHz, 2.08-2.49 GHz, 3.29-3.47 GHz and 4.09-6 GHz. The antenna is simulated using CST simulator. The results of simulation are presented in the paper.

articleTitle: Design of a Reconfigurable Wideband LNA for Multiband Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents the design of a reconfigurable wideband low noise amplifier with switchable dual bands. The LNA also achieves a continuously tunable operational bandwidth in 0.2 - 1.5GHz and 2.2GHz - 3.2GHz. It implements a switching and a tuning circuit in the input and output stage of the LNA, respectively. Reconfiguration between bands is achieved through a PIN diode in input matching network and continuous tunability in each band is achieved using a varactor diode in the output matching network. The designed LNA is fabricated as microwave integrated circuit (MIC) on FR-4 substrate. It achieves a high measured wideband gain of 9 - 14.5 dB in the lower band and around 8 dB in the upper band. Additionally, The circuit achieves a low NF of 1.2 - 2 dB in lower band and around 2 dB in the upper band. The LNA also achieves a linear and stable operation in all operation modes.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Circular Polarized Patch Antenna Using EBG Structure
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Modern wireless communication devices desire antennas with enhanced performance and low profile. EBG (Electromagnetic Band Gap) surfaces are artificially engineered to improve antenna performance. The performance of a square patch antenna over a 2D-Mushroom EBG ground plane is investigated by comparing patch antenna with conventional ground plane. In this paper, a circular polarized patch antenna resonating at 2.4 GHz, for ISM band applications is designed, fabricated and tested. The antenna is a square patch with truncated edges, exhibiting Right Hand Circular Polarization (RHCP). Circular polarization is crucial to eliminate antenna orientation requirements. Band gap nature of mushroom EBG unit cells are investigated and loaded between patch and the ground plane to eliminate back lobe and improve antenna performance. The mushroom EBG is designed to resonate at 2.45 GHz, with a forbidden band gap of 450 MHz, in-phase reflection band gap of 390 MHz and a high impedance of 3475 Ω at resonance. The introduction of EBG ground plane enhanced the gain to 5.35 dB with an excellent axial ratio at resonance and an operating bandwidth of 7%, with reduction in patch dimensions. The design was simulated in HFSS and tested using VNA after fabrication, resulting in highly correlated results.

articleTitle: Planar X-Band Reflecting Surfaces Based on Rhombic Loop Pair
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents design and analysis of two band stop FSSs offering wider band rejection along with polarization independence and linear reflection phase characteristics separately. The polarization dependent vertical dual rhombic loop (VDRL) unit cells arranged with periodicity ratio 1:2 as well as horizontal dual rhombic loop (HDRL) with periodicity ratio 2:1 exhibit two separate stop bands for TE and TM incident EM waves. Both FSSs are evolved from orthogonally oriented polarization dependent arrays of rhombic loop pairs those are first printed on both sides of dielectric substrate back-to-back (BTB) to form a BTBDRL FSS and later merged together on same side of dielectric substrate to form merged dual rhombic loop (MDRL) FSS respectively. The transmission responses of both VDRL and HDRL FSSs for orthogonally polarized incident EM waves coincide when they are cascaded back-to-back on both sides of dielectric material. The non-linearities in their reflection phase responses are compensated by merging both the arrays on the same side of dielectric substrate. The array of BTBDRL exhibits 4.15 GHz wide stop band with two transmission nulls at 7.46 GHz and 9.52 GHz respectively while the MDRL FSS provides 4.8 GHz wide stop band centered at 8.2 GHz.

articleTitle: Compact Bow and Arrow Shaped Flexible Antenna for Medical Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper focused on the design of a Super wideband compact flexible monopole antenna for Medical applications. Nowadays, there is a great demand for flexible microstrip antenna in medical applications where compact size, higher data rate, better efficiency and long-distance communication are important parameters. A tapered feed circular monopole antenna with bow and arrow shaped structure is presented for medical applications. The designed antenna has dimensions of <tex>$\mathbf{28}\mathbf{mm}\times \mathbf{36}\mathbf{mm}$</tex> using RT/Duroid substrate with a thickness of 0.508mm with permittivity <tex>$\varepsilon \mathbf{r}=\mathbf{2.2}$</tex> and loss tangent tanб=0.0009. The designed antenna was simulated using CST Studio Software and achieved a bandwidth of 55.7 GHz i.e. from 2.58 GHz to 58.28 GHz with a peak gain of 7.38 dBi. The percentage bandwidth is 183 percent and BDR 2542.

articleTitle: Multi-Octave VHF Push-Pull Power Amplifier Using Coaxial Balun
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A multi-octave push-pull power amplifier has been designed for VHF band applications. In order to validate the design, two 10-watt power amplifiers are fabricated and tested from 70 MHz to 350 MHz. The balun used in the push-pull configuration is designed using a coaxial transmission line, which can handle high power at the output. The coaxial line is encapsulated by ferrite beads to improve its performance in the lower frequency band. The balun has been characterized in terms of its mixed-mode S-parameters. The proposed push-pull architecture is tested using a 10 MHz long-term evolution signal. The second and fourth harmonics have been suppressed by more than 40 dB and 50 dB, respectively, between 70 MHz to 350 MHz.

articleTitle: A Ka-band Amplifier System with Large Gain and Wider Bandwidth for Onboard Telemetry Transmission
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Here, we present the design and development of a Ka-band amplifier system using cascaded topology. The Gallium Arsenide (GaAs) pseudomorphic High Electron Mobility Transistor (pHEMT) based amplifier system is designed to produce a reasonably high gain over a wide bandwidth with high output power at Ka-band. The Q-point of the amplifier system has been set through bias to confine its operation between the active and saturation region of the solid-state power amplifier (SSPA). It helps in realizing the maximum output power with marginal compromise in the linearity by ensuring system operation does not exceed the P1 dB compression point. The realized prototype has been experimentally evaluated through a series of measurements. It demonstrates a realized gain of 32dB with an operational bandwidth of about 17% (27 GHz to 32 GHz). The achieved output power is 1 Watt ( <tex>$+\ \mathbf{30}$</tex> dBm) with a gain flatness of better than <tex>$\pm \mathbf{0.5}\ \mathbf{dB}$</tex>.

articleTitle: Wideband High Power Amplifier Supporting 3.5GHz Instantaneous Bandwidth
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A 3.5GHz instantaneous bandwidth Solid State Power Amplifier (SSPA) is presented in this paper. To create a compact module, wideband matched device fabricated on GaN-SiC technology is used. Modular design approach followed with 37W Power Amplifier (PA) device as the basic building block. To achieve higher power, four PA devices combined in quadrature coupled fashion. Continuous Wave(CW) output power level of 100W from 2.5GHz to 5.4GHz is measured and above 5.4GHz to 6GHz 70W is measured with primary emphasis on design to reliably operate in 5:1 load mismatch condition and in -30°C low temperature to +55°C high temperature environments.

articleTitle: A TM0 Mode Launcher Designed with Gear Shaped Planar Structure
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This article presents mode launcher for surface wave excitation on a single conductor Transmission line (SCTL). The launcher is designed with planar microstrip technology on an FR4 substrate and operates between 530 MHz - 940 MHz frequency bands. The proposed surface wave launcher is simulated using CST Studio with 100 cm separation between the launcher and mounted on a single conductor transmission line. In experiment with fabricated launcher, the peak efficiency (measured S21) of −6.5 dB is observed when the two launchers are placed facing each other at a gap of 100 cm on SCTL. The presented surface wave launcher is compact, low-profile, has high transmission efficiency, and can be easily installed without harming the conductor line.

articleTitle: High Gain, Wide Band and Wide Scanning Substrate Integrated Waveguide based U-Slot Phased Array Antenna for X-band
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: The aim of this research work is to investigate a probable Substrate Integrated Waveguide (SIW) based U-Slot Microstrip Patch Antenna (MPA), operating in X-band to provide a high gain, wide scan coverage and wideband especially for radar applications. The combination of U-Slot and thick substrate leads to wider bandwidth operation. It also leads to a form factor reduction tending to broaden the beam which helps to reduce the scan loss. The SIW structure is carefully designed with an optimal form factor having fabricable via diameter to via spacing ratio. SIW structure formed from PTH vias around the element emulates the metallic cavity effect, which helps to mitigate the surface wave propagation in the substrate controlling the mutual coupling (MC) in turn. This paper presents a thorough and systematic design process enunciated with simulation results generated using ANSYS HFSS software. A 16-element U-Slot SIW MPA Array is designed and examined in this paper. The array shows a bandwidth > 15%, peak gain <tex>$\sim \mathbf{17.7}\mathbf{dB}$</tex> and scan volume <tex>$> \pm \mathbf{45}^{\circ}$</tex> with worst level of MC < -18dB over the operating frequency band. These features make it suitable for the phased array antenna (PAA) developments.

articleTitle: Dual-Band Shared Aperture Antenna (SAA) Array for Feedback-Enabled WPT Application
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A novel dual-band shared aperture antenna (SAA) array radiating at 2.45 GHz and 7.35 GHz is proposed in this paper. In order to make a compact design with low mutual coupling, a shared aperture antenna (SAA) configuration is employed. For miniaturising the antenna structure a patch radiating at 7.35 GHz is placed inside the loop antenna radiating at 2.45 GHz. The proposed antenna exhibits gains of 8.832 and 15.58 dBi at 2.45 GHz and 7.35 GHz respectively with efficiencies of −2.312 dB and −1.131 dB. Both the loop and patch array are fed by coaxial feed for the ease of integration with back-end electronics.

articleTitle: Model-Based Design and Simulation of Monopulse Tracking System
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: The monopulse principle is used in many RADAR applications to estimate the position of the target in space by calculating the error in the azimuth and elevation direction. Monopulse tracking can be achieved using various configurations of antennas and comparators. Different configurations can be used based on the requirements, but the integration of the antenna and comparator needs to be perfect to achieve the desired results. In this paper, MATLAB®, Simulink®, and RF Blockset™ are used to build a model for a monopulse tracking system with the integration of transmitter antenna, receiver antenna and comparator. The model can be tested on different antennas and comparators, and its design can be optimized to get the desired results. Integrating the antenna and comparator directly on the hardware results in amplitude and phase mismatches which can vary the outputs. Hence, it is important to simulate the integrated model to get accurate results, anticipate the mismatches in phase, and to devise a corrective action before the hardware is fabricated. The antennas and couplers are available as catalog elements in Antenna Toolbox™ and RF PCB Toolbox™ respectively.

articleTitle: A Novel Design for Polarization Control in CDRA using Integrated Cross-Slot and Annular-Slot Coupled Feeding
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: An integrated cross-slot-coupled and annular-slot-coupled is used to feed the cylindrical dielectric resonator antenna (CDRA) to control the polarization, which is demonstrated in this paper. Left-hand circular polarization (LHCP) or Right-hand circular polarization (RHCP) is operated by the proper selection of unequal lengths of cross-slot. On the other hand, Circular polarization (CP) or Linear polarization (LP) is achieved by choosing the proper width of the annular slot. <tex>$\mathbf{HEM}_{11\delta}$</tex> mode is used to generate the LHCP/RHCP and LP operation. Through the parametric study, optimum antenna designs are carried out using an HFSS-15 simulator for LHCP, RHCP, and LP based on the proposed theory.

articleTitle: Enhancement of Oblique Incidence Performance of a Microwave Absorber using Cylindrical Dielectric Resonator
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Dielectric resonator based microwave absorber is investigated here which provides broad absorption bandwidth with wide angle of incidence. Two designs have been proposed for cylindrical dielectric resonator based unit cell for realization of microwave absorber. In first design, the ring dielectric resonator is investigated, whereas for second design the concentric cylinder along with ring dielectric resonator is used in unit cell geometry. The proposed absorbers work in C, X and Ku bands which establishes the structure to have broadband absorptivity signature over a wide range of incident angles. The advantages of these absorbers are ultra-broadband absorption without using multiple layers of resistive sheets or any other bulky elements. Moreover, the absorbers are completely 3D printable and economically efficient if we want to extend the technology to large scale manufacturing.

articleTitle: Design and Development of A SIW based Narrowband Bandpass Filter In LTCC Technology
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A SIW based five-pole narrowband bandpass filter (BPF) has been designed and implemented in low-temperature co-fired ceramic (LTCC) technology. The problems associated with a narrowband BPF in LTCC technology are discussed in detail. An X-band filter with a fractional bandwidth of 230 MHz is implemented at 11.575 GHz. The filter is integrated with a back-to-back CPW-to-SIW transition for measurement purposes. The measured passband insertion loss of the transition integrated filter at the passband center frequency of 11.38 GHz is 3.194 dB. The filter provides an excellent out-of-band response, rejection being more than 30 dB below 11.13 GHz and above 11.63 GHz the passband.

articleTitle: EM Design and Analysis of FSS based Low Observable Antenna
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Frequency selective characteristics of printed patterns are employed for the structural RCS reduction of planar antennas, in view of stealth applications. A high impedance FSS based electromagnetic absorber, which exhibits its absorber characteristics in Ku-K band is incorporated with an X-band patch array. Thus, this configuration can act as an absorber in the high frequency region. Further, a low pass FSS is included in the ground plane to deal with the RCS reduction in the low frequency region. A 1×4 linear patch array is designed at 8.84 GHz with cross dipole FSS-RAS elements on the substrate, along with a hybrid ground plane. This composite structure shows a maximum out-of-band structural RCS, −12.85 dBsm and −2.83 dBsm in-band structural RCS reduction without any adverse effects on the radiation performance of the reference antenna array.

articleTitle: Dual Polarized Antenna with Guard Band Characteristics for 3G/4G and 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A Dual polarized antenna with guard band characteristics with modified dual-polarized dipole antenna using the grounded coplanar waveguide (GCPW) filter for the 3G, 4G, and 5G base station applications are explored in this research paper. Firstly, the modified dipole arms are arranged in a crisscross manner to generate orthogonal polarizations with CPW feed designed to operate in the frequency band of 1.6-3.6 GHz. Secondly, meandered slot GCPW is patterned on the modified dipole antenna and is modeled to provide band stop characteristics with sharp roll-off for 3G, 4G, and 5G. As an outcome, the anticipated antenna is operating in the band of 1.6-2.78 GHz and 3.2-3.8 GHz for VSWR < 1.6 with a guard band of 2.85-3.18 GHz. The proposed antenna provides the isolation of more than 30 dB, the half-power beam width of 70o±1 0, and realized gain of 8.73 dBi throughout the operating band of 3G, 4G, and 5G for Base Transceiver Station (BTS) applications. Simulation studies shows that for the deployed cell sites, the maximum downlink data rate and throughput were 2.03 Mbps and 50.97 Mbps, and the maximum uplink data rate and throughput were 0.15 Mbps and 35 Mbps. The maximum received power and SNIR are -50 dBm and 60 dB, and the maximum RSRP of -65 dBm, RSRQ of -11 dB, and RSSI of -40 dBm.

articleTitle: Validation of the Forward Scattering Expressions in Half-space using Full-wave Solution
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This article aims to validate the developed analytical models of scattered electric fields when cylindrical objects are buried in a two-dimensional half-space using a full-wave solution. A full-wave simulator, grpMax, works on the principle of finite difference time domain has chosen in this case as the simulator is specially designed for use in half-space. Fast Fourier Transform has been used to convert the time-domain scattered field data generated from gprMax to frequency domain when necessary.

articleTitle: Compact Dual Polarized Ultrawideband (UWB) Antipodal Vivaldi Antenna for Rover Based GPR System
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: The design of a compact ultrawideband (UWB) dual polarized antipodal Vivaldi antenna has been presented in the manuscript. 4 nos. of compact single polarized antipodal Vivaldi antennas, designed with exponential tapering, have been arranged in the box configuration. The antenna elements having like polarizations are combined with a 1:2 wideband Wilkinson power divide and hence, dual polarization has been obtained. The proposed antenna has volume <tex>$\left(0.2 \lambda_1 \times 0.2 \lambda_1 \times 0.08 \lambda_1\right)$</tex> (where <tex>$\lambda_{1}{=}$</tex> wavelength at 0.3GHz) and has been optimized to achieve the bandwidth from 0.3GHz to 3GHz. The proposed antenna structure has also been developed and characterized.

articleTitle: Planar E-plane Horn Antenna with Multiband and High Gain Characteristics
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This article proposes a planar higher gain substrate-integrated waveguide-based E-plane horn (SIEW horn) antenna that operates in the 5G frequency range. This design utilizes a flag-shaped copper strip directly connected to the coaxial feeding probe to excite the antenna from the backside of the SIEW horn.
