This strip is placed on the top plane of the bottom substrate in between the two supporting metallic strips running along via holes in the horizontal plane. An air layer is also included between the top and bottom substrates to improve the impedance bandwidth response at all five operating bands (23.38-24.36 GHz, 25.32-26.66 GHz, 27.09-28.41 GHz, 28.63-29.25 GHz, and 30.77-31.38 GHz). The proposed SIEW Horn antenna exhibits a maximum peak gain of 11.34 dBi at 28 GHz with an average peak gain of 9.05 dBi across all the operating bands. Step-by-step design procedures along with detailed physical analysis based on electromagnetic (EM) simulation results are presented sequentially. Unlike the conventional SIEW Horn, this proposed structure conceives a new feeding mechanism to realize better impedance matching.

articleTitle: A 2x4 microstrip antenna array for monopulse tracking radar at S-band
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper proposes a 2x4 microstrip antenna array for mono-pulse tracking radar in the S-Band. In the proposed design, a rat-race coupler is paired with a 2x4 patch antenna array at 3GHz. The feed is given to the sum and difference ports of the rat-race coupler to obtain the sum and difference patterns. The design aims to help in tracking. The tracking is done in one-dimensional space, and the design has limited elements with better efficiency. In the proposed design, the simulated and measured results have a return loss of at least - 10 dB at 3 GHz and the sum pattern has a main lobe and side lobe difference of at least 12 dB, while a null depth of at least 20 dB is achieved in the difference pattern. A gain of 17 dB has been noted. The simulation of this design was done on Ansys HFSS and MathWorks Antenna Toolbox softwares with an epsilon value of 2.2 of the Rogers RT 5880 substrate with a thickness of 1.6 mm. The design also contains chamfered elements to decrease the side lobe levels.

articleTitle: Design of Slotted Microwave Sensor for Evaluation of Water Quality
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, a planar Micro-strip based Slotted topology CSRR is proposed for water quality assessment. The modelled Slotted topology CSRR (S-CSRR) sensor resonates at 4.14 GHz with a Q of 226 and fractional sensitivity of 9.5%. The advantage of a Slotted structure is its improved coupling with incident E-field of the Sample Under Test (SUT) and its improved notch level in case of high loss samples like water <tex>$({\varepsilon} \mathbf{r}=\mathbf{80})$</tex>. The detection of lossy liquid like water is carried out by the inclusion of a thin Teflon layer placed on top of the ground etched sensor. The equivalent circuit of the proposed sensor is further optimized in ADS software. The sensor is fabricated on a 0.8mm thick Taconic TLY-5 substrate <tex>$({\varepsilon} \mathbf{r}=\mathbf{2.2})$</tex>. Finally, the measurement of the S-CSRR sensor is carried out for different solute concentrations of dissolved salt, detergent and sugar variants respectively in pure water for its quality assessment. With the developed sensor, it was observed that even for a slight change in solute concentration there is a significant shift in S<inf>21</inf> dB level of 0.7 dB, 0.9 dB, and 0.05 dB for unit percentage change in detergent, salt, and sugar solution respectively in the measured values.

articleTitle: Array Antennas Characterization and Fault Diagnosis in Plane Polar Near Field Test Range
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Phased Array Antennas (PAA) are now extensively used in various satellite communications. More Accurate characterization of PAA is very much required for better performance which is more challenging task nowadays. For accurate measurement of PAA, amplitude and phase of the phased array antenna should be uniform over the aperture at a fixed distance. In this paper, PAA characterization in Plane Polar Near Field Test Range and its importance in improving the Accuracy of the gain and directivity measurements by correcting the phase distribution and making it uniform over the entire aperture is described. The various measurement results have been compared and the results are shown.

Author Keywords: Near Field to Far Field Transformation

articleTitle: A Technique to Improve RCS in Passive Chipless RFID Tags by Incorporating Array Structure
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: The vast applications and advantages of chipless Radio Frequency Identification (RFID) tags have taken a broad role in wireless and identification technologies. RFID is replacing barcodes in many contexts due to being in the advantage of not requiring communication with a line of sight. The IoT industry and biomedical sector have seen an enormous use of RFID tags as a sensor for interfacing with different devices. This paper aims to analyze and compare two 5-bits resonator tags. Based on the resonator techniques, the octagonal ring structure and the array of the ring structure are analyzed. The Radar Cross Section (RCS) of both designs is compared to show a better RCS curve was obtained with the array structure. The paper analyses the improvement in RCS using a resonator array. The design uses the substrate of dimensions having a length and width of 26 mm for both. The structure designed for the tag can be used for Ultra-Wideband (UWB) applications.

articleTitle: The Design CP Square Slot Antenna with Open Loop and Single Inverted-L-Shaped Ground Strip
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: The proposed and constructed CPSS Antenna has an inverted L-shaped grounded strips at corner. By attaching a vertical stub to the feed line and an L-shaped strip to the ground plane, it is possible to increase the axial-ratio bandwidth. The lower left of the slot is opened to create broadband circular polarisation radiation. Based on the results of the experiments, a very small, broadband circularly polarised planar antenna excited by coplanar waveguide is designed and constructed in this work. The antenna is made up of a square patch, a square radiator patch, and inverted L-shaped grounded strip lines. AR and impedance bandwidth of the realised CPSS antenna measured with optimised parameters are 4.8 GHz to 8.15 GHz for S11, 4.5 GHz to 6.5 GHz for less than 3 dB ARBW. However, because the antenna's overall size is only 18 X 18 X 0.8 mm3.

articleTitle: Enhanced Gain Open-ended Waveguide Antenna using a Circular Substrate Disk
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This work presents the gain enhancement technique of a conventional open-ended waveguide (OEWG) by using a circular dielectric substrate disk backed by a thin, perfect electric conductor (PEC) sheet along with PEC rings on the front side. This technique is applied on a commercially available WR-28 waveguide to enhance its gain from 5.62 dBi to 19.45 dBi at a frequency of 26 GHz. To validate this approach, the simulations and optimizations of the OEWG antenna are carried out using the full-wave simulator, Ansys HFSS.

articleTitle: Time Modulation Using Switchable Frequency Selective Surface
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper a Frequency Selective Surface (FSS) for electromagnetic(EM) wave modulation in L-band is proposed. The presented time modulated FSS is designed for modulating electromagnetic (EM) waves reflected from it, to generate numerous sideband frequency components in the frequency spectrum of the modulated wave. The EM wave modulation is accomplished by changing the reflection properties of the FSS in time. The unit cell design of the presented time modulated FSS consists of metal strips loaded with PIN diodes. A reflection coefficient that varies with time is accomplished by using a periodic biasing signal on the PIN diodes. The modulation scheme is designed to mimic Doppler effect from a moving target. In the reflected wave frequency spectrum the sideband frequency components have more power than the incident frequency component.

articleTitle: Design of High-Power Harmonic Rejection Filter for SDR Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents a design of lumped elements based low pass elliptic filter for UHF frequency band. Elliptic filter is preferred to provide higher roll off. The filter is designed with power handling capability of 50 watts in continuous wave mode operation. The design is simulated and it is further validated by the measurement results. The experimental results show close agreement with the simulation results. The filter has a pass band cutoff frequency of 400 MHz, insertion loss better than 1.13 dB and return loss better than 14 dB. The rejection achieved is greater than 55 dB at stop-band to pass-band transition ratio greater than 1.125:1. The designed filter can be integrated with a 225 MHz-400 MHz power amplifier for software defined radio (SDR). The filter is implemented in 52 mm × 23 mm circuit area.

articleTitle: A Triple-Band Passive Detector Circuit With Improved Sensitivity
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This work presents a triple-band passive detector circuit for monitoring radiated power by the base stations at 3G, and 4G/LTE bands. The detector does not use any active component other than one single Schottky diode. A miniaturized triple-band impedance matching network is designed. This design can detect three frequencies simultaneously. A new design strategy for the input matching network helps to decrease the overall size of the detector to just 29.4 mm × 10.43 mm when fabricated in a RO4003C substrate with dielectric constant 3.55. Improved matching also helps to greatly enhance the sensitivity of the detector circuit at the desired frequency points. Measurement results show that it can detect an RF input power as low as -45 dBm without using any RF or low frequency amplifier. Compared to the previous designs, this detector has simpler impedance matching network, compactness and better response at low input powers.

articleTitle: Multifunction GaN Power Amplifier Single Chip
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A multifunction Ku-band power amplifier chipset is designed using 250nm GaN/SiC HEMT process. This single chip provides more than 2W saturated output power with large signal gain of 30dB over 10.5-12.5GHz. This chip offers higher level of integration by incorporating on-chip output power detection capability for RF telemetry and analogue gain control circuit for temperature compensation and power stability. This chip is suited for realization of pocket size SSPA for miniaturized Beacon transmitters for satellite onboard applications. DC consumption is about 13W.

articleTitle: Low Power Signal Processing Implementation Using STM32 Controller for FMCW Radar
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: FMCW Radar today finds various applications and with growing technology, the requirement of low-cost and low-budget implementation has risen. Such applications require a compact hardware design and fast, precise functioning. In aircraft, FMCW radars are used as an altimeter for computing height. In this paper, we have designed a customized signal processing card using the STM32L432KCU ARM cortex M4 con-troller. The use of the cortex M4 controller for DSP application has been discussed in this paper. The card functionality is tested with an X-band RF Module and checked with hardware and loop testing using co-axial cables with small electrical lengths. The results obtained during the experiment are up to the mark and are presented in this paper.

articleTitle: Stub Loaded Dual-Mode Dipole Antenna for Wide Bandwidth in a Compact Size
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, a compact and broadband dual-mode dipole antenna is proposed. Mode compression is utilized to achieve broad bandwidth in a compact-sized antenna. Third-order mode of the dipole antenna is compressed in the vicinity of the fundamental mode. This is done by loading stubs to the dipole arms. The loading point and the stub size play a crucial role to achieve broad bandwidth. The proposed antenna was fabricated. Antenna measurements were also carried out to validate the simulation results. Good compliance is observed in the simulated and measured results.

articleTitle: Novel Frequency Modulated Radar Waveform Generation with Improved Main to Side Lobe Ratio
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: The radar waves are designed under the type of target to be detected, its environmental characteristics, and the use of radar. Waveforms play a vital part to decide radar performance. High signal energy, high spectral efficiency, and interference mitigation can be achieved with low peak power and good radar waveforms. The efficient design of Radar waveform and waveform parameters enhances radar anti-jamming and target detection probability. In this paper dual band chirped hybrid waveforms are presented with improved main-to-side lobe ratio. Novel waveform experimentally generated with a good range resolution and 24 dB higher Main and Side Lobe Ratio (MSLR). This performance was obtained without loss of SNR, major lobe widening, and post-processing.

articleTitle: A Miniaturized Frequency Selective Rasorber Based on Meanderline and Square Slot Structure
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, a frequency selective rasorber (FSR) for getting two wide transmission windows in between the absorption windows is proposed. The proposed structure consists of a meanderline type structure surrounded by square ring and a cross dipole in the top layer and square slot in bottom layer. The FSR exhibits two transmission bands at 5.5 GHz and 7.65 GHz having bandwidth of 288 MHz and 475 MHz respectively, while the absorption windows are at 2.8 GHz and 9.45 GHz with absorptivity of 94.5% and 91% respectively. The novelty of the structure is its compactness, design, wide angle polarization insensitivity and angular stability for all the transmission and absorption bands. The surface current distributions in absorption and transmission windows have been plotted. The structure shows the angular stability upto 75° in both Transverse Electric and Transverse Magnetic mode of polarization. Keywords-absorption, FSR, meanderline, polarization

articleTitle: Design of a Spherical Lens Antenna with Multiple Meridian Hollow Dielectric Rings
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A 3D spherical lens with multiple meridian hollow dielectric rings is designed to improve the gain of an antenna unit. The lens is excited by a broadband dual-polarized high-gain microstrip antenna. The average gain is increased by 5.9 dB, reaching 15.1 dB with a maximum gain of 16.2 dBi @4.4 GHz. The impedance bandwidth of| S<inf>11</inf>| < -10 dB for the feeding antenna is 3.3 GHz-4.5 GHz, and the relative bandwidth reaches 30.8%. The diameter of the spherical lens is 150 mm, which is about twice the wavelength at the center frequency, and the structure is simple and easy to manufacture. The lens antenna has the advantages of high gain, dual-polarization, broadband, and miniaturization, which can meet the demands of a 5G base station antenna.

articleTitle: Design of a Monopulse Antenna using SIW Technology and Slot Arrays
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents a monopulse antenna designed using Substrate Integrated Waveguide (SIW) Technology and slot array concept. The monopulse antenna is designed and simulated at 24 GHz using ANSYS HFSS software. The designed monopulse antenna is observed to be having a -10dB impedance bandwidth (BW) of 540 MHz within the frequency range 24.37GHz to 24.91GHz. The normalized peak sum gain is 11.9dB and null depth of the difference pattern is about -20dB. The proposed antenna is fabricated and experimentally tested. The simulated and experimental results are observed to be in good agreement.

articleTitle: Multiplexing Gain and Sum-Rate Loss of MIMOAntennas
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: The multiplexing gain for multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) antenna for both multi-user and single-user MIMO and sum rate loss for MIMO antenna for multi-user MIMO are introduced. Several case studies for finding these new performance metrics of MIMO antennas are also discussed. The first three case studies are for three typical arrangements of antenna elements in MIMO wireless and their impact on the multiplexing gain and channel capacity loss for MIMO antenna. The fourth practical case study is for point-to-point or single-user MIMO employing highly compact MIMO antennas. The fifth practical case study is for multi-user MIMO uplink systems. The MIMO antenna for 5G mobile terminal is analyzed. Mobile terminal employed two antenna elements for the fifth case study. It is revealed that the MIMO performance is much better for the multi-user scenario as compared to the single-user MIMO case.

Author Keywords: Sum rate loss for MIMO antenna

articleTitle: Time Shared Ubiquitous Radar Architecture for Detection of Slow Moving Targets
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Surveillance Radars designed using traditional methods have limitations with respect to power, maintainability and reliability. Currently techniques are being employed to improve detection through the use of higher transmit power or transmit gain. Higher transmit power impacts weight and higher antenna gain requirement necessitates increase in antenna size. Use of innovative radar architectures and signal processing techniques provide a solution for such Size, Weight and Power (SWaP) constraints. Techniques by increasing Time on Target with parallel processing improve target detection. Ubiquitous Radar architectures allow simultaneous and effective utilisation of resources which theoretically provide an infinite Time on Target. This paper a technique is proposed to synthesize multiple beams simultaneously and process the beams in parallel which effectively improves the Time on Target. Customised Ubiquitous Radar architecture is proposed to improve radar detection capability of slow moving targets without increasing the radiated power and antenna aperture. This is achieved through effective utilisation of the RF hardware resources. Paper also explores possibility of using MIMO waveforms to improve update rate and detecting fast moving targets. Proposed architecture can be used in both FMCW and Pulsed Radar configurations. The proposed signal processing schemes were simulated and feasibility was ascertained for various target scenarios.

articleTitle: Intelligent Reflecting Surfaces for Wireless Communications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents a systematic methodology for active and passive Intelligent reflecting surfaces (IRS) implementation for wireless communication. A 20 x 20 periodic array with variable Microstrip patch unit cell and PIN diode loaded Microstrip patch unit cell are proposed for passive and active IRS implementation respectively at X band. The passive IRS is demonstrated for predesignated incident (Theta −15° & Phi 0°) and reflected (Theta 15° & Phi 45°) angles of the signal with peak scattered reflection of 18.2dBsm. Digital codes are used to evaluate the performance of 20X20 element active 1-bit IRS for multiple beam scenario. The peak scattered reflection varies from 21dBsm to 16dBsm and scanning angle varies from 5° to 60° for normal incidence.

articleTitle: A Monopole Filtenna Based on Square Loop Resonator for Wireless Communication
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A narrowband planar monopole filtenna using filter synthesis technique is demonstrated in this paper. A Square open loop resonator along with L shaped antenna is utilised to get the filtering characteristics. A coupled line used to integrate filter and antenna without extra matching circuitry. It consists of one arm of the last resonator filter and extended feed arm of the antenna, for proper integration between filter and antenna. The simulated result shows that, the proposed filtenna provides a narrow impedance bandwidth of 7.14% (2.43 - 2.61 GHz) with a good selectivity at band edges, wide rejection band, with an omnidirectional radiation pattern well suited for wireless application.

articleTitle: Dual Polarized Phased Array Antenna Element for SATCOM on the Move Application
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Polarization diversity is one of the key requirement for Active Electronically Scanned Array (AESA) based SATCOM on the move application. Polarization diversity enables polarization tracking which mitigates loss of signal between the satellite and the terminal while on the move. This paper presents a dual polarized cavity backed patch antenna element for a Ku band phased array SATCOM on the move application. The dual polarized aperture coupled Microstrip patch element has a low profile and light weight. The element is designed in an array environment by using EM Simulation Software HFSS. The design of the element incorporates vias around the patch element to emulate a cavity in order to minimize the coupling between the elements. The simulated performance of the dual polarized aperture coupled microstrip patch element in an 8X8 array is presented in this paper.

articleTitle: Wideband and High Gain Circularly Polarized Microstrip Antenna Array using Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A metasurface based compact dual-feed <tex>$2 \times 2$</tex> circu-larly polarized antenna array is proposed in this paper to operate in the C band. Each single element consists of a stub inserted dual-feed square-shaped patch stacked between the ground and metasurface with <tex>$4\times 4$</tex> periodic unit cells. The sequential phase rotational approach is used to realize wideband circular polarization characteristics. The overall size of the <tex>$2\times 2$</tex> antenna array is 68 mm x 68 mm x 3.2 mm <tex>$(1.25\lambda_{0}\times 1.25\lambda_{0}\times 0.059\lambda_{0})$</tex>, at an operating frequency of 5.5 GHz. Metasurface based dual-feed 2 × 2 antenna array structure obtains -10 dB impedance bandwidth of 4.32-7.52 GHz (58.18%),3 dB axial ratio bandwidth of 4.48-6.62 GHz (38.9%), 3 dB gain bandwidth of 4.66-6.34 GHz (30.55 %), and simulated radiation efficiency greater than 83 %. The simulated results of the proposed circularly polarized antenna array exhibits good performance in terms of -10 dB impedance bandwidth, 3 dB axial ratio bandwidth, 3 dB gain bandwidth, gain, and radiation efficiency.

articleTitle: Side Lobe Reduction and Interference Rejection in Concentric Hexagonal Antenna Array using Differential Evolutionary Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Side lobes and interference signals result in decreased performance of antenna array. In this paper a method to reduce the side lobe levels (SLL) and for rejecting the interference signals in Concentric Hexagonal Antenna Array (CHAA) using differential evolutionary (DE) algorithm is presented. CHAA will give lower SLL compared to circular and linear antenna arrays and are hence preferred in the presented method. DE algorithm is an evolutionary algorithm in which mutations are performed by combination of individuals and an optimized solution is obtained. The simulation results are presented for a single ring CHAA, 4 ring CHAA with 2 different interference signal scenarios and a 6 ring CHAA with 2 different interference signal scenarios. From the results it can be inferred that there is a 6 dB SLL reduction in single ring CHAA and at least 8 dB and 9 dB SLL reduction in 4 and 6 ring CHAA. Also, nulls with a minimum of -60dB have been placed in 4 different interference signal scenarios.

articleTitle: A Wideband Circularly Polarized Patch Antenna for Active Array Radar Applications in X Band
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This article presents a wideband circularly polarized patch antenna designed on PTFE (Teflon) substrate in X band. The simulation of the design shows that by introducing two asymmetric diametrically opposite slots on the patch, two orthogonal modes are generated which can create a phase difference of 90° on the radiated fields. Particularly, this antenna achieves an impedance bandwidth of 45.36%, (7.7-11.8) GHz, axial ratio (AR) bandwidth of < 3dB (9.05-9.8) GHz which is 8.51% and a gain of over 5 dB in the X band. The designed antenna has the potential to be used in the formation of an active array system for weather and unmanned aerial vehicle detection radar.

articleTitle: Compact Wideband Uni-directional Circularly Polarized Antenna
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A compact circularly polarized two-arm Archimedean spiral antenna backed by a shallow cavity is presented. Different miniaturization techniques were incorporated to reduce the overall dimensions of the conventional cavity-backed spiral antenna. Rigorous iterations on the spacing between the spiral and cavity back plate were carried out to achieve optimum performance. The overall dimension of this fabricated antenna is <tex>$0.326^{\star} \lambda_{\mathrm{L}}$</tex> diameter and <tex>$0.0393^{\star}\lambda_{L}$</tex> height. The fabricated prototype antenna exhibits a measured VSWR bandwidth (VSWR <tex>$\leq 2$</tex>) of 1.4 GHz to 9.7 GHz and measured Axial Ratio bandwidth <tex>$(\text{AR}\leq 3\text{dB})$</tex> of 1.3 GHzto 7 GHz.

articleTitle: Wideband Widebeam Dual Polarized Magneto Electric Dipole Antenna
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A wideband widebeam dual-polarized magneto-electric (ME) dipole antenna is presented. The antenna element is implemented by orthogonally combining a pair of slotted stair-shaped radiators, stair-shaped feed lines, and metallic columns to impart a wide impedance bandwidth and beamwidth. Simulated and measured results show that the antenna has stable radiation performance with a return loss of better than 10dB in the span of 1.85-3.65GHz (>65<sup>%</sup>). Over the bandwidth antenna gain varies from 2.44-6.28dB with 3dB beamwidth in the range of 113°-153°.

articleTitle: Sub-6GHz Novel C-Shaped Antenna for 5G Application
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A novel C-shaped antenna design resonating at Sub-6GHz band for 5G application is reported in this work. The radiator is etched on FR4 dielectric <tex>$({\varepsilon}_{\mathbf{r}}=4.3)$</tex> having height of 1.6 mm. On the other side of dielectric, the mirror image of the radiator is etched on the ground plane which is an inverted ‘C’. Conventional quarter-wave transformer is designed to match the antenna impedance to 500. The entire dimension of proposed design which is simulated in CST Microwave Studio is 34 ×32 × 1.6 mm<sup>3</sup>that achieves the gain and bandwidth of 3.4 dB and 500 MHz at the resonating frequency of 3.5 GHz lying in mid-band frequency range allocated for fifth-generation.

articleTitle: Design of Triple Band RF Energy Harvesting System Using Monopole Antenna
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, a triple band rectenna consisting of a rectifier and the corresponding antenna for the GSM 1.8 GHz, Wi-Fi 2.4 GHz and WiMAX 3.5 GHz bands is proposed. The triple band antenna is chosen to be a Y-shaped monopole antenna along with an L-shaped slot in partial ground plane. The antenna is analyzed numerically using the CST Microwave Studio. The designed antenna is linearly polarized at 2.4 GHz and circularly polarized at 1.8 GHz and 3.5 GHz, henceforth minimizing the losses due to misaligned orientation of the receiving antenna. The antenna size is 40mm x 60mm and it is fabricated on a low cost FR4 substrate. The triple band rectifier is designed using the Villard voltage doubler topology. Radial stubs are used for the designing of matching circuit. The rectifier is then integrated with the designed antenna configuration. The designed rectenna is analyzed numerically using circuit simulation ADS Software. The measured efficiency of the rectenna is 39.2% at 1.8 GHz, 35.1% at 2.4 GHz and 21.11% at 3.5 GHz corresponding to 3.5 dBm input power.

articleTitle: Millimeter-wave Wideband Half-Mode SIW Phase Shifter based on IDC Slots and Thin Dielectric Slab
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This research work proposes a compact, low-profile, wideband half mode substrate integrated waveguide (HMSIW) phase shifter employing interdigital capacitor (IDC) slots and a very thin dielectric slab. The proposed phase shifter design is divided into three sections. An HMSIW with a series of rectangular grooves are etched on the top conducting layer to obtain the initial phase shift. Next, the IDC-based slots are engraved to further improve the phase shift. Lastly, the phase shift is obtained in wideband due to the extra loading of the dielectric slab patterned with rectangular strips that constitutes the final structure. The proposed three versions of the HMSIW phase shifter designs provide a phase shift of 15 degree, 70 degree, and 101 degree, respectively, for the three cases with an overlapping bandwidth of 24.6 GHz to 33.2 GHz corresponding to a fractional bandwidth of 29.7%.

articleTitle: Coupled Characteristic Mode Splitting Analysis
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This manuscript focuses on mode splitting phenomena in the context of the theory of coupled characteristic modes (TCCM). Unlike the conventional approach of temporal coupled mode theory or wave-guide mode theory, it utilizes the full-wave method of moments impedance matrix to understand the mode coupling mechanisms. It investigates the underlying mathematical mechanisms to generate the cross-over of the coupled eigenvalues. It also provides a closed-form solution of the eigenvalue perturbation. Numerical experiments have been reported with an array of dipoles. The proposed modal analysis of generalized eigen mode splitting will be useful in applications like antenna shape synthesis, mutual coupling control, bandwidth enhancement, etc.

articleTitle: Dual Band Antenna Array for Concurrent Shared Aperture Operation
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: The paper presented herein introduces a novel method for the practical implementation of dual band antenna (DBA) arrays that are well-suited for simultaneous multifunction operation. The antenna elements operating at L-and C-band frequencies and sharing the same physical aperture allow for the antenna to serve multiple purposes. To achieve the desired radiation characteristics, a Genetic Algorithm (GA) is used to determine the optimal inter-element spacings for L-band frequency elements and C-band frequency elements. Two non-uniformly spaced antenna (NUSA) arrays, one consisting of a <tex>$\mathbf{1}\times \mathbf{8}$</tex> -element linear array operating at L-band and the other a <tex>$\mathbf{2}\times \mathbf{32}$</tex> -element Planar array operating at C-band, have been interleaved into a common aperture, and their numerical, EM simulation, and experimental studies have been conducted to validate the feasibility of the proposed approach for the development of a multi-functional antenna array.

articleTitle: Co-axial fed W-shaped wideband antenna with defective ground plane for WLAN Application
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, co-axial fed W shaped wideband antenna with defective ground plane for WLAN Application has been proposed. The proposed antenna is designed to operate from 5.68 to 6.65 GHz. The designed antenna achieved bandwidth of 18.9 % (5.68 −6.65) GHz and has good gain in resonating frequency band.

articleTitle: Efficient fault diagnosis in an antenna array incorporating mutual coupling
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: The inverse problem for locating faulty elements in an antenna array from electromagnetic field measurements is an interesting and relevant research topic. We present a novel idea based on compressive sensing to detect the faulty elements from fixed probe measurements, which is based on the optimizing of the element excitations. Unlike many previous works, our approach considers the inter-element mutual coupling effects and identifies their importance in fault diagnosis. This study illustrates the effects of coupling in a loop antenna array with varying array sizes. We used two coupling models, namely, the average embedded pattern and the coupling matrix approach to include coupling effects in the analysis. Our work significantly improves antenna array fault diagnosis using the coupling-aware method compared to the existing methods.

articleTitle: Fast and Hardware-Efficient Variable Step Size Adaptive Beamformer
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Constant step size least mean square (CSS-LMS) is one of the most popular adaptive beamforming algorithms. However, for varying channel signal-to-noise ratios (SNRs), the CSS algorithms are not effective, and there is a need for variable step size (VSS) algorithms. The VSS algorithms provide extremely deep nulls for the interferences; however, they are complex to implement on hardware. Hence, this paper proposes two hardware efficient variable step size algorithms namely, efficient variable step size LMS (EVSS-LMS) and reduced complexity parallel LMS (EVSS-RC-pLMS). The proposed EVSS algorithms eliminate the complex operations of VSS algorithms like division and exponential and approximates them to simpler operations. Further, MATLAB simulations demonstrate accelerated convergence, deep nulls, lower error floor, and better performance in varying SNR environments for the proposed algorithms. Additionally, the finite precision radiation patterns are similar to infinite precision. Hardware synthesis results show the outstanding performance of EVSS in terms of resource utilization on the Xilinx Artix-7 FPGA.

articleTitle: Gain Enhanced mm-Wave Dipole Patch Antenna with an End-fire Radiation for 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A uniplanar compact End-fire dipole antenna with a size of 20mm×19mm and height 0.8mm is proposed for 5G applications. An array of a Double Negative (DNG) cells is introduced on the planar antenna structure for a flat gain enhancement of 4 dB throughout the bandwidth(BW) of 4 GHz., i.e., 24–28 GHz. The maximum obtained gain is 9.8 dBi, and maximum efficiency of 92% is achieved after double DNG cells loading. The front-to back-ratio (FTBR) is 20.59 dB and is improved by 9.78 dB due to double DNG cells loading.

articleTitle: Design and Development of 100 GHz Quadrature Heterodyne Interferometer system at IPR
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, we are report design, development, and characterization of indigenously developed 100 GHz Heterodyne interferometer system which provides real time plasma density measurement. The developed system consists of two free running Gunn oscillators which have been used as radio frequency source (RF) and local oscillator (LO) and produce stabilised intermediate frequency (IF) of 850 MHz using biased mixers for the down conversion at low power of LO.The IF signal is then coupled to an IQ demodulator for the generation of IQ signals. IQ for in phase and quadrature phase are known as IQ. Using highly stabilised signal conditioning electronics and DAQ system, the IQ signal is then processed by the Arctan function in MATLAB and LABVIEW for the phase measurements. Also these signals are coupled to FPGA based system to generate real-time signal. The developed system has the sensitivity or the noise floor - 69 dBm and dynamic range - 65dBm to -10dBm. The IQ phase imbalance is +/-15 degree(0.26 radian)

articleTitle: Front-to-Back Ratio Improved 60 GHz Substrate Integrated Coaxial Line Balanced Antipodal Vivaldi Antenna
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A new front-to-back ratio (FBR) improved Balanced Antipodal Vivaldi Antenna (BAVA) is presented, with optimized microstrip (MS) to Substrate Integrated Coaxial Line (SICL) feed, that operates in the frequency range of 57 GHz to 67 GHz. The MS-SICL transition facilitates unimodal wideband operation and improves the FBR by a maximum of 7.14 dB at 62 GHz and a minimum of 1.01 dB at 57 GHz. With the dimensions of <tex>$\mathbf{45\times 19\times 0.26}$</tex> mm3, it is compact in size and a significant enhancement of gain is observed by selective positioning of metallic vias with a maximum peak gain of 11.36 dB at 58 GHz. S11 is observed to be less than -10 dB throughout the band of operation. Stable electric field distribution along with consistent radiation patterns are achieved in the E-Plane. The proposed structure maintains a good impedance bandwidth centered around 62 GHz and maintains stable gains throughout the working frequency range.

articleTitle: A Slotted Circular Patch Antenna with Defected Ground for Sub 6 GHz 5G Communications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, a slotted circular patch antenna with Defected Ground Structure (DGS) is presented. The slots created on radiating element and the defect introduced on the ground plane shifted the resonance frequency from 2.49 GHz to 1.17 GHz. This corresponds to 53% reduction in size at 1.17 GHz. The proposed antenna is designed on FR-4 substrate <tex>$(\varepsilon_{r}=4.4)$</tex> with thickness of 1.6 mm. Simulations are carried out using HFSS Ver. 18.2. The simulated reflection coefficient of Circular Patch Antenna (CPA) at 2.49 GHz, Slotted Circular Patch antenna (SCPA) at 2.34 GHz and Slotted Circular Patch antenna with Defected Ground Structure (SCPA-DGS) at 1.17 GHz are − 28.7 dB, −31.33 dB and −11.03 dB respectively. For validating the simulated design, SCPA-DGS is fabricated and measured its reflection coefficient and VSWR using Vector Network Analyzer (Anritrsu S820E). The measured and simulated values are very well matched with each other. Therefore the proposed antennas may be used in sub 6 GHz 5G communication applications.

articleTitle: Trident Shaped Compact Planar Antenna for Microwave Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A compact planar antenna for X/Ku-band microwave communication is suggested in this paper. The presented geometry is capable of radiating the large frequency band from 6.8 to 20GHz, which covers the X-Band/Ku-Band Communication with high efficiency. The impedance bandwidth of the radiator is 98.5%, with an electrical size of. 34λx.34λx0.034A in lambda. The suggested design includes a modified patch in the trident shape fed by a microstrip line. Rectangular elements have been designed for better resonances at lower modes. The antenna is simulated with an FR4 substrate using CST Simulator. The exact dimensions of the antenna are 15x15x1.5 cubic millimeter. Five stages evolution process is also investigated by simulations, and corresponding S-parameter results are presented. The proposed structure also demonstrates stable radiation patterns across the operating bandwidth. The proposed radiator has a high gain of 3.1 dBi, and an efficiency of 87%. Therefore, it is useful for X-band, and Ku-band, including Radar, Space, Terrestrial, and Satellite microwave communication.

articleTitle: Compact Dual-Band CRLH Metamaterial Planar Antenna in Laptops for WLAN/WiMAX Frequencies
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A simple, compact, and efficient dual band metamaterial planar antenna has been designed for WLAN/WiMAX applications. The antenna is designed on FR-4 substrate of 1 mm thickness, and is electrically connected to a 15.6-inch laptop ground plane. The antenna studied achieves a -10 dB reflection <tex>$(\mathbf{S}_{\mathbf{11}})$</tex> bandwidth of 240 MHz (2.34-2.58 GHz) in the 2.4 GHz band and 2.65 GHz (4.2-6.85 GHz) in the 4 GHz-7 GHz bands. It shows relatively higher peak realized gains, higher antenna efficiencies as well as improved omnidirectional characteristics in the azimuthal plane (plane transverse to the plane of the antenna structure). The computed results indicate that the designed antenna can be suitable for WLAN/WiMAX applications in laptop antenna.

articleTitle: Wide Band Polarization Insensitive Absorber using Thin Resistive sheet
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A polarization-insensitive absorber for wideband applications is presented in this paper. This proposed absorber can cover the entire X-band and partially in C-band and Ku-band. It contains a symmetric resistive patch on the upper surface of the substrate, and the bottom of it is entirely covered with copper. This proposed design has only 2.4 mm thickness. It is found that the absorber can absorb the signals from 7.31GHz to 16.70 GHz (nearly 9.39GHz bandwidth) with 90% absorptivity. The proposed absorber maintains the absorption at incidence angles up to 45 degrees for TE modes and up to 60 degrees for TM modes, respectively.

articleTitle: A compact ground-slitted CPW-fed polarization reconfigurable antenna for wireless LAN applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Here, a small, CPW-fed monopole antenna with reconfigurable polarization is introduced. Two stubs positioned at each side of the monopole radiator are connected to the ground plane via two p-i-n diodes to achieve an asymmetric ground plane. Two horizontal slits inside the ground plane assist in increasing the impedance matching. The antenna either produces linear polarization or left/right circular polarization, depending on the p-i-n diode's switching state. The structure was fabricated, and its performance was evaluated to confirm the planned design. At 5.8 GHz frequency, the requisite S11 bandwidth (IBW) and axial-ratio (AR) bandwidth is attained by correctly incorporating the stubs and slitting the ground plane. Two C-shaped metal strip is loaded on top of the substrate layer to increase the AR bandwidth. The measured impedance bandwidth is 5.50-6.10 GHz (600MHz, 10.34%) and the AR bandwidth is 5.52-6.0 GHz (480MHz, 8.62<sup>%</sup>) for circular polarization and 5.25-5.81 GHz (560MHz,10.18%) impedance bandwidth for linear polarization. With a maximum CP gain of 3.8 dBic, the suggested antenna displays a nearly uniform gain over the operational AR bandwidth. The recommended antenna is appropriate for higher frequency WLAN applications and has a compact structure with a large 3dB AR bandwidth.

articleTitle: Rectangular Patch, U & H Slot Triple Band Antenna for Different Wireless Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, a rectangular patch microstrip line fed partial ground plane antenna for the triple band operation is developed and analyzed. For designing the antenna, low cost FR4 epoxy substrate with the overall dimensions of <tex>$80 \mathrm{mm} \times 78.93 \mathrm{mm} \times 1.58 \mathrm{mm}$</tex> corresponds to <tex>$0.34 \lambda_0 \times 0.335 \lambda_0 \times 0.0067 \lambda_0$</tex> is used. For creating the different resonance bands, an additional strip and combination of U-shaped and H-shaped slots are embedded on the patch. Partial ground plane ensures the bandwidth enhancement at lower resonating frequency. For inspecting the antenna performance, different parameters like reflection coefficient, gain, radiation efficiency and E, H plane radiation patterns are analyzed. CST MWS is used for the simulation purpose and simulated results shows impedance bandwidth of 1.56GHz (1.275-2.84GHz), 433MHz (3.334-3.767GHz) and 1.46GHz (6.79-8.25GHz). Gain and radiation efficiency variation of antenna is in between 2-3dBi and 67-90% respectively with omnidirectional radiation pattern. Proposed antenna ensures its applicability for GSM 1800, Wi-Fi, WLAN, WiMAX and UNII-8 bands.

articleTitle: Isolation Improvement in MIMO Using PRSR with DGS for Wireless Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In order to improve isolation, a two-element Microstrip Patch Multiple Input Multiple Output (MIMO) antenna with a Parallel Rectangular Strip Resonator (PRSR) with Defected Ground Structure (DGS) has been implemented in this work. The PRSR is made up of two rectangular strips that are parallel to one another and are spaced closely apart. The proposed decoupling configuration gives band stop characteristics over the operating range from 5.08 to 5.27GHz with edge-to-edge distance of 4mm (<tex>$\mathbf{07}\boldsymbol{\lambda} \boldsymbol{o}$</tex> at 5.17GHz) on FR-4 Material. The technique enhances the antenna parameters. The improved isolation and reflection coefficients are -38.8dB and - 32.74dB, respectively. Diversity gain and Envelope Correlation Coefficient (ECC) over the operational range are found to be more than 9.99dB and less than 0.00006 respectively. The proposed design is suitable for WLAN and WIFI applications.

articleTitle: Active Wideband Polarization Insensitive Absorber for Ku and K-Band
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents a simplified active frequency selective surface (AFSS) design with a wide tuning frequency range. The structure uses four variable resistance p-i-n diodes (NXP BAP 70–03) to achieve this characteristic. Secondly, the biasing complexity of the AFSS is simplified. The AFSS operates with -10 dB reflectivity in the 17.5-21.5 GHz and in both transverse electric (TE) and transverse magnetic (TM) modes. The unit-cell design strategy to achieve this response is discussed.

articleTitle: Simple Way of Controlling Cross-Polarized Radiations from Dielectric Resonator Antennas Without Affecting Other Salient Features
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This work explores a simple technique of ground plane engineering to optimize the radiation characteristics of a Dielectric Resonator Antenna (DRA). It identifies the unruly fields in the corners of a ground plane, and subsequently discards the corners from a ground plane. This eventually leads to a uniform co-to-cross polar isolation over the entire azimuth. In addition, it helps in reducing the ground plane size by 20-25%, keeping all other antenna characteristics unchanged. This simple technique to XP reduction, especially over the Diagonal Plane should find potential applications in commercial usage.

articleTitle: A High Gain Switchable Beam Reflectarray Antenna for Sub-6 GHz MIMO Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, the design of a high gain switchable beam reflectarray antenna for 5.8 GHz MIMO applications is presented. A three-port microstrip patch MIMO antenna which operates at a center frequency of 5.8 GHz, is used to excite the reflectarray surface for switching the radiation beam in the xz-plane. The unit cells of the reflectarray have an overall volume of 0.49λ x 0.49λ x 0.13λ (λ is the wavelength at a frequency of 5.8 GHz). The reflectarray consists of 19 x 19 1-bit phase quantized unit cells. The switchable beam reflectarray has a focal to dimension ratio of 0.23. The feed antenna elements have a center-to-center distance of λ/2 between each other, and mutual coupling of less than 22 dB is obtained at 5.8 GHz. The reflectarray antenna can tilt the beam in ±5° along the x direction. The antenna shows gain of 18.2dB in port-1 with a scanning loss of 0.5dB in the two offset radiation beams. The radiation beams in the xz-plane have a half power beamwidth of 5°. The antenna can be used in sub-6 GHz radar systems and cellular and satellite communications. The antenna prototype is fabricated, and performance parameters are measured.

articleTitle: Obtaining the True Antenna Pattern Based on Measurements in Non-Ideal Condition
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: The accuracy of navigation systems depends on the direction finding of passive objects or beacons and is based to a decisive extent on the antenna characteristics. Measuring antenna radiation pattern (ARP) is an important step in both the design and verification phases. Nevertheless, many universities and small technology companies do not have the proper infrastructure to run this type of test. In this paper, we analyze the possibility of retrieving ARP from the measurements in non- ideal test conditions, which are mainly due to the short distance to the irradiator and the moderate quality of the absorbent coating on the walls of a compact chamber. The basic idea is to represent the total field irradiating the tested antenna by a converging cluster of plane waves. To do this, a probe antenna must first measure the total field on the surface surrounding the antenna under test. The results of the numerical simulation confirm the robustness of the proposed algorithm for retrieving ARP from the data of real measurements.

Author Keywords: a converging cluster of plane waves

articleTitle: A Compact Printed Quasi-Yagi Antenna with End-Fire Radiation Pattern Over Super-Wide Bandwidth
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, a simple microstrip line fed super-wideband quasi-Yagi antenna (QYA) is presented. A bow-tie shaped monopole is employed as a driver for higher impedance bandwidth (BW) and a simple feed structure. The shape of the reflector and director are modified to obtain impedance matching and directive end-fire radiation. A prototyped antenna has been fabricated and tested where measured results agree well with simulated ones. With a very small profile of 45 mm × 55 mm, the proposed antenna obtains a super-wide impedance bandwidth from 1.54 to 16 GHz (164.8%, at 8.77 GHz mid-frequency), a peak gain of 5.9 dBi, and good end-fire radiation performance. The measured cross-polarization levels and front-to-back ratio are better than 18 dB and 8 dB, respectively. Furthermore, in comparison with previously published QYA, it has a simple feed structure, simple design, widest BW, and smallest overall footprint.

articleTitle: A Very Narrow band Ka-band cavity Filter
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper is aimed to discuss the design of extremely narrow band filter with a fractional BW of 0.016% at Ka band with capability to operate at wide range of temperature. For realizing a very narrow bandwidth filter with low loss, resonating structure with high quality factor is needed. Cylindrical cavity with TE<inf>011</inf>mode is the most optimum choice for this type of realization owing to its high unloaded Q and low loss characteristic. However, its realization poses its own challenges. The filter presented in this paper is a 4-pole Chebeyshev filter designed and developed at 30.5 GHz with 0.016% fractional bandwidth. The return loss is better than 20 dB over the temperature (-10°C to 60°C) with maximum insertion loss of 2.94 dB and rejection is better than 20 dB at CF±25 MHz. This type of filter is highly required for the tracking chains used in multi-beam satellites.

articleTitle: A Conical Shape Monopole THz Super Wideband Antenna For MIMO Application
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents a conical shape monopole super wideband antenna. The proposed antenna consists of a conical shape radiator fed by tapered feedline and a defected ground plane. The simulation result shows that the proposed antenna offers an impedance bandwidth of more than 185% varying from 2.2- 60 THz. For antenna element peak gain of more than 12 dB is achieved. Besides, the proposed antenna is used to design a <tex>$\mathbf{2}\times \mathbf{2}$</tex> MIMO configuration. The isolation more than 25 dB is achieved throughout the frequency band.

articleTitle: A compact slot and strip-loaded ultrawideband antenna with reconfigurable band-notched behaviour
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This article presents a compact frequency reconfigurable slot-loaded ultrawideband (UWB) antenna with triple rejected bands. The gaps between the parasitic elements and radiating structure are loaded with metallic strips for frequency reconfigurable property. The operation of the UWB antenna changes from single band elimination to dual and triple band elimination by connecting and disconnecting the metal strips. A low loss Rogers RT/Duroid 5880 substrate (thickness 0.79 mm) is used for antenna design. The antenna performance is studied in terms of return loss, gain, efficiency and radiation characteristics. The proposed design has advantages like compact and simple structure along with band elimination characteristics for portable UWB applications.

articleTitle: Circular Shape Dual Element MIMO Antenna for 5G (Sub-6GHz) Application
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this article, a two-element multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) design is suggested for use in sub-6 GHz 5G wireless access points operating in the 3–4 GHz frequency range. The proposed antenna uses microstrip fed circular shape and the optimized bandwidth and isolation are obtained using an E-shaped stubs associated with partial ground plane. Ansys HFSS simulations are used to describe the proposed antenna's design process. Each antenna element has a peak gain of 2.12dBi. Simulated results are verified with measured results and found a good agreement between them. The diversity performance of MIMO antenna is also studied with envelop correlation coefficient (ECC) <tex>$<\ \mathbf{0.15},\mathbf{DG}\approx \mathbf{9.98}\mathbf{dB}$</tex> and mean effective gain (MEG)-ratio within <tex>$\pm \mathbf{3}\ \mathbf{dB}$</tex>. The proposed antenna is designed on FR-4 substrate with a dimension of <tex>$\mathbf{30}\times \mathbf{20}\times \mathbf{1.6}$</tex> cubic millimeter.

articleTitle: A Transmittive-type Metasurface for Dual-band Linear to Circular Polarization Conversion
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, a transmittive-type dual-band linear (LP)-to-circular Polarization (CP) converter has been reported. The structure can convert the incident LP wave into right-handed circularly polarized wave in two non-adjacent frequency ranges of C and Ku bands. It bears a tri- layer configuration of three concentric square shape split ring resonators having slits oriented along 45° with each other. The simulated results show that the axial ratio of the proposed converter is under 3-dB over the frequency ranges of 4.07-4.15 GHz and 14.19-14.51 GHz. The ellipticity of the structure is - 0.98 and -0.99 at 4.1 GHz and 14.3 GHz, respectively; thereby confirming the right-handed CP nature of the transmitted wave. This transmittive-type metasurface can be easily mountable to a simple dual-band LP antenna to obtain the desired dual-band CP wave for satellite communication system. The structure has the periodicity of λ/5 while maintaining thickness of λ/6.6 w.r.t. the center frequency of the first conversion band.

articleTitle: Top Loaded Wideband Electrically Small Antenna and Its Quality Factor Analysis
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This work presents a top-loaded wideband electrically small antenna (ESA). Here a 2D metallic (PEC) strip is loaded at the top of the conventional monopole to design an electrically small antenna. The bandwidth enhancement mechanism of the proposed antenna is analyzed by considering fringing field capacitance between the ground plane of the CPW feed and radiating element. In addition, to support the effectivity of the proposed method, the lower bound Quality factor (Q.F<inf>lb</inf>) of the proposed antenna is estimated by considering the theoretical limitations of an electrically small antenna. The overall surface area of the antenna is 0.2λ×0.15λ, where λ is the wavelength at 4.4GHz. The antenna exhibits −10 dB impedance bandwidth of 1950 MHz for the intended 5G WLAN and new radio (n79) applications. Furthermore, it offers more than 85% efficiency with an omnidirectional radiation pattern over the operating band. The achieved impedance response and radiation characteristics validate the suitability of the proposed antenna for indoor wireless applications.

articleTitle: Analysis of Impairments, Error Correction and Evaluation of Adaptive Antenna Arrays Based on Vector Modulators Beamforming ICs
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper describes the impairments, calibration, evaluation and integration of core ICs for antenna beamforming using vector modulators. The analysis of the main sources of degradation in vector modulators such as amplitude and phase imbalances, quantization noise, isolation, and phase variations with amplitude control are presented. The impact of limited isolation on the system phase margin and the accuracy of phase and amplitude is also discussed. A 4-TX and 4-RX channels vector modulator core IC with 8-bit phase resolution has been fabricated. A 2-step calibration method for phase and amplitude was employed. The phase calibration is initially performed directly at the phase measurements of the core IC with a second step for amplitude calibration carried out at the antenna array. By reducing the errors associated with the quantization noise and applying 2-step calibration for the phase and amplitude, very low sidelobe levels were obtained. New applications in the area of antenna beam forming which traditionally suffered from limited suppression of the interference due to the high sidelobe levels can be explored by realizing vector modulator core ICs with having low error sources and using separate phase and amplitude calibration techniques.

articleTitle: Active Frequency Doubler at X-Band
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Wide band frequency multiplier at X-band using GaAs MESFET is presented in this paper. Calculation and optimization for a wide band frequency doubler (X2 multiplier) using classical theory is performed and then the same is implemented using non-linear harmonic balance simulation of Advanced design system. CFY25-20P is used as an active non-linear device and implemented on alumina substrate. The salient features of this work is that it is providing worst case conversion loss of 5.71 dB with 47dBc suppression at fundamental frequency and having stable performance over the temperature extreme from -15°C to +55°C.

articleTitle: Investigation into a C-Band Probe-fed Asymmetric Circular Microstrip Antenna with Improved Radiation Characteristics
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this work, an asymmetric circular microstrip antenna has been proposed for with two fold objectives: i) to reshape substrate E-field beneath the patch structure that leads to XP radiation suppression, ii) to introduce minimal perturbation over the patch surface for ease in fabrication. The structure is low profile, and easy to manufacture. The proposed structure exhibits improved CP-XP isolation of around 20–30 dB along the bore-sight. The proposed antenna exhibits flat top radiation patterns in both the planes with a gradual roll-off, which enhances the novelty of the design.

articleTitle: Experimental Study of Outdoor Radio Wave Propagation Scenario Near the L-Shaped Building
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: The radio wave Propagation scenario around an L-shaped building has been demonstrated in this work. The experimental study has been carried-out using the long-range technology. The theoretical results are computed by employing uniform theory of diffraction based formulations, in a deterministic manner, to incorporate the multiple wedge diffracted rays in the shadow region of the building. The theoretical and experimental results are also compared with results obtained using the Method of moments based Electromagnetic simulation tool.

Author Keywords: Radio Wave Propagation and Uniform Theory of Diffraction

articleTitle: Frequency and Pattern Reconfigurable Cylindrical Dielectric Resonator Antenna
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This study aims to design a frequency reconfigurable and pattern reconfigurable cylindrical dielectric resonator antenna (DRA) with a single PIN diode. A PIN diode is used to achieve reconfigurability across two bands at 4.8GHz and 6.5GHz. The cylindrical DRA is excited with two different hybrid modes HEM<inf>11</inf>δ and H EM<inf>21</inf>δ at lower and higher frequency bands respectively. A different radiation pattern is produced also achieved at two different frequency bands. The antenna gain is stable with 5.5dBi and 5.8dBi in bands 4.5GHz and 6.5GHz respectively. The proposed antenna is suitable for C band applications.

articleTitle: Design of COCO Antenna with Bandpass Filter Based on Micro-Coaxial Structure
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In order to achieve the further integration of RF terminals, a design scheme of coaxial colinear (COCO) antenna with bandpass filter based on micro-coaxial structure is proposed. For the COCO antenna, the simulated <tex>$\vert S_{11}\vert$</tex> parameter is below -15dB in the frequency range of 28.65-29.75GHz, the maximum omnidirectional gain on the H plane can reach 6.82dBi, and the out of roundness is less than 0.49dB. For the filter, the <tex>$\vert S_{11}\vert$</tex> parameter is below -10dB in the frequency range of 28.3-33.6GHz, the insertion loss is less than 0.5dB, and the 30dB rectangular coefficient is 2.38. When the two parts are connected, the <tex>$\vert S_{11}\vert$</tex> parameter of the filtering antenna is less than -10dB in the frequency range of 29.2-30.5GHz, and the maximum omnidirectional gain on the H plane is 7.44dB. The size of the filter antenna is only <tex>$59 \text{mm} \times 6.3 \text{mm} \times 0.7 \text{mm}$</tex>, using wafer level micro coaxial processing technology. The designed filtering antenna has the characteristics of ultra miniaturization, lightweight and high integration, and can be used in the integrated circuit of various small electronic communication equipment.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of 1.5 GHz LNA with Sufficient Gain and Noise Performance
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper aims to provide a deep insight into design and analysis of Hybrid Microwave Integrated Circuit of a low noise amplifier (LNA), functioning at 1.5 GHz with an operational bandwidth of 90 MHz (1.48 GHz to 1.57 GHz), suitable for very narrowband (5.9 % fractional bandwidth) application. The designed prototype has been printed on FR-4 board and assembled with Surface Mount Devices; with “ATF-21170” as an amplifying candidate. The proposed LNA has minimum gain of 13.08 dB and maximum noise figure of 1.95 dB. It is unconditionally stable in the operational band. Moreover, this LNA offers a very good non-linear characteristic; Output third order intercept point (OIP3) nearly 17.5 dBm. It also gives a 26.9 dB isolation between output and input port.

articleTitle: CPW Fed SRR Inspired Decagon-Trident Slotted Shape Antenna for On-Body Communication
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: The coplanar wave guide (CPW) fed split-ring resonator (SRR) inspired trident-slot dual band antenna is designed for on-body communication. The miniaturized, flexible, and low-cost antenna has been designed on a commercially available Teflon substrate. The proposed antenna is mainly used for wearable medical body area network applications (MBAN). Decagon-trident slot provide dual-band resonance are observed at 7.9GHz, and 12.3GHz frequency, with return losses of 26dB, and 40dB, respectively. Due to biocompatible material, low cost and small size, high gain, and bandwidth, the proposed antenna is highly fit for healthcare monitoring applications.

articleTitle: Digital signal processing simulation for plasma electron density measurement on FPGA
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Heterodyne interferometry is an active diagnostic techniques for electron density measurement. Measured line integrated electron density is related directly to phase difference between transmitted and received microwave sig-nals. Phase variation measurement requires different phase detection techniques. Analog and digital phase measurement techniques are available for real time density estimation during plasma discharge. However, the analog circuit of the phase measurement is prone to noise handling and phase jump. This can be overcome by digital phase measurement techniques. Digital phase measurement having controller and high speed FPGA have become very popular for electron density measurement. FPGA based digital phase measurement techniques (zero cross, Fast Fourier Transform, CORDIC, ArcTAN and cross -correlation) are available for real time density measurement in tokamak. The zero cross and CORDIC plus zero cross algorithm have been developed on FPGA for phase estimation between two electromagnetic waves. The FPGA algorithm has been simulated with Vivado-15 and the density compared with density measured by 140 GHz heterodyne interferometer for functional validation.

articleTitle: Manpack Antennas for Tactical Communication Radios
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents the design of a whip antenna operating in VHF/UHF band using multi stage passive loading and a wideband impedance matching network. The antenna loading location and passive elements are optimized for stable radiation pattern. The designed antenna is optimized on man-pack platform in presence of approximate human body model. The effect of earth ground on the radiation pattern is also studied. The developed antenna is made of flexible spring steel material for use in tactical communication radios. The designed antenna has a gain more than -12dBi and VSWR <3 from 30-512MHz. Simulation and measured results are presented.

articleTitle: A 10 Port MIMO Antenna For 5G NR Smartphones in the Sub-6GHz
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A 10 port MIMO antenna design to work in the frequency range (4800–5250) MHz is presented for the 5G New radio (NR) Smartphones in the sub-6GHz. The 10 antennas are identical and placed in a symmetrical manner. The presented MIMO antenna is composed of a L shape slot with one end having a unique staircase shape slot structure. The proposed structure was both simulated and a prototype was practically verified. The dimensions of the prototype were 150mm×75mm which is a typical 6.6 -inch display. The measured results show that the measured reflection coefficient was better than −6dB and isolation is lower than −10dB between any two antenna pair elements in the n79 band. The ECC (envelope correlation coefficient) was found to be lower than 0.07 for the frequency range (4800–5250) MHz and is a good MIMO antenna array candidate for the upcoming 5G Smartphones in the sub-6GHz.

articleTitle: Experimental Demonstration of Optical PAM-4 Generation for Short-Reach Optical Communications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: The demand for higher bandwidth is increasing exponentially due to high-speed applications and increase in the number of users accessing internet. To meet this demand several modulation techniques are proposed which have higher spectral efficiency exploiting different dimensions of the optical carrier amplitude, phase, and polarisation. Further, by combining wavelength division multiplexing scheme with the dimensions of the optical carrier, capacity of the network can be further enhanced. Optical telecommunication networks can be broadly classified as long and short-haul, where m-Quadrature amplitude modulation (m-QAM) schemes are popular in former, and 4-level pulse amplitude modulation (PAM-4) is a promising economical solution for latter. In this paper, a proof-of-concept technique of generating optical PAM-4 signal is proposed. Experimental demonstration and simulation of PAM signal generation and transmission is done at bit rate 240 Mbps and baud rate 120 Mbps over various fiber lengths. Generation of signal optically circumvents the need for high speed electronics transmitter and also it is possible to exploit the complete dynamic range of the optical source characteristics, which otherwise would be limited to linear region. This concept can be extended to Integrated optics for very high signal rate generation optically.

articleTitle: Hardware Impairments in mmWave Phased Arrays
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: The impact of hardware impairments on the array radiation characteristics of a fully integrated 8 × 8 5G mmWave phased array is presented. The inherent hardware impairments arising in the various building blocks (2 × 2 antenna unit cell, quad-channel Tx/Rx beamformer chip, power dividers, and feed network) of the proposed phased array are captured through simulations. The effects of systematic and random hardware impairments on the radiation characteristics of the proposed 5G mmWave phased array are simulated and presented. The hardware impairment values are randomly varied over 100 iterations, and their impact on peak power, sidelobe level, and beam pointing angles are analyzed. Hardware impairments show a maximum variation of 1.6dB in the main lobe, -12dB first sidelobe level, and 3° beam pointing error for a uniformly weighted array.

articleTitle: A Surface Wave Launcher Designed with Biconical Monopole feed
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This article presents a TM<inf>0</inf> mode launcher with surface wave propagation on a single conductor transmission line. The launcher operates between 4.90 – 5.12 GHz frequency band and can excite the surface wave signal on a single conductor transmission line. For excitation of TM0 mode at the input port of the circular waveguide, a mode feed is also designed for converting TEM mode (Coaxial TEM) to TM0 mode with high efficiency. The suggested design is simulated using CST Simulator with 100 cm separation between the launchers. The designed launchers are attached to a single conductor transmission line. The peak efficiency (measured S21) of −5 dB is observed when the two launchers are facing each other and placed at a gap of 100 cm on SCTL. The proposed launcher supports the transmission and reception of microwave signals over existing power lines for power line communication.

articleTitle: Air and Ferrite Core Loaded Axial Mode Helical Antenna for Completely Filled Cylindrical Water Pipe Network
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper reports design and performance comparison of an air core and ferrite core loaded axial mode helical antenna for completely filled cylindrical water pipe network at 5 GHz and 500 MHz operating frequency. Due to the finite permeability and permittivity of hexaferrite material, 74.18 % reduction in size has been achieved at 500 MHz. Further, we performed an experimental study for empty and completely filled cylindrical water pipe network. With the help of electromagnetic wave solver CST Microwave Studio, signal transmission distance of 50 meter have been achieved in completely water filled piped network. The gain of the designed antenna is: 10.5 dBi.

articleTitle: Mushroom Shaped Printed Monopole Antenna for UWB Application
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A mushroom-shaped printed monopole antenna with simple in structure and low profile is designed in this paper. To obtained UWB characteristics here use the mushroom-shaped circular radiating patch and defective ground plane on the opposite side of the substrate. To increase the gain and the bandwidth a rectangular stub is added on the defective ground plane. To design the antenna Ansys HFSS software is utilized. The dimension of the antenna is 35×34.9×1.6 mm3 with 5.4% reduction in size compare to conventional design procedure. Commercially available low cost FR4- epoxy substrate is used here. The structure gives simulated impedance bandwidth (IBW) 8.5 GHz, ranges from of 3.1-11.5 GHz, fulfilling ultra-wideband (UWB) application standards (3.1-10.6 GHz) with a fractional bandwidth of 128.0 percent and a maximum simulated gain of 4.9 dBi

articleTitle: Ex-Vivo Performance of A Multiband Catheter Antenna Suitable for Percutaneous Tumor Ablation at 2.4 GHz
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A multiband reactive loaded quarter-wavelength monopole antenna designed as a catheter applicator working at and around ISM bands with center frequencies at 1.38 GHz, 2.4 GHz, and 5.2 GHz is proposed herein for microwave ablation of superficial and deep-seated tumors. The design, conceived from the standard techniques of series inductive or shunt capacitive loading of monopole antenna for better impedance matching, has been improvised herein for high permittivity percutaneous applications for providing flexibility and tunability in catheter antenna design. It comprises a quarter wavelength monopole <tex>$(L=\lambda/4=30\ \mathbf{m} \mathbf{m})$</tex> loaded with a helical coil and a parallel plate capacitor connected in series and this whole ensemble is enclosed in a biocompatible parylene catheter tube <tex>$(\epsilon_{r}=3)$</tex>. The series reactively loaded catheter antenna portrays a peak gain varying over 1.38-2.25 dBi with uniform monopole type radiation at all the aforesaid frequencies of operation thereby producing a spheroid ablation zone intended to ablate near spherical hepatic and renal tumors.

articleTitle: Performance Investigation of Absorption Characteristics of Pyramidal Absorbers of Agricultural Residues
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Agricultural residues are eco-friendly and biodegradable alternatives to otherwise utilized polystyrene and polyurethane foams as pyramidal absorbers for applications in an anechoic chamber. In this investigation, test samples of two agricultural residues, namely, corn husk and wheat straw composites using polyester resin have been fabricated, and using the transmission line method their dielectric properties are measured in X- band. Also, two designs of pyramidal microwave absorbers are modeled in CST microwave studio with the measured value of dielectric parameters. Also, absorption performance has been evaluated by studying return loss profile of the corn husk and wheat straw composites based pyramidal array microwave absorber and double pyramidal array microwave absorber.

articleTitle: Uncertainty in the Antenna Measurements with the Broken Absorbers
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: The pyramidal absorbers are very costly affair in the design of the Anechoich chamber (AC). Also, as they are 3-D structure and fragile, the possibility of breaking it while doing experiments is very much. In this paper the authors have proposed to use the broken absorbers and calculate the difference in the reflection <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(S_{11})$</tex> of the absorber for normal and oblique incidence for height of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L/2,\ 3L/4$</tex> compared to the full height <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(L)$</tex>. It is observed that the maximum error in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S_{11}$</tex> for the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$3L/4$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L$</tex> is - 5 dB for oblique incident till 40°. This analysis tells that the even if the absorber is broken by <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L/4$</tex>, the measurements could be done with some uncertainty. The reflected fields in the quiet zone (QZ) which is 600 mm in front of the absorbers of different <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L$</tex> is simulated for the front wall. From the analysis it is observed that the electric field reflected in the QZ is same for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$3L/4$</tex> absorber array.
