However, for the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L/2$</tex> array absorber, the reflected fields are 31 dB (V/m) more than the previous <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L\mathbf{s}$</tex>. The simulations for the side walls with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$3L/4$</tex> array absorber is also done.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of Aircraft Communication Antenna for Lightning Strike Protection : A Coupled Electrical and Thermal Analysis
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper addresses direct and indirect effect of lightening on aircraft components. The lightning phenomenon is the discharge of a charged particles from cloud to the earth. A substantial risk exists if lightning strikes an aircraft. It is struck at least once per 1000 hours of flight. It is crucial to shield the antenna from lightning strikes as it is a conductor located on the skin of the fuselage. A VHF (Very High Frequency) and UHF (Ultra High Frequency) antenna is modelled, and the performance evaluation is carried out and it is observed that the frequency is within the given range. The gain is 4.5dB and 6.58dB respectively. Current component A and C are considered as there could be a direct lightning attachment to antenna since it will be protruding outside fuselage. Rise in temperature for an antenna under lightning strike is simulated and analyzed by coupled electrical-thermal study. Further a comparative analysis was done considering copper and aluminum materials and observed that temperature rise in copper is lower than aluminum material. Level 5 is considered for the present case as antennae are located in a severe electromagnetic environment.

articleTitle: Design and Investigation of Broadband High-Efficiency Continuous Inverse Class - F Power Amplifier
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents the design and experimental results for a broadband highly efficient power amplifier. The power amplifier (PA) was implemented by extending the continuous inverse Class-F mode through the use of resistive-reactive harmonic terminations. The desired load and source impedances were achieved through the design of hybrid stepped-impedance matching networks. Measurement results show that the designed power amplifier achieves 74 - 90% efficiency and an output power of 43.2 - 46.5dBm over the frequency band of 1.5 - 2.7 GHz. Investigation into harmonic suppression showed harmonic levels lower than -18dBc over the band. A two-tone inter-modulation test was performed, resulting in IM3 levels of better than -17dBc. The PA was tested using a 1.8GHz 1Msps 16-QAM excitation for an average output power of 39.6dBm, where the power amplifier exhibited an average efficiency of 56%.

articleTitle: Compression Mount Connector-to-SICL Transition Optimization at Millimeter-Wave Frequencies
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A transition optimization for vertical launch solder-less compression mount connector to substrate integrated coaxial lines (SICL) transition is presented up to K and Ka bands. The design for the coaxial-to-SICL transition is delineated while emphasizing on the key design parameters considering fabrication feasibility using printed circuit board (PCB) technology. Through full-wave simulations, an improvement of 1.07 dB in the insertion loss exhibited by the coaxial-to-SICL transition is demonstrated by using an array of plated through hole Vias in the vicinity of the transition. Furthermore, potential causes of performance degradations due to imperfect ground connections and SICL bending due to compression are considered. It is shown that SICL bending minimally impacts the performance, however, inadvertent effects such as an air gap may prominently impact the connector performance.

articleTitle: Low Profile Dual Polarized ‘Ʊ’ Shape Loaded 4G and 5G Antenna for MIMO Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A dual band and dual slant ± 45 deg polarized omega shape loaded MIMO antenna element, operating for 4G LTE-A (2.3-2.4 GHz) and 5G (3.4-3.6 GHz) applications is presented. Dual band is realized by introducing ‘Ʊ’ shape is loaded with the S-type slots in the planar printed dipole antenna element. The omega dimensions, length and width of the slots increases the total electrical length and are optimized to operate antenna in dual band 4G and 5G. Dual slant ±45 deg polarization is achieved by utilizing two such modified dipole antennas in orthogonal orientation. Unidirectional radiation for 4G and 5G simultaneous operation is achieved by concatenating electric conductor as ground plane. The antenna is backed by metallic ground plane at λ/4 for 4G and 5G operations. Antenna exhibits a measured beam width of 72 deg and 89 deg with gain of 7.32 dB and 8.12 dB for a VSWR 1.5 and 2.0 in 4G and 5G frequency bands respectively.

articleTitle: Analysis of SNR Enhancement in 1.5T MRI by Using Metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) is a clinical diagnostic tool for detection of malfunctional tissues and organs in a human body. The image resolution and scanning efficiency of MRI are directly dependent on signal-to-noise ratio (SNR). A higher SNR can be obtained by increasing the RF magnetic field which is accomplished by using metamaterials or metasurfaces. Here we present a thin metasurface which can be used as an ‘add-on’ in clinical 1.5T MRI for its SNR enhancement. A convoluted cross-type structure has been employed for increasing the magnetic flux density in the region of interest (ROI) by local confinement of electromagnetic fields in the near field region. A dielectric phantom made up of saline solution is integrated with the metasurface to demonstrate the enhancement of magnetic flux density up to a depth of 105 mm. The metasurface placed behind a human head bio-model, to emulate virtual brain-scan, results in SNR enhancement by a factor of 400 on the surface of the phantom.

articleTitle: Effect of Pulse Width on Various Performance Parameters of UWB Antenna in Time Domain Analysis
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: The paper highlights the effect of various pulse width of monocycle pulses from a signal source of UWB antenna on time domain parameters and its importance for selecting a suitable pulse width for far field communication of UWB antenna. The effect of different pulse widths on antenna parameters like the reflection coefficient, group delay, transfer function and power spectral density are analyzed for a star shaped printed UWB antenna which operates from 6.5 to 10 GHz with 48% impedance bandwidth (<tex>$\mathbf{S}_{\mathbf{11}} < -\mathbf{10}\ \mathbf{dB}$</tex>). For the mentioned antenna the monocycle pulse with pulse width 150ps and 200ps provide suitable performance.

articleTitle: A Resistive Sheet Based Absorber for Ku Band Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This article describes a metamaterial-based Kuband microwave absorber. On top of the substrate, there are metallic patterns with sheet resistance. The geometry parameters have been tuned to achieve an absorption level of over 90% in the 10.02-18.02 GHz frequency range. Also, the design has two absorption peaks with more than 90% absorption at 11.24 GHz and 15.97 GHz. Examining the design electric field and surface current profile helps to explain the absorption process.

articleTitle: Circularly Polarized Substrate Integrated Waveguide Filtenna for S- band Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: The paper presents a circularly polarized SIW(Substrate Integrated Waveguide) filtenna for S-band application. The parasitic patch with HMSIRC acts as a filter to pass the desired band.Furthermore, a Fractal Modified Ground Structure (FMGS) aids the generation of circular polarization. The impedance bandwidth of the antenna is obtained as 110 MHz/4.81 %(2.35 GHz-2.46 GHz) with an axial ratio bandwidth of 8 MHz/(2.436-2.444 GHz). The antenna radiates in Right Hand Circularly Polarization with gain of 6.37 dBi at the operating frequency 2.44 GHz.

articleTitle: Planar Tapered Metasurface Unit Cell Shaped Array for Augmenting Multipart Radiating Systems for 5G mm-Wave Beam Forming Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This article presents a four-port antenna design for beam forming applications between 26GHz to 29GHz, FR2 band of frequencies. It incorporates a gradually tapered size of metasurface unit cell as an array that results in a Gradient Refractive Index Metasurface (GRIM). The metasurface unit cells are meticulously designed to operate at the desired range of frequencies and two such surfaces are integrated with four CPW-fed planar Yagi-Uda antennas, which inherently offer high gain, narrow beam radiation patterns suitable for beam steering purposes. The article presents the design methodologies followed by simulation results for validation. Single and dual antenna beams are generated using the proposed architecture with control over their tilting angles and beamwidth, with stable pattern characteristics over the frequency range of operation. For generating the non-trivial radiation patterns and controlling the same, suitable port excitations are chosen for this multiport antenna system and fixed phase differences are introduced between the ports concerned to enhance the functional diversity of the structure.

articleTitle: A Novel Broadband 3D Pyramidal Antenna for UWB Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this article, the authors have developed and presented a novel 3D pyramidal antenna for ultra-wideband (UWB) applications. The proposed antenna has only 2 design parameters yet yields a wideband frequency response. The reflection co-efficient (S<inf>11</inf>) bandwidth (S<inf>11</inf>< -10 dB) covers the UWB frequency specifications from 3.1 GHz to 10.6 GHz. Over the entire bandwidth, the radiation pattern is observed to be consistent as well.

articleTitle: SIW Cavity Backed Elliptical Patch Antenna with Wideband Characteristics for 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, a new technique to design a compact substrate-integrated waveguide (SIW) cavity-backed antenna have been proposed. This technique utilizes a metallic feeding strip sandwiched between two layers of the same substrate and directly connected to the center conductor of the coaxial feed. Due to the incorporation of the metallic feeding strip, effective electrical path length increases, which shifts the operating frequency to a lower frequency range on a large scale. As a proof of concept, an elliptical cavity is designed by conceiving this new feeding mechanism that helps to shift the lower cut-off frequency from 32.97 GHz to 23.67 GHz without increasing the size of the cavity-backed antenna. Further, focal feed, slot-loading at two focal points, and incorporation of the metallic rod at the slot positions are also conceived to improve the radiation properties. A broad impedance bandwidth (IBW) ranging from 21.65 GHz to 31.49 GHz (37.03%) has been observed, with a peak gain of 4.86 dBi at 24.50 GHz. The design evolution and operation mechanism are discussed based on electromagnetic (EM) simulation results.

articleTitle: Beam Steering Antenna Array based on Reconfigurable Feeding Network
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents the design of a wideband pattern reconfigurable antenna array using a reconfigurable feeding network. The proposed antenna consists of three stacked dielectric substrates. Two rectangular parasitic patches are arranged on the top layer of the third substrate to widen the antenna bandwidth. To achieve the reconfigurability in radiation pattern, a reconfigurable feeding network is designed and arranged on the bottom layer of substrate 1. By turning the states of the pin diodes, the different excitation paths can be selected to steer the radiation pattern. The proposed antenna can steer its beam discretely from -36 deg. to +36 deg. with respect to the antenna broadside within the overlapping bandwidth from 4.6 GHz to 5.6 GHz.

articleTitle: Re-engineering of Quad Channel IF Receiver to improve reliability & manufacturability
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper describes about re-engineering, redesign & development of a Quad channel single stage down converter. This downconverter module is a part of ERP unit that forms a major entity for Track Radar operating at Ka band. Quad channel IF receiver is second stage of down conversion. The first prototype was made meeting all necessary specification. But had multiple sub-assemblies and interconnection, resulting in complex & time-consuming assembly & manufacturing process. Also due to multiple interconnects reliability of module was at stake during extreme operating conditions. Thus, version two design was taken up to address these issues. The major challenges were to meet key specifications like Isolation between channels, Gain & phase tracking between channels and Noise figure over temperature (-25°C to +55°C) with minimum sub-assemblies & interconnects. This paper discusses first prototype design, its drawbacks, then the second prototype to meet short comes of first prototype and a comparison of both. This paper gives insight about how to improve DFX i.e., design for X (X- Manufacturability, Assembly, Reliability).

Author Keywords: multi-layer composite PCB. Channel to channel Isolation

articleTitle: Development of Corona and Multipaction-Free Waveguide Offset-Iris Filter for X-Band TT&C Application in Deep Space Missions
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: For the new deep space missions, for the first time, X-band has been proposed for the telemetry, tracking and command (TT&C) application. Design of filters at higher frequencies with high power handling capacity and high rejection requirements, but free from the inevitable high-power problems under vacuum conditions viz., corona and multipaction, is challenging as the size and internal dimensions are small. This paper presents development and qualification of waveguide offset-iris filter, designed to operate at the transmitter frequency band (8.42 to 8.54 GHz) with a CW power level of about 10.0W and an insertion loss of better than 0.25 dB. To achieve isolation between high power transmitter & sensitive reviver, filter with a rejection of better than 80.0dB at the receive band (7.0-7.3 GHz) is designed. Furthermore, the high-power test results show that the filter is free from corona and multipaction.

articleTitle: Electronically Tunable Reflection Type Phase Shifter Using PIN Diode As A Variable Resistor
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents a new attempt to utilize the PIN diodes as variable resistors to realize a continuously tunable phase shifter. A diode is used in parallel to a capacitor. Thus, the diode resistance and hence the imaginary part of the impedance can be varied. The tuning range of a varactor capacitance is usually limited to 1:2. However, the resistance of a diode can vary from a few Ohms to a few kilo Ohm. Therefore, a much wider tuning range is possible. The next challenge is to reduce the power lost in the real part of the impedance. As an example, a reflection-type phase shifter (RTPS) is designed and implemented at 2.4 GHz.

articleTitle: High-Selectivity Wideband Filter With Ultra-Wide High-Attenuation Stopband Region Using Mixed Lumped-Distributed Circuits
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents design of a wideband bandpass filter exhibiting high passband selectivity and ultra-wide stop-band with high rejection levels. The design is based on mixed lumped and distributed elements. A wideband cell, consisting of two series LC tank circuits coupled through an open-ended microstrip stub, provides a quasi-elliptic passband with wide bandwidth. The tank circuits suppress the harmonic passbands of the open stub to a certain extent, which is enhanced by integrating sharp-rejection low-pass sections at the access ports of the wideband cell. The novel design of the low-pass sections enable achieving high out-of-band rejection levels. The composite filter exhibits ultra-wide stopband on account of multiple transmission zeros introduced by the constituent circuits. A prototype filter, designed at the center frequency of 0.528 GHz with 3-dB bandwidth of 72.5%, shows rejection better than 42 dB from 1.12 GHz to 6.2 GHz (138.8 %). The measured selectivity factor, defined as the ratio of 3-dB to 30-dB bandwidths, is 0.735. The size of the filter is 0.128 by 0.096 times the wavelength at the center frequency.

articleTitle: Parallel Solution for 3D Volume Integral Equation using PETSc Library
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: The Method of Moments (MoM) is a popular method for solving volume integral equations arising in electromagnetic scattering from a Three-Dimensional (3D) in-homogeneous body problem. The MoM results in dense matrice, which makes it difficult in the application to realistic and complex large scale problems due to the high solution time. The solution time limitation can be overcome by going for distributed system computation. In this work we use the open source package ‘PETSc’ library which stands for ‘Portable, Extensible Toolkit for Scientific Computation’. PETSc is a suite of data structures and (iterative) solvers based on MPI to solve the matrix/linear system in parallel. The Krylov subspace method, GMRES (Generalized minimum residual) iterative scheme is used to solve the linear system of equations. In this work we show the implementation of PETSc for dense and complex valued MoM matrices. The algorithm is shown to scale well.

articleTitle: Design, Analysis and Experimental Verification of 4-Element MIMO Antenna for 5G Sub:6 GHz N77/N78 and N79 band Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This work proposes a novel design of a 4-element MIMO antenna for 5G sub: 6GHz N77/N78 and N79 band applications. The proposed work is designed on a 100 × 100 mm<sup>2</sup>size FR4 defected substrate having a height of 1.6mm, constant of 4.4. Initially, a 30 × 30 mm<sup>2</sup>size single antenna is designed; later, it is extended to a 4-element antenna. Both the antennas work in the range of 3.0GHz to 5GHz and cover the 5G sub:6 GHz bands, which include N77 (3.3-4.2 GHz) and N78 (3.3-3.8 GHz) and N79 (4.4-5.0 GHz). The isolation values above 17.5 dB when elements are placed orthogonal and above 25 dB are attained in the structure's entire working region. High radiation efficiency and gain values are attained due to the systematic design. The proposed antenna is fabricated and checked with the measured results with simulation results. The compared results are almost in good agreement, and these results include S-parameters and diversity performance characteristics. The proposed antenna is designed with a popular and efficient simulator known as Ansoft HFSS.

articleTitle: A UWB MIMO Antenna using a Y-shaped Extended Ground Structure and Y-shaped Slot for Wideband Isolation
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: The paper proposes the numerical modeling and empirical investigation of a compact ultra-wideband diversity antenna within a small footprint of 42(L) mm × 61(W) mm for mobile wireless terminals. The antenna possesses an extensive bandwidth ranging between 3-14.75 GHz. The isolation over the entire operational bandwidth is well below −15 dB. To attain this wideband isolation improvement a modified Y-shaped extended ground stub is employed along with the incorporation of a Y-shaped slot on the shared ground structure. The feeding of the radiating monopoles is executed via a 50 Ω micro-strip feed along with a 6.5 mm long strip line for attaining adequate impedance matching. The antenna showcases acceptable diversity characteristics concerning envelope correlation coefficient (ECC) and diversity gain (DG) along with stable gain as well as omnidirectional patterns. The owing of desirable impedance, radiation, and diversity characteristics make the recommended radiator a prime contender for applications in UWB MIMO mobile terminals.

articleTitle: Compact Single-Balanced Mixer Using Microstrip Circular Patch Resonator
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Inthis paper, design of a compact single-balanced diode mixer utilizing a microstrip circular patch resonator at 2.4 GHz is presented. The novelty in the design is that the circular patch resonator behaves as a 180 degree hybrid as well as a filter to provide good LO to IF and LO to RF isolations thus makes the mixer configuration compact. The mixer works in down-conversion mode for low-IF operation and provides 6.7 dB conversion loss for +7 dBm local oscillator (LO) power and 330 MHz 3-dB radio frequency (RF) bandwidth. The LO to IF and LO to RF isolation are greater than 28 dB and 23 dB respectively. Design approach of the mixer is outlined in the paper with its simulated and measured results.

articleTitle: Microstrip Antenna as a Temperature Sensor for IoT Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Temperature sensing plays a vital role in applications like the medical industry, agriculture, automobile, home automation, textiles industry, and many more. Sensing accurate temperature and its maintenance at a particular value is another requirement of many applications. Temperature sensing can be done using various temperature sensors. This paper uses a microstrip antenna as a temperature sensor without human intervention. Change in the resonant frequency of the microstrip antenna is observed with variation in temperature. The sensed temperature variation is provided for processing through the IoT platform. Using arduino and GSM module extracted data can be sent to the cloud and can be used for data logging on the cloud. Using serial monitor of arduino IDE data has been observed. Thing-Speak cloud IoT analytics platform is used to combine, visualize and investigate live data streams.

articleTitle: Analysis of a Wideband Hybrid Metamaterial as an Absorber vis-a-vis a Polarizer
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Metamaterial structures are often used as microwave absorbers however, anisotropic structures are not suitable for the design of metamaterial absorbers. To verify this, a hybrid metamaterial absorber composed of a cross-loaded circular split ring resonator is analyzed in this article. It is noticed that the linearly polarized incident electromagnetic wave is proficiently converted into its orthogonal components because of the anisotropic geometry of the design. Under this scenario, the cross-polarized reflection coefficient is considered for the calculation of absorptivity, and a significant drop (from 90% to less than 30%) of the absorptivity is observed in the frequency band of interest. However, it can be used as an efficient broadband cross polarizer with a polarization conversion ratio (PCR) of more than 90%. The mechanism of cross-polarization, polarization efficiency with the variation of oblique incidence, polarization insensitivity, and optimization with respect to some parameters are also presented in this article. In addition, it is observed that the cross-polarization reflection coefficient value is high for anisotropic geometry, and both co- and cross-polarization reflection coefficients should be considered for the calculation of absorptivity.

articleTitle: A Wideband Six-Port Receiver With 40% Effective Bandwidth Using an Optimized 3dB Branch Line Hybrid Coupler
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents a new design of a wideband six-port network for the six-port receiver system. Considering, input matching, isolation, amplitude, and phase imbalances, it shows an effective bandwidth of more than 40%. The wideband operation is achieved using a new two-section branch-line hybrid coupler with excellent phase response. The design concept is validated by implementing a six-port network in a microstrip line technology, which covers the whole X-band. Measurement results show that the phase imbalance is within ± 7.5 degree, an amplitude imbalance of ± 1.5 dB and with reasonably good isolation and input matching over the whole band.

articleTitle: Analysis of Frequency Shift due to the Misalignment of Upper and Lower Plates of W-Band Planar Interaction Structure
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, the simulation of W-band planar interaction structure (Staggered Double Vane Interaction Structure) has been discussed to analyze the misalignment of upper and lower plates. This simulation has been carried out by HFSS. Driven Modal solution type has been used to study the S-parameters plots and the field patterns. The lateral shift of 10, 15 and, 20 microns along x and y-axis has been investigated. It has been demonstrated that the frequency shift is from −0.5 GHz to +0.4 GHz due to the misalignment of plates for 10 to 20 microns.

articleTitle: Signal Estimation and Measurement for the Reflectometry Diagnostic at IPR
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Refiectometry measures the beat frequency between radiated electromagnetic waves with a reference signal. We derive the relation between the phase change, path length and sweep rate and estimate the frequency of the beat signal. Data acquisition parameters are calculated based on the sampling frequency required for different sweep rates of the radiated waves. Synchronisation of the very short sweep time of ultra wide bandwidth of the reflectometer with the tokamak plasma pulse and its easy configuration is then discussed. To simplify and remotely operate reflectometer system an Ethernet based Lab View application software has been developed which is controlled by a single master TTL trigger. The complete system is tested in lab and also in the tokamak hall with the complete reflectometry system and is found to be working as designed.

articleTitle: A Hybrid UHF Passive Tag Antenna for RFID Applications at 865 MHz
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A planar UHF RFID tag antenna comprised of nested slot and T-match network is presented. A novel T-match network in Nested slot is introduced for better conjugate impedance matching between tag antenna and the semiconductor microchip is obtained. Moreover, by expansion the nested slot area and increasing the T-match branch length enhances the electrical length and increase the antenna inductance. Thus by utilizing the arm of matching network and feeder line, conjugate impedance is achieved in accordance with the semiconductor chip at 865 MHz. A surpassing UHF tag with volume 120mm x 60mm x 1.6mm (0.346λ×0.173λ×0.0046λ), with impressive power transmission coefficient of 99.9% has been flourishingly demonstrated and it is able to obtain detection range of 13.9 m. This tag antenna composition is simulated with respect to 4 W EIRP reader.

articleTitle: Switchable CSRR Sensor Array for Microwave Nondestructive Testing of Structures
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents a unique RF sensor geometry for characterizing dielectric materials and structures at various frequencies. In contrast to previous techniques, the proposed approach employs switchable complementary split ring resonator (CSRR) arrays, allowing for rapid imaging of a large sample. In this work, a <tex>$\mathbf{4}\times \mathbf{1}$</tex> array of CSRR sensors is designed and integrated with a 1 to 4 power divider at the input, and a 4 to 1 power combiner at the output. The sensor array is controlled by switches, and the entire measurement can be performed with a simple two-port arrangement, eliminating the need for mechanical movement. Using this one-dimensional sensor array, the dielectric characteristics of unknown structures are determined, thereby demonstrating its applicability.

articleTitle: RF Energy Harvesting Module Integrated Self Powered Multifunctional UWB Antenna
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This article proposes a reconfigurable UWB antenna which can automatically detect and block an ambient interfering signal using an RF energy harvesting powered frequency notching system. The design concept is demonstrated using a coplanar waveguide (CPW) fed circular printed monopole antenna as UWB radiator and a slot antenna is integrated in the ground plane of the CPW feed of the monopole antenna, for creating a compact energy harvesting system. Switching between UWB and frequency-notched UWB modes are actuated by closing/opening the gaps of Split Ring Resonators (SRR) using low power RF switches, powered by the RF energy harvesting module. The proposed slot antenna integrated circular monopole antenna is simulated for UWB and frequency notch characteristics. The rectifier, powered by the slot antenna, for energy harvesting is also studied. It is demonstrated by simulation that the proposed system activates/deactivates the RF switch, creating a frequency notch, when a high power interfering signal is detected and restores the UWB operation when interfering signal is weak.

articleTitle: Multifunctional Four-Port MIMO Antenna for Sub-6 GHz Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A switchable four port multiple input multiple output (MIMO) antenna has been presented in this paper for sub-6 GHz underlay cognitive radio applications. The proposed antenna is made on a coplanar waveguide (CPW) concept with a microstrip line feeding a semicircular patch element. Two narrow width slots are etched in the feed line, and one p-i-n diode is carefully placed across the pathway such that the overall geometry exhibits a switching response between an ultra-wideband (UWB) and a bandstop response. During the UWB state, the single antenna exhibits a wide impedance bandwidth (reflection coefficient <-10 dB) from 2.7 GHz to 6.30 GHz, thereby behaving as a sensing antenna. On the contrary, a bandstop response is obtained from 3.3 GHz to 4.3 GHz during the reverse bias of the diode. Afterward, a four-port MIMO antenna has been designed, where satisfactorily values are attained for various critical antenna parameters, such as isolation between antenna elements (<20 dB), envelope correlation coefficient (<0.5), and channel capacity loss (<0.5 bits/sec/Hz). Low profile, compact size, and ease of switching between the states make the proposed antenna geometry suitable for various wireless communications.

articleTitle: Wideband Polarization Reconfigurable Crossed Bowtie Dipole Antenna Based on Liquid Metal Switches
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, a wideband polarization recon-figurable dipole antenna based on liquid metal switches is proposed. The main parts of the antenna are two single-fed crossed bowtie dipoles with slots loaded on the arms of one dipole. Two sets of fixed-length liquid metal columns filled in polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) tubes are attached on top of the slots as switches. Because of the coupled connection between the liquid metal columns and the dipole arms, the slots can be shorted/opened by changing the position of the liquid metal columns, leading to alteration in phase differences between dipoles, and thus achieving polarization reconfiguration. The bowtie dipoles are used to obtain wide operating bandwidth, while the use of a cavity-backed reflector can make the antenna obtain directional radiation characteristics. The simulated results obtained by CST Microwave Studio® show that the impedance bandwidth of the antenna is from 1.01 GHz to 2.25 GHz and the axial ratio bandwidth is from 1.18 GHz to 1.36 GHz. Moreover, the peak gain can reach 8.78 dBi.

articleTitle: A Circularly Polarized Cylindrical Cavity backed Substrate Integrated Waveguide Antenna for Millimeter wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, a circularly polarized cylindrical cavity backed substrate integrated waveguide resonator for millimeter wave application is proposed. A feeding structure is designed and integrated on the same layer of circular cavity backed antenna. The feeding structure comprises of orthogonal feed, using substrate integrated waveguide technology. A circular ring slot is etched on the top plane of the cavity to radiate antenna in broadside direction. Two symmetrical rectangular slots are placed diagonally on the top metal plane of cavity and position of feed is optimized which improves the impedance matching. The dimensions of the proposed antenna with feeding structure is 3.55λ x 3.56λ x 0.19λ, where λ is the guided wavelength. The antenna achieves a peak gain of 5.85dBi, peak directivity of 6.23dBi, radiation efficiency of 94.1% and an axial ratio of 120MHz bandwidth below 3dB. The proposed antenna maintains a low profile and is compatible with planar structures. A comparative study of microstrip feeding and substrate integrated waveguide feeding is done and results are plotted in Ansys high frequency structure simulator. The performance of antenna is measured in terms of reflection coefficient, radiation pattern, front to back ratio, gain and directivity. The proposed antenna provides high gain, circular polarization and high front-to-back ratio at the high frequency thus, it is suitable for various millimeter wave applications.

articleTitle: Improving Simulation-Measurement Correlation for Compact Wi-Fi Laptop Antenna
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: The article proposes very compact flexible Wi-Fi 6E antenna (23 x 10 x 0.135 mm3), specifically designed for laptop systems. The S<inf>11</inf> of the proposed antenna within laptop environment is better than -6 dB and efficiency in the range of -3.5 dB. Various causes of mismatch between simulated and measured results have been identified, specifically for internal antennas. Also, a MATLAB tool is developed to find the correlation between simulated and measured results. The percentage correlation is improved from 30% to 88% (minimum) using the proposed mitigation techniques.

articleTitle: Compact, Wide-band, Dual linear Ku-band CATF feed for radiated mode characterization of multi-beam spacecraft
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A Compact, wide band, dual linear CATF feed with two corrugations in Ku-band (10–15 GHz) is designed for performing radiated mode payload characterization of multibeam spacecraft in Compact Antenna Test Facility (CATF). The design of Ortho-mode transducer (OMT) and radiating aperture which constitutes CATF feed is described. Simulated results are presented in this paper.

articleTitle: Does a Dielectric Resonator follow the Same Trend as in a Microstrip Patch in Interpreting the Sources of Cross-Polarized Radiation!
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: The work conjectured that the sources of cross-polarized radiation from a Dielectric Resonator Antenna (DRA) follow the same trends as in microstrip patches and verified the same through some extensive studies. A set of DGS geometries i.e. arc-shaped and resonating DGS (R-DGS) have been employed for the present investigation. While the arc-DGS can suppress XP fields only over the H-plane of the antenna, the R-DGS shows its impact on both H- and diagonal plane (D-plane). A coaxial fed cylindrical DRA is used for C-band operation. The optimized results are as follows: the arc-shaped DGS suppresses the XP level by 8 dB only over the H-plane of the DRA while R-DGS reduced the same by 8 dB over the H-plane and 17 dB over the diagonal planes. The near E and H fields on a surface close to the DRA of conventional ground, arc-shaped DGS, and R-DGS justify the conjecture.

articleTitle: Design and Simulation of Microstrip Based IDC Humidity Sensor
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This proposed research work presents designing and simulation of Inter-Digital Capacitor (IDC) and its coupling with micro strip line. Our purpose is to identify the presence of humidity in the environment. The humidity sensor model is capable of detecting relative humidity of a sample as per change in its permittivity. The principle of humidity sensor is based on frequency shift due to change in the permittivity. The operation frequency of the proposed system is in S band around 2.8 GHz, for the Relative Humidity (RH) variation of 20- 80% is analysed. The proposed sensor is found to have substantially higher sensitivity when compared with the models available in the literature. This system has been proposed for percentage of relative humidity classification. It exhibits frequency shift of 161.1 MHz for above RH range at ambient temperature. This model is cost effective and can operate without any sensitive material. It is easier to fabricate in comparison to various microwave techniques like N coupled Substrate Cavity Resonator and Substrate Integrated Waveguide (SIW) microwave planar sensors etc. It has an excellent sensing property that can be used in various applications like in food processing, electrical equipment and chemical gas purification.

articleTitle: An Efficient Lossy Media Implementation on the Improved WCS-FDTD Method
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents an efficient lossy media implementation on the improved weakly conditional stability finite-difference time-domain (WCS-FDTD) method. Here, four schemes such as averaging, forward-forward, forward-backward, and exponential time differencing schemes are used to implement lossy media. With the help of symmetrical source implementation and fundamental algorithm, the forward-backward scheme gives higher efficiency than the other three schemes. The efficiency of the proposed schemes is analyzed through numerical simulations and compared with the same, using the alternating-direction-implicit finite-difference time-domain (ADI-FDTD) method.

articleTitle: Design of Wideband Asymmetric Ortho-Mode Transducer WithTwist Based Symmetrical Co-Oriented Rectangular Waveguide Ports
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents a wideband orthomode transducer (OMT) with symmetrical rectangular waveguide ports.The designed OMT operates over frequency range of 10.7GHz-14.5GHz with standard rectangular waveguide ports for achieving orthogonal polarizations. The proposed OMT consists of multi section waveguide transformers, circular to rectangular waveguide transition and a 90 degree waveguide twist. Design approach with full wave EM simulations and experimental results are explained in detail. Experimental prototype shows a return loss of better than 18dB over the designed band, maximum insertion loss is 0.6dB for both ports and port isolation is better than 35dB. Experimental results are compared and discussed.

articleTitle: Pattern reconfigurable, perforated patch metasurface antenna for wide-angle phased array scanning
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper a pattern reconfigurable Metasurface antenna has been proposed for potential phased array applications, which works on three states with four diodes attached at four corners of the antenna. The beam is tilted to <tex>$\pm 30^{\circ}$</tex> when two diodes are in ON state and the other two are OFF. With this configuration bandwidth of 28 % and gain of 7.7 dBi is achieved at 7.5 GHz. The size of the antenna is <tex>$0.63\lambda\times 0.63\lambda$</tex>. By using <tex>$1\times 8$</tex> finite array setup, it is demonstrated that the proposed design can eliminate the occurrence of grating lobes and can achieve the beam scanning upto 70° in elevation plane.

articleTitle: Design and Development of ultra wideband Transceiver's functional blocks MMICs Using GaN Technology
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper discusses GaN based ultra-wideband high-power amplifier (HPA), low noise amplifier (LNA) with high input power survivability and RF single-pole double throw (SPDT) switch with low insertion loss along with high isolation and high-power handling. These functional blocks can be further used in development of transmit (TX) -receive (RX) module (TRM). Power amplifiers in ultra-wideband C-Ku band is designed to provide 10W of output power during transmission. A low noise amplifier with 30 dBm survivability and less than 3.0 dB noise figure over the complete band is designed for receiver side. Furthermore, an RF switch that is capable of withstanding 20 W RF power is developed for the selection of Tx/Rx path. Also, this paper discusses methodology to measure HPA, LNA and SPDT switch using CPW probe. The measurement of the circuits is done in pulse mode for HPA and in CW mode for LNA and SPDT switch. The measured results are in good agreement with the simulated results. Measurement results show that power amplifiers give power output of better than 10 W. Low noise amplifiers having 18 dB small signal gain with 3 dB noise figure. RF switch has 45 dB of isolation with 1 dB insertion loss.

articleTitle: RCS reduction of Microstrip Patch Antenna using Ku-band Perfect Polarization Convertor Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, we discuss the design and simulation of a Ku-band Perfect Polarization Convertor Metasurface (PCM) and its use in reducing the Radar Cross Section (RCS) of microstrip patch antenna while preserving its radiation characteristics. We first arranged the designed PCM in a chessboard configuration; the metasurface divided into four quadrants, each quadrant consisting of original PCM unit cell or its mirror image. Numerically simulated results show 10 dB monostatic RCS reduction in the frequency range 13.2-20.5 GHz for normally incident y-polarized EM wave. This metasurface is integrated with conventional microstrip patch antenna enabling 10 dB monostatic RCS reduction value over wide frequency band from 13 GHz to 21 GHz (out of operating band) for normally incident y-polarized EM wave as compared to antenna without metasurface while preserving all its radiation characteristics like radiation pattern, impedance bandwidth. In addition, nearly 15dB in-band RCS reduction value is achieved at 7.34 GHz as compared to reference antenna (antenna without PCM). Thus, both in-band and out-of-band RCS of microstrip patch antenna is reduced using proposed technique.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Cavity Wide-Band antenna
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: The paper focuses on the design of a wide-band pattern diversity antenna module for vehicular communication. A four-port pattern diversity antenna whose radiations maximize the coverage of the antenna azimuthal plane is presented. The individual antennas resonate at 5.8 GHz with 540 MHz impedance bandwidth. The proposed design also provides equal gains throughout the antenna coverage. The individual antennas produce a pattern diversity of 0, 90, 180, and 270 degrees and their gains vary from 6.8 dBi to 7.5 dBi. The pattern diversity antenna has a mutual coupling of less than 19 dB which is a reasonable value to reduce the interferences among the ports. The topology of the four-port antenna design also provides space in the middle of the structure for placing any external circuitry, thus saving some extra space. Both the single-element cavity antenna and four-port cavity antenna were fabricated and later tested. The proposed design can be used for vehicular network applications as it is able to sweep the azimuth plane using its four ports.

articleTitle: Design of Compact Power Divider for MMIC Applications Using Periodically Loaded Slow Wave Structure and MIM Capacitive Loading
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: <tex>$A$</tex> technique to further improve the compactness of a power divider that utilizes periodically stub-loaded slow wave structures is presented using shunt MIM capacitive loading. The circuit implementation challenges which include a trade-off between number of open stubs and the length of an open stub versus the distance between them is demonstrated. The improved power divider using MIM capacitive loading indicates an overall compactness of 73% compared to the conventional Wilkinson power and 65% compared to the power divider that utilizes only the stub-loaded slow wave structure at 32 GHz. The measured insertion loss is less than 0.67 dB. The power divider demonstrates the minimum measured magnitude and phase imbalance combination which is lower than 0.08 dB and 0.6 deg respectively compared to the state-of-the-art designs reported in the literature. The measured fractional bandwidth is 83%.

articleTitle: A Ku-Band Low Noise Amplifier Implemented in 0.15 µm Gallium Arsenide pHEMT Process
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A compact, low-power consumption Ku-band low noise amplifier implemented in WIN Semiconductor's 0.15 µm Gallium Arsenide process is presented in this paper. The amplifier achieves a measured average noise figure of 1.4 dB, at a nominal bias, across a broadband between 11 to 19 GHz. The amplifier consists of two stages with source inductive feedback in the first stage to achieve noise and input match simultaneously. It operates at 3 V drain voltage and 0.6 V gate voltage. The measured small signal gain of the amplifier is approx. 20 dB at midband and the 3-dB bandwidth is between 10 to 20 GHz, at a nominal bias. The amplifier has a positive gain slope of 2 dB between 10 to 16 GHz. The measured saturated output power is greater than 12.5 dBm at a nominal bias, between 11 to 18 GHz, with a maximum of 13.5 dBm at 18 GHz. The output PldB of the amplifier is higher than 11 dBm across the band. The size of the amplifier is 0.73 mm<sup>2</sup>only.

articleTitle: Analysis of Direction Finding Antenna System for Sonobuoy Positioning
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Location of a sonobuoy with respect to an airborne platform can be obtained by homing, which involves following a bearing (or azimuth course) directed towards it. A simulation study of bearing estimation of a sonobuoy from an airborne platform using 3 antenna configuration using phase interferometry has been done in this paper. Variation of phase shift in the incoming signals from sonobuoy received by the three antenna elements on airborne platform for different elevation, range, frequency and element spacing has been modelled.

articleTitle: Design of an Optically Transparent Wideband Absorber with 15 dB Absorption Bandwidth for C, X and Ku Band
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper demonstrates a simple design of an optically transparent polarisation insensitive wideband absorber for C, X, and Ku bands. An indium tin oxide (resistive film) coated on a polyethylene terephthalate (PET) sheet is utilized to design the proposed absorber. It provides a 15 dB absorption bandwidth from 4.8 to 20 GHz spanning over the C, X, and Ku bands. The proposed design remains unchanged up to 45° for TE polarisation and up to 30° for TM polarisation under oblique incidence. An equivalent circuit layout is modeled to better comprehend the working principle of the presented structure. Anechoic chamber measurements are performed after the prototype is fabricated. The simulated response matched well with the measured result.

articleTitle: Design of Substrate Integrated Waveguide-based Periodically-loaded Archimedean Spiral Slot Leaky Wave Antenna
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A novel structure of a periodic leaky-wave antenna with continuous beam scanning for Ku-band (12–18 GHz) applications is presented here. The design of a frequency-scanning antenna, which comprises of tapered microstrip line for feed and dual spiral slots as the radiator on the upper metallic plate of substrate integrated waveguide, is discussed. Leakage of electromagnetic energy from the leaky line (SIW) occurs through periodic loading of dual spiral slots. Antenna characteristics and performances are illustrated using full-wave simulation. The proposed LWA has features of a high gain of 13.4 dB (at broadside) with a maximum variation of 2 dB in the desired range of frequency. The designed antenna has 7 unit cells that provide directive comprehensive scanning of -60 deg. to +25 deg. over the operating frequency of 12.73-17.35 GHz with a consistent gain of 12 dB (avg.).

articleTitle: Design of Monopulse Comparator Network Using Gap Waveguide Technology at W-Band
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents a monopulse comparator network which is the key component in a monopulse antenna system used for mm wave tracking. It helps in generation of sum and difference patterns necessary for tracking a target. The network is designed based on novel gap waveguide technology. Initially, a magic-tee with 4 ports, is built at W-band with an operating frequency of 94GHz. Reflection coefficients at the ports are better than -10dB. The isolation between collinear and orthogonal ports is around -36.04dB and coupling is near -3dB. The amplitude imbalance is 0.17dB and phase imbalance is within 2 degrees. A monopulse comparator network is designed using 3 magic-tees and a power divider. The proposed low loss network has reflection coefficients better than -10dB at sum, E plane difference (elevation) and H plane (azimuth) ports. Isolation between the sum and difference ports is better than -30dB. The amplitude response of transmission coefficients is near -6dB and phase imbalance is within 2 degrees. The network is designed in three layers and can be manufactured using gap waveguide technology where there is no need to form electric contact.

articleTitle: Full-Wave Green's Function Analysis of a Coaxial Probe Coupled Two-Layer Hemispherical DRA with an Imperfect Concentric Conductor
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this work, full wave analysis of a coaxial probe coupled two-layer hemispherical dielectric resonator antenna (DRA) with an imperfect concentric conductor is investigated. Green's function method is used to analyze the proposed structure. Impedance boundary condition is applied on the interface of imperfect surface and dielectric region to derive the unknown constants. Electromagnetic boundary conditions are also applied on the dielectric-dielectric and dielectric-air interfaces to obtain the relevant unknown constants. The Method of Moment with sinusoidal basis and testing function is used to obtain the current distribution on the probe surface and thereafter the input impedance, reflection coefficient and radiation pattern are evaluated. The effect of imperfect surface, dielectric permittivity, sphere radius and probe length on the input impedance and reflection coefficient is also reported.

articleTitle: Doppler Navigation on Helicopter: Error Analysis
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Doppler radar navigators have been used by the military services of the USA, Great Britain, Canada and Australia since 1955. The first applications were in long range bombers and transport aircraft followed by use in fighters and Helicopters. The complete Doppler navigation system has two major components of error namely Doppler radar velocity error and the heading reference error. In this paper an attempt is made to discuss theory of error in Doppler navigation and correlate experimental flight test data with theoretical treatment. Experimental data gathered from Doppler system fitted on Helicopter is used to develop mathematical model for doppler navigation error. This model is validated using experimental flight test data.

articleTitle: Dual Circularly Polarized Quad Band Ring Shaped Monopole Antenna for Wireless Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A ring shaped multiband integrated wideband monopole antenna is presented. The antenna attains quad band along with dual circular polarization. Half-moon shaped slots are replicated in the radiator. Due to the placement of L- shaped slot, asymmetric effect is attained and circular polarization is achieved. The proposed ring-shape antenna occupies 1.51-1.67 GHz (0.16 GHz), 2.19-2.53 GHz (0.34 GHz), 4.79-6.60 GHz (1.81 GHz), 6.60- 9.92GHz (3.32 GHz) and 9.7-10.41GHz (0.71 GHz) in -10 dB impedance BW with 3-dB axial ratio BW of 2.19-2.26 GHz (0.07 GHz) and 9.73-9.93 GHz (0.20 GHz). The measured and simulated results are illustrated and verified. The proposed antenna covers present day wireless communication applications.

articleTitle: Design and Development of Transceiver Module for Spacecraft Intra Package Wireless Communication
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Spacecraft platforms are highly complex systems which involves interaction between various subsystems or packages that are all managed and supervised by a single entity. Cable Harness forms an important part of spacecraft which almost contributes to ten percent of the total dry weight. Not only harness contributes to the dry mass of satellite but also increases the complexity during assembly, integration and testing activities. A huge number of data measurements at various locations are required to be monitored which steadily adds on to the difficulty in spacecraft testing. Hence there is a need to replace this wired communication with wireless technologies used in market. Use of wireless technology and its existence has been available for commercial purposes, but they are yet to be explored in spacecraft. This paper mainly focuses on intra spacecraft wireless communication of data signals as a solution for minimizing the spacecraft harness thus reducing the integration effort, spacecraft dry mass and also the danger of damaging the mechanical interfaces during testing.

articleTitle: A low profile ferrite sleeve choke for localized power delivery during hyperthermia using coaxial wire antenna
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, a compact (0.24λ) customized ferrite sleeve choke with very low radial profile (thickness of 0.3 mm) is reported for intracavitary hyperthermia treatment at 915 MHz. The ferrite choke is used to design a dielectric loaded monopole antenna for delivering targeted power deposition at the cervix using an intracavitary applicator with 15<sup>○</sup>bend. Antenna surface current distribution, volume loss density, local specific absorption rate (SAR) in tissue, and applicator power reflection were used to assess the applicator performance. Applicator power coupling characteristics in tissue indicate a power reflection coefficient of -27 dB and 25% axial specific absorption rate coverage of 41 mm at 915 MHz. Thermal simulations indicate spherical heating volume at the distal end of the applicator confining the heating zone to the cervix.

articleTitle: Development of an Electrical Model of a Two-Layer Group Crossed Rectangular Spiral Inductor
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents the development of an electrical model and verification with measured results of a planar group crossed rectangular inductor. The model consists of the self-inductance, series resistance, substrate capacitance, adjacent metal capacitance, and underpass capacitance of the inductor. Closed-form expressions have been formulated from the equiva-lent electrical model of the group crossed rectangular inductor. The measured results show that the proposed inductor has the inductance of 50 nH, with a maximum quality factor of 70 at a frequency of 175 MHz. In addition, the proposed inductor achieves a self-resonance frequency of 510 MHz, inductance density of 11.11 (nH/mm) and figure-of-merit of 37.11. Close agreement between the analytically calculated inductance and measured inductance of the group crossed rectangular inductor is observed, which validates the proposed model.

articleTitle: A Spiral Ended Meandered RFID Tag at 915 MHz
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, a planar UHF RFID tag antenna comprised of spiral meandered line with double sided T-matching is presented. The presented novel compact spiral ended meandered tag having double sided T-match microstrip dipoles scale down the extent of tag antenna and provide improved conjugate impedance matching among tag antenna and semi-conductor microchip. This tag antenna operates at 915 MHz. A surpassing compact UHF tag with volume <tex>$\mathbf{59}\mathbf{mm}\times \mathbf{14}\mathbf{mm}\times \mathbf{1.6}\mathbf{mm} (\mathbf{0.18}\lambda\times \mathbf{0.043}\lambda\times \mathbf{0.0049}\lambda)$</tex>, with impressive power transmission coefficient of 99.9% has been flourishingly demonstrated and it is able to obtain detection range of 10.1 m. This tag antenna composition is simulated with respect to 4 W EIRP reader.

articleTitle: A Wideband Substrate Integrated Waveguide Bandpass Filter for 5G Millimeter Wave Transceiver
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) bandpass filter (BPF) for 5G millimeter wave (mmW) applications is proposed. First, a wideband grounded coplanar waveguide (GCPW)-to-SIW transition is designed for 22 GHz to 35 GHz. An SIW filter with eleven cavities arranged in a zigzag manner is designed to achieve the desired passband characteristics in the 5G mmWave band at 28 GHz and to reject harmonics caused during frequency up-conversion from baseband. The overall filter performance has been maximized by adjusting the dimensions of individual cavities, introducing openings at decoupling walls between cavities and chamfering cavity corners. Full-wave EM simulation with CST Microwave Studio is used for this optimization. The measured low side rejection and the insertion loss are comparable with the simulated results.

articleTitle: A Cornetto Shaped Super Wideband Antenna for Microwave and Millimeter Wave Communication
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A new co-planar waveguide (CPW) fed compact monopole antenna of size <tex>$\mathbf{51.6}\mathbf{mm}\times \mathbf{40.4}\mathbf{mm}\times \mathbf{0.8}\mathbf{mm}$</tex> is proposed in this article. The antenna patch is formed by taking intersection of triangular and circular patches which gives cornetto shape monopole. The antenna provides impedance bandwidth from 2 GHz to more than 60 GHz with maximum gain of 6.8 dBi and non-directional radiation patterns. The antenna also offers linear (piecewise) transfer function and flat group delay profile over the entire bandwidth. The proposed antenna is suitable for various microwave and millimeter wave communication applications including short range wireless communication, ad-hoc wireless systems, microwave imaging applications, 5G and beyond wireless technologies.

articleTitle: A Quad-band Graphene Printed Antenna Loaded with Graphene Metasurface for Application in Terahertz Gap
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents the performance analysis of a rectangular microstrip graphene-based printed antenna loaded with graphene metasurface between two dielectric substrates for efficient operation in the terahertz spectrum. The graphene patch with inset feed reports high return loss of 55.2 dB at 2.134 THz and noticeable fractional bandwidths of 23 %, 9.8 %, 6.9 %, and 4.6 % at the frequencies 1.762 THz, 2.134 THz, 2.462 THz and 2.782 THz respectively. With highest realized gain of 5.37 dBi at 2.782 THz, the proposed antenna may be suitable for spectroscopy, security scanning and numerous medical applications.

articleTitle: Dielectric Resonator Loaded U-shaped Printed Hybrid Antenna for Multiband Wireless Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents a new type of hybrid antenna geometry which can operate over triple bands. It consists of a U-shaped printed antenna and a cylindrical dielectric resonator antenna (CDRA) along with a ground plane which contains T-shaped slot. The proposed antenna operates over frequency ranges 5.75-6.56 GHz, 9.46 -12.7 GHz and 14.29-16.13 GHz and provides peak gain about 7.3 dBi. Different modes of CDRA like HEM<inf>11</inf><inf>δ</inf>, TM<inf>01δ</inf>-like, HEM<inf>12δ</inf> and HEM<inf>21δ</inf>are being excited. The proposed antenna can be used as an electromagnetic sensor for C, X and Ku band applications.

articleTitle: Compact Dual Band Antenna for Sub-6GHz Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper a coplanar waveguide (CPW) fed, compact planar antenna having the dimension of 35mm×30mm is developed and analyzed for the dual band applications. Symmetrical patch and ground plane are designed on a low cost FR4 epoxy substrate with the thickness of 0.8mm. Three slots of different dimensions are integrated on the triangular shaped patch to resonate the proposed antenna at required frequency bands. Antenna parameters like, reflection coefficient, gain, radiation efficiency and radiation pattern are analyzed for inspecting the antenna performance. For the simulation, CST microwave studio is used and simulated results shows impedance bandwidth of 810MHz (3.12-3.93GHz) and 410MHz (5.46-5.87GHz). Antenna shows omnidirectional radiation pattern in both resonating bands with gain variation between 2-3.5dBi and efficiency greater than 80%. All these characteristics ensures antenna's applicability in IEEE 802.16 WiMAX and IEEE 402.11n Wi-Fi (ISM) band.

articleTitle: A Wideband High Gain Cavity-Backed Slot Ring Antenna using Higher Order Modes
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: An improved design of a cavity-backed slot ring antenna is presented. The antenna maintains its radiation characteristics and good impedance matching over at least 10 % frequency band. Over the band, the antenna does not show any beam tilt. Two higher order resonant modes are used to obtain high gain. The improved antenna characteristics is obtained by elevating a part of the top cavity plate containing the ring slot. A prototype antenna is designed and fabricated for 2.25-2.5 GHz short-range indoor radar applications. The antenna provides a measured gain of <tex>$7\pm 0.5\text{dBi}$</tex> over the entire band. The overall dimension of the antenna is <tex>$0.64\lambda_{0}\times 0.64\lambda_{0} \times 0.08 \lambda_0, \lambda_0$</tex> being the free space wavelength at the mid-band frequency. Design guidelines are provided for the frequency scaling.

articleTitle: Compact Eight-Element MIMO Antenna for UWB Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A compact, low-profile eight-element UWB-MIMO antenna is presented in this investigation. The proposed eight-element MIMO antenna is configured by placing symmetrically orthogonally two identical same-oriented antenna elements on an octagonal-shaped substrate board, which are fed through the tapered microstrip line. A combination of ground stubs is utilized between a pair of antenna elements for better matching and low correlation simultaneously. The proposed MIMO antenna obtained a -10 dB impedance bandwidth <tex>$(S_{ij}\in i=j)$</tex> of 3.05-15.05 GHz (132.59<sup>%</sup>) and a minimum isolation value <tex>$\mathbf{(S_{ij}\in i\neq j)}$</tex> of 15 dB. The peak gain and total efficiency values are 7.3 dBi and 68.2-88.7%, respectively, in the respective ultra-wideband. Also, the value of ECC is less than 0.15. The performance of the proposed MIMO antenna is found satisfactory, which may be appropriate for UWB application-based user devices.

articleTitle: Design and Development of A Novel 6 dB Microstrip Directional Coupler Using Partial Overlay Structure at C-Band
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper describes the design and development of a 6 dB directional coupler designed using microstrip for use in radio front-end by using the technique of partial overlay structure. The overlay structure has been used partially to achieve tight coupling of 6 dB along with high directivity and isolation over a bandwidth of 600 MHz at C-Band. Overlay structure has been implemented for one of the coupled lines while keeping other as simple microstrip on top of it so as to have easy integration with the complete RF Front-end having surface mount configuration. In order to validate the design, hardware realization of directional coupler has been carried out and also has been tested. The measured directivity of coupler is higher than 22 dB.

articleTitle: Slotted Waveguide Leaky Wave Antenna at W Band for RADAR Application
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this article a W band slotted waveguide antenna with improved performance is introduced for radar imaging application. Presented antenna is designed for 92 GHz-98 GHz frequency band and almost constant gain above 18 dBi is achieved in the operating band. Slotted waveguide leaky wave antenna with improved performance is presented and for high precision wire EDM manufacturing process is used. Prototype of W band antenna is fabricated and performance of antenna is demonstrated by simulated and measured result. Side lobe level below -13.5 dB is achieved in both plane and half power beamwidth of 2.5°is realized. Beam scanning rate of presented leaky wave antenna is 1° /GHz.

articleTitle: Submillimeter-Wave Phased Array for Titan Atmospheric Sounding Instrument
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Titan, the largest moon of Saturn, is an organically reach world with Earth-like geological conditions such as thick nitrogen atmosphere and stable liquid on its surface. Unique to Titan is the surface-atmosphere interactions which transfer the complex organic molecules formed up in the atmosphere to the surface. These organic materials are then moved and shaped by wind and rain into dunes, lakes and seas. Understanding of this complex surface-atmosphere relation is the need of the hour as it will facilitate future missions to this unique world. In this work, we present a submillimeter-wave limb sounder instrument concept that can directly measure the vertical profiles of temperature, winds, and trace gases in Titan's atmosphere which will help to improve our understanding of the complex atmospheric circulations on Titan as well as on other slow rotating planetary bodies. Here we present a demonstration of submillimeter-wave phased array antenna system for electronic beam steering that will enable significant reduction on size-weight-and-power requirements of the potential future missions.

articleTitle: AQuad-Band Monopole Antenna using Metamaterial Inspired SRRs for Mobile Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A compact-sized quad-band monopole antenna for 5G, Radiolocation, and WLAN services is presented in this paper. The proposed antenna employs a metamaterial-inspired elliptical split ring on the top surface of the FR4 substrate to form a monopole antenna and an SRR unit cell on the partial ground plane. The SRR unit cell on the ground plane is a combination of the pentagonal and the circular SRR. The four operating frequency bands resulting from the proposed design are 2.3-2.4 GHz (n40- 5G NR/WCS), 2.8-3.2 GHz (radio location services), 5.7-5.85 GHz (WLAN), and 6.4-6.87 GHz(Wi-Fi 6E) respectively. The peak gain values at 2.35 GHz, 2.9GHz, 5.75 GHz, and 6.6 GHz are found to be 0.55 dBi, 2.02 dBi, 2.60 dBi, and 3.21 dBi respectively. The proposed antenna offers an advantage of the small size of 0.17 λ<inf>0</inf>×0.23 λ<inf>0</inf> (λ<inf>0</inf>being the free space wavelength at 2.3 GHz).

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Design of Stealth Unmanned Combat Aerial Vehicle in Hostile Environment
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Low observable techniques for stealth applications have become the need of the hour. RCS analysis for airborne platforms in military bands is the stringent requirement. Techniques such as shaping of aircrafts and use of absorbers suppresses radar echoes. This paper discusses about the use of special absorber techniques such as multi-layered Radar Absorbing Techniques with and without FSS to cater the reduction of echoes in the X-Band. The RCS analysis with and without absorber for Unmanned Combat Aerial Vehicle has been compared and analysed. The target tracking for the UCAV has also been covered in hostile environment condition using Altair Feko.

articleTitle: A Comparative Study of Two Different Octagonal Structure-Based Split Ring Resonators
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Radio Frequency Identification (RFID) Tags market has led to a rise in various sectors and applications due to significant advantages over other wireless communication technologies. Due to the edge of not requiring line-of-sight communication, RFID has acquired the barcode technology market. With RFID, the process of automatic tagging and advanced tracking have been much easier. This paper presents the results of a split ring resonator with split length in different patterns with the octagonal ring structure. The tags in the study can be used for ultra-wideband (UWB) applications with a frequency range of 3–11 GHz. Two different split rings were compared to analyze the encoding (number of bits) and the RCS of the tag. The encoding capacity is found to be increased from 3-bits to 5-bits with the change in the split pattern.

articleTitle: Self-referenced Terahertz Optical Sensor with Dirac Semi-metal and Topological Photonic Crystal
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In recent years, the research on tunable terahertz devices has drawn significant attention. This article presents a novel optical sensor consisting of bulk Dirac semi-metal and topological photonic crystals. The numerical simulation results reveal that the Tamm plasmon state and topological edge state cause multi-mode absorption. It is found that one of the modes remains unaffected while other modes experience significant change by altering the analyte refractive index. Taking advantage of this, a self-referenced refractive index sensor with a sensitivity of 0.365 THz/RIU and FOM, 717 RIU-<sup>1</sup> is proposed. The tunability of the device with Fermi energy and the thickness of Dirac semi-metal has also been established.

articleTitle: Digitally Coded Single/Twin- Beamforming Metasurface Lens Antenna for Millimeter-Wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A low-profile single / twin- beamforming digital metasurface lens (DMSL) antenna is proposed for millimeter-wave applications. The complete antenna prototype comprises of 1-bit coded transmission-type DMSL and a slot-coupled microstrip patch antenna (MPA) as feed source placed at a focal distance of 20 mm beneath the DMSL. The proposed DMSL comprises of slotted meta-atoms arranged in an array. The adopted meta-atom is highly insensitive to wave polarization and oblique angle of incidence of upto 60°. To achieve focused beam in the broadside direction antenna configuration with DMSL-1 is adopted which is constructed using an array of 25 × 25 meta-atoms. The maximum gain of 19.5 dBi is achieved for DMSL-1 antenna configuration in the broadside direction showing a gain enhancement of 13.4 dB. Further, the antenna with DMSL-2 is designed to split and focus the beams simultaneously in ±30° direction resulting in two equal beams each having a gain of 16.6 dBi and a gain enhancement of 10.5 dB. The f/D ratio for both antenna configurations is 0.2 resulting in a compact antenna.

articleTitle: A Comparative Analysis of Dielectric Lenses for Wide Scanning Performance
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: One of the most challenging aspects of low-profile antenna systems is achieving low scan loss for both azimuth and elevation without compromising the other antenna parameters. A phased array can be used as the feed and the dielectric lens geometry can be reformed for wide scanning capability in addition to gain enhancement. In this paper, four different types of dielectric lenses are considered over the designed antenna array in X-band to improve scan performance along with gain. The Dielectric lens structures in various configurations and placements have been considered. The inner layer of the dielectric lens completely encases the antenna array. For the Single Solid lens structure, the gain increment of 3.6dB and scan performance of ±10 degrees is observed. For Multi-layered dielectric lens structure, scan performance of ±30 degrees and gain improvement of 1.73dB is observed.

articleTitle: Design of Miniaturized Four-way Power Divider with Predefined Sequential Phase Difference for Antenna Feed Network
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: The manuscript presents a miniaturized four-way power divider with a sequential phase difference of 90°. The proposed power divider is designed using one rat-race coupler (RRC) and two branch-line couplers (BLC). For the minia-turization three open stub conversion of a single transmission line technique with meandering has been used. A Four-way power divider for the frequency of 145.825 MHz is designed and fabricated to discuss the proposed concept. The measured result shows a low insertion loss of 6.7 to 6.8 dB at each output ports. Also, the return loss for each port is better than 20 dB. Isolation between different output ports are better than 30 dB. The measured phase imbalance at each port is not more than 3°. The fabricated circuit size is <tex>$0.265 \lambda_g \times 0.275 \lambda_g$</tex>.

articleTitle: Enhancing Load Range of Concurrent Dual-band Real to Real Matching Network Using Load Shifters
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents enhancement of the load range of dual band real to real matching networks for a given frequency ratio through load shifters. The proposed structure is a simple L-section and has versatility to serve any impedance environment ranging from almost a short circuit to nearly an open circuit for any frequency ratio. In this paper, the cascaded stepped impedance structure proposed by Monzon is analyzed in details using Smith chart, and its limitations regarding the load range with increase in frequency ratio have been studied. The proposed load shifter has been successfully applied to Monzon's structure at larger frequency ratios for both small and large loads. The simulated and the measured results are in a good accordance. This structure can also be used with any other regular matching network capable of matching limited range of load.

articleTitle: Design of Guard Antenna for Radar Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper proposes the design of a wideband and relatively wide beam Guard antenna for radar applications. The antenna has been designed around the concept of a Linear Resonant Slotted Waveguide Antenna. The antenna is required to work in the X band, covering a bandwidth of 500 MHz. The design and simulation have been done on HFSS. The return loss is less than 10 dB and the gain of the guard antenna is better than 14.6 dBi over the 500MHz band.

articleTitle: Wide Band and High Gain Hollow Cylindrical Dielectric Resonator Antenna Design using Aluminum Cavity for Ku Band Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A compact wideband high gain co-axial probe fed hollow cylindrical dielectric resonator antenna using Aluminum cavity is proposed in this paper for Ku band applications. A proposed hollow CDRA is placed on FR4 substrate along with ground plane, which is surrounded by aluminum conical cavity. This configuration enhances the impedance band width of 48.5% and co-polarized peak gain of 15.03dBi from 6.5 dBi of conventional CDRA. The conical cavity also helps to convert broadside radiations of CDRA into highly directional radiations. The proposed HCDRA is compared with the existing bandwidth and gain enhancement techniques in the literature shown in the Table 1. From the comparison it is found that the proposed HCDRA configuration is compact, having high gain and bandwidth.

articleTitle: Two Element Polarization Diverse MIMO Antenna with Modifed Ground Structure
