publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A two-element multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO)antenna of size 36 <tex>$\times 46.1$</tex> mm with polarization diversity for sub 6GHz application is proposed in this paper. The single antenna operating at 3.5 G Hz frequency consists of a triangular patch antenna. A modified fractal structure is employed in the ground to produce circular polarization.An impedance bandwidth of 9.5% is obtained from 3.39 GHz to 3.73 GHz, while the 3-dB axial ratio bandwidth of 1.1% is from 3.48 GHz to 3.52 GHz. The antenna exhibits a tilted directional radiation pattern with 3.49 dBi gain and 75% efficiency. Two element MIMO antenna with a circular polarization diversity arrangement is designed with a distance of approximately 1.35 mm. The isolation obtained between two antennas is more than 14 dB. Envelope Correlation Coefficient (ECC) is well below 0.005 with a Diversity Gain value close to 10dB. The antenna has application in a 5G sub 6 GHz band and wireless communication.

articleTitle: Frequency and Polarization Reconfigurable Slotted Microstrip Antenna
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, a PIN diode radio frequency (RF) switch integrated frequency and polarization reconfigurable antenna is reported. Three pin diodes are used to change the current path length and to modify the surface current distributions, resulting in frequency as well as polarization diversity. When all switches are in the ON state (mode-1), the antenna operates in 2.42 GHz band with linear polarization and when the switches are OFF (mode-2), the antenna resonates at 2.13 GHz with circular polarization. The desired results are obtained using a surface modification of the patch which is achieved by rigorous optimization in Ansys Electromagnetic Suite. In the mode-1, the antenna has an axial ratio of above 10.68 dB, which indicates linear polarization and, in the mode-2, the antenna has an axial ratio of 0.78 dB which ensures circular polarization. To validate the simulated results, the prototype of the antenna is fabricated and measured results are compared.

articleTitle: Multi-Bit Passive RFID Tag Design using Concentric Rectangular Strip Resonators for 2.4 GHz and 5.8 GHz ISM Band
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents chipless radio frequency identification (RFID) tags based on concentric rectangular strip resonators (CRSRs). The 6-bit compact CRSR-based tag with a physical size of 39 mm × 20 mm resonates at 2.4 GHz and 5.8 GHz industrial scientific medical (ISM) bands, hence suitable for biomedical scenarios. The resonant peaks of this 6-bit tag make it well-suited for on-body applications. The resonant structure is implemented on a low-cost FR4 substrate material of dielectric constant and loss tangent values of 4.4 and 0.02, respectively. In addition, an approach has been discussed using Kalman filtering, one of the noise reduction algorithms for the efficient detection of radar cross section (RCS).

articleTitle: A Planar Log Periodic Dipole Array Antenna for IEMI Detection
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, we design an optimal antenna in the frequency band of 0.5 GHz to 2 GHz for Intentional Electro-magnetic Interference (IEMI) detection application. We design the Conventional Planar Log-Periodic Dipole Array (CPLPDA) antenna, and a compact Planar Log-Periodic Meander Dipole Array (PLPMDA) antenna using a Ring Resonator (RR) to achieve miniaturization in size. The gain improvement at low frequency is done by introducing the rectangular shape balun, meander shape dipole, and ring resonator. We design the CPLPDA antenna and PLPMDA antenna to obtain their performance through simulations using Ansys High-Frequency Structure Simulator (HFSS) 2019 R3.7 electromagnetic simulation software. Using simulations, we show that the PLPMDA antenna achieves an average gain of 4.3 dB. Also, compared to the CPLPDA antenna, the PLPMDA antenna achieves a 26.08% reduction in antenna width and provides better performance across the desired frequency band. The proposed PLPMDA antenna takes care of the safety of electronic systems from IEMI attacks.

Author Keywords: conventional planar log periodic dipole array antenna (CPLPDA)
planar log periodic meander dipole array antenna (PLPMDA)

articleTitle: Dual Transmissive Frequency Selective Rasorber Designed Using Minkowski Fractal Shaped Resonator
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, a novel design strategy for realizing a polarization-independent and compact absorption-transmission-absorption-transmission type frequency selective rasorber (FSR) is presented. A resonator with cross-loop slot in the Minkowski fractal (MF) design is studied and incorporated within the top resistive layer of the square loop broadband absorber. The proposed MF resonator incorporated within the resistive layer is capable of realizing a dual transmission pole inside the broad absorption band. A cross slot based bandpass layer is replaced with the ground layer of absorber as such the desired transmission bands are achieved, while acting as ground plane outside the passbands. The proposed FSR design realizes two transmission windows at 10.4 and 15.2 GHz with the adjacent absorption bands from 5.2 to 10.1 GHz and 10.7 to 14.4 GHz. Measurements carried on the fabricated 15 x 15 array prototype experimentally validates the design. The proposed rasorber is a suitable contender for shielding and radar cross section reduction of the dual-band radiating systems.

articleTitle: Loop Rectenna Unit for Far Field Wireless Power Transfer Application
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This article describes a 2.4 GHz two-port Loop Rectenna Unit (LRU) designed for a distant field wireless power transmission application. Two diodes are used in the configuration with intrinsic combiner characteristics to rectify the signal. Simulations in the full wave EM solver of ANSYS HFSS and Keysight ADS are used to analyse the performance of the suggested structure. When excited, the proposed LRU provides a total gain of 4 dBi and a peak rectification efficiency of 64%. At 2.4 GHz, source power levels between -6.8 dBm and 11.6 dBm exhibit above 40

articleTitle: A Patch Rectenna Fed with L-probe to Harvest Solar and RF Energy
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, a hybrid energy harvester consisting of a solar panel and a broadband loop rectenna is designed as a part of power management unit for IoT devices. The harvester comprises of a solar panel mounted on top of circular patch fed with an L-probe rectenna for RF energy harvesting. The rectenna achieves a monopole like radiation pattern in azimuth plane. The measured results demonstrate that at 630 μ W/cm2 power density for 858 MHz to 1.175 GHz, a DC output voltage of 0.647 V has been produced via a 10 KΩ resistor. The presented energy harvester is useful in mountainous or elevated areas where the majority of cellular towers are located at the same altitude as the sensor node of IoT device.

articleTitle: Low Actuation Voltage DMTL Phase Shifter with Improved Reliability
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A distributed MEMS transmission line (DMTL) phase shifter is designed using a novel tri-layer sandwich (Insulator-Metal-Insulator) membrane based shunt switch which results a reliable phase shifter and operates at a lower actuation voltage of nearly 16 V. Using combination of Bulk-micromachining as well as Surface-micromachining techniques, this phase shifter is fabricated on a high resistivity silicon substrate <tex>$(\boldsymbol{p}=10,000\boldsymbol{\Omega}.\mathbf{c}\mathbf{m},\ \boldsymbol{\varepsilon}_{\mathbf{r}}=11.7$</tex>, h=675 µm) and achieves a true-time delay operation from DC to 18 GHz. Measurements show a close match to the designed phase shifter with less than 1.7 dB of insertion loss (I.L.) and better than 14 dB return loss (R.L.) from DC to 18 GHz with an overall phase shift of 50.82 degree. This phase shifter can have wide applications in high-performance microwave and millimeter-wave integrated circuits in telecommunication, defense and space based phased array system, mobile satellite broadcasting communication etc.

articleTitle: Lumped element-based P-band In-Quadrature phase Mixer
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This work describes a lumped element based compact In and Quadrature phase (IQ) Mixer designed and realized at 450±25 MHz. This mixer is designed on wideband modulation approach using single balanced topology and transmission line section is designed using equivalent “pi” lumped-element network for miniaturization. The realized mixer exhibits worst case conversion loss 10 dB, LO isolation better than 30 dB and rejection of better than 35 dBc for 3rd order (1,2) intermodulation product over 11% of fractional bandwidth. The realized performance is better with respect to spurious suppression, LO power requirement, I/Q bandwidth, Isolation, amplitude imbalance and phase imbalance against the procured one. The reported IQ mixer is fabrication friendly and a cost-effective indigenous space component.

articleTitle: Implementation of Wideband Filter and High Gain Antenna Using Novel Uniplanar Electromagnetic Bandgap Structure for X-Band Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This article implements the high gain superstrate antenna and wideband bandpass microwave filter using a novel uniplanar compact Electromagnetic Bandgap (EBG) structure. The proposed EBG unitcell consists of an outer inductive grid connected to four square loops at corners separated by a center-spitted Jerusalem cross resembled dipole. The design is printed on top of a 0.8 thin Rogers RT Duroid 5880 grounded dielectric substrate. Wide bandgap behavior is observed in the intended EBG from 9.6 GHz to 12 GHz (22.22% FBW). Here, the two different applications of the proposed EBG are presented, which gain the main focus of this work, i.e., EBG loaded microstrip filter and an EBG superstrate for a microstrip patch antenna (MPA) gain enhancement. The unitcell performance is stable for different oblique incidences under Transverse Electric (TE) and Transverse Magnetic (TM) modes. Compared to the reference antenna, the EBG-loaded patch exhibits a gain improvement, and 10.95 dBi is achieved along with bandwidth improvement. The C-band is the intended operating range of a proposed EBG-based wideband filter having less than 1.05 dB Insertion Loss (IL) over the operational range 5.26-13.32 GHz or 86.86%, and its passband BW covers from 5.30 - 13.71 GHz (88.48%).

articleTitle: Transparent and Flexible Single-layer Metasurface with Specially Chosen Unit Cell for Multi-band Operation in X-K Band
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Optically transparent, flexible, single layer, light weight, and conformal frequency selective surface with periodic arrangement of circular ring and flower shaped unit cells is designed and investigated. The structures are analyzed in the frequency range of 1 to 25 GHz covering the broad range of electromagnetic spectrum from C to K band. The periodic arrangement of circular ring structure provides stop-bandwidth of 12.34 GHz spanning over 7.58 GHz to 19.92 GHz. The second design containing the periodic arrangement of flower shaped unit cells enhances the stop- bandwidth to 14.00 GHz. In addition, narrow pass-band and stop- band selectivity is achieved in the frequency range of 21 to 25 GHz. Our designs for the flexible frequency selective surface thus offer options to use them as stop-band filter and pass-band filter at different frequencies in X, Ku and K bands. The simulated and experimental results show good concurrence with each other.

articleTitle: Investigations on Crosstalk reduction in high frequency Circuits using commercial foam
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Rapid developments in the field of high frequency circuits have led to more aggressive approach in enhancing quality of transmission for signal and power across the system for better performance. Crosstalk remains one of major challenges specially in miniaturized and flexible circuits. Foam provides a low-cost solution for the reduction of the crosstalk. This paper presents a performance comparison of the crosstalk reduction based on simulation and experimental investigations using different types of foam layers to tackle the problem of crosstalk by enhancing the signal and power integrity.

Author Keywords: Near end and far end crosstalk

articleTitle: Wide band active Up-Converter MMIC with over 40 dB Isolation in Overlapping RF/IF bands
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A wideband up-converting active mixer with better than 40 dB isolation between all ports is demonstrated in this work. The mixer architecture is based on differential active LO and RF balun feeding a diode quad, while the IF input is a passive in-phase power combiner. A highly linear on chip active balun is designed to handle distortion-less LO power upto 14 dBm. The design is based on 0.13µm pHEMT process of GAETEC foundry. The proposed mixer exhibits a very high RF-IF isolation of 40 dB over overlapping RF (1-3.5 GHz) and IF (0.1-2.6 GHz) band. The mixer has a conversion Gain of -11 dB, return losses> 10 dB, port isolations> 40 dB and harmonic suppressions better than 40 dBc. The measured P1 dB input is 11 dBm and IIP3 is 17 dBm making it attractive for wideband receivers for EW applications. The chip size is 3mm X 2mm.

articleTitle: Synthesis of highly directive broadside arrays using nested Chebyshev polynomials
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents the synthesis of highly directive broadside array using nested Chebyshev polynomials. It is known that, the best possible directivity is achieved by uniform excitation coefficients. It is also known that by reducing the inter-element spacing d to less than <tex>$\frac{\lambda}{2}$</tex> invisible regions are created in the radiation characteristics. Improved radiation characteristics can be theoretically achieved by increasing the radiation intensity in the invisible regions. Nested Chebyshev polynomials have been used to achieve this condition. Simulations showed a significant improvement in the half power beamwidth, without any degradation in the side lobes for <tex>$\mathbf{d}=\frac{\lambda}{4}$</tex>.

articleTitle: Independent Control Over the Passband of Bandpass Filter Based on Semi-Circular Mushroom Loaded Substrate Integrated Waveguide
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents a method to control the passband of a bandpass filter by independently varying the bandwidth (BW) and center frequency (CF) of the bandpass filter which is based on a circular substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) loaded with two cascaded semi-circular mushroom resonators (ScMRs). The dimensions of two mushroom vias are varied within a range of 0.6 mm to affect the resonance frequency of the cascaded mushroom resonators and consequently shift the center frequency of the passband by more than 6.5% keeping the passband bandwidth undisturbed. The internal capacitive coupling between the two cascaded ScMRs across the slot gap is varied by changing the slot width by 0.3 mm, which consequently establishes a control over the passband bandwidth and changes the 3dB fractional bandwidth independently by more than 6.6%. A simulative study shows that the proposed filter occupying a compact area of 0.3 λ<inf>0</inf>× 0.3 λ<inf>0</inf>has the passband centered at 2.3 GHz with a minimum insertion loss of 0.7 dB.

articleTitle: A Low-Complexity Decoupling and Matching Technique Using a Third-Order LC Network
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A novel decoupling technique to enhance the isolation between two antennas is proposed. This provides a compact and distributed solution to the problem of isolation enhancement in any two closely spaced antennas. Closed-form design formulas for the LC decoupling network are derived. The proposed technique is applied to decouple three types of antennas and it is shown that the LC network provides good isolation while preserving the input matching characteristics.

articleTitle: Transmission characteristics of Plasma-based microwave absorbing panel in Near and Far field region of testing antenna
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Microwave absorbers come in variety of types depending upon their operational frequency regime, environment of application, type of operation and several other physical parameters. Plasma-based microwave absorbers are of importance because of its adaptive nature. This paper is an attempt to study the Transmission characteristics of two types of Plasma-based microwave absorbing panels in the X- band viz. 8–12 GHz. A plasma panel is formed by series of fluorescent tubes enclosed in two different shapes of Teflon enclosures. A free space Transmission tunnel method is adopted to study the transmission properties of both plasma panels. The experiment has been carried out in an anechoic chamber using standard gain horn antennas. The panels are tested in the near and far field of the test antenna and the results are discussed. The difference in the transmitted microwave power with and without plasma gives the information about the absorption of the power. An average of 60% of microwave power is absorbed when the plasma is turned on. This makes the panel an attractive solution for using it as an active microwave absorber.

articleTitle: A Compact and Flexible Dipole Antenna to be Integrated into Military Berets
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A compact dipole antenna designed to be integrated into a soldier's beret is discussed in this paper. The antenna is designed to be operated at the UHF RFID frequency of 866 MHz. Performance in terms of reflection coefficient and realized gain of the compact dipole antenna is reported. Later, an AMC structure is designed on the same flexible fabric to block the downward radiation and the performance of this structure in terms of the reflection phase is reported. The proposed solution is a flexible antenna; it can easily be integrated into a soldier's beret for tracking purposes.

articleTitle: Pentagon-shaped Microstrip Patch Antenna in ISM band for Hyperthermia Application
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, a pentagon-shaped microstrip patch antenna was proposed for the Hyperthermia application. The proposed antenna operates in the ISM band of 434 MHz with a size of 120mm x 120mm x 1.6mm. FEM-based HFSS software has been used for simulation and using FR-4 substrate with relative permittivity of 4.4 and thickness of 1.6 mm. The proposed antenna structure is considered in a combined single-layer human tissue model phantom. The specific absorption rate (SAR) is achieved along the x-axis variation inside the phantoms at different distances from the antenna.

articleTitle: A Closed-Form Electrical Model of Skin and Proximity Effects for Circular Microstrip Inductors
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper develops a closed-form electrical model of skin and proximity effects using a three-ladder circuit and verifies it with measured results for a circular microstrip inductor. The complete equivalent electrical model of the inductor consists of the three-ladder circuit using RL elements, substrate capacitance, and adjacent metal capacitance of the inductor. Closed-form expressions are formulated for self-inductance, substrate capacitance and adjacent metal capacitance from the equivalent electrical model of the inductor. All the model parameters of the ladder circuit are accurately derived and calculated using layout and process parameters. Four planar circular spiral inductors are fabricated on FR4 substrate to verify the proposed models. The measured results, EM simulated, and analytically calculated results of the modelled three-ladder circuit are in close agreement with each other.

articleTitle: Design and Simulation of RF Front End Receiver Mixer for 5G NR Application
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: The need for new technologies to handle peak high speed data rates for the aforementioned communication benefits has unquestionably grown exponentially over the last few years. In this paper, a receiver RF front end mixer design operating for 5G NR application. The BJT transistor with part number BFP405F is selected for the down conversion mixer design. Transistor is biased and check for the stability at the given frequency. Matching circuit is designed for the transistor to obtain the better conversion gain and return loss. The input RF and LO frequencies are 3.5 GHz and 3.3 GHz, respectively, with input power -10 dbm at LO path. The output frequency obtained at the IF is 200 MHz. The designed active down conversion mixer is simulated in ADS. The desired mixer has good linearity, a modest conversion gain, and good return loss. Conversion gain for the designed down conversion mixer is +5.03 dB.

articleTitle: Design and PIC simulation Studies of Cluster Cavity W-Band Gyro-twystron
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A W-band gyro-twystron operating in fundamental TE<inf>01</inf>using clustered cavity has been designed and studied for its performance improvement. The designed amplifier has been modeled in 3D PIC code “CST particle-in-cell code”. The simulation of the present gyro-twystron predicted an RF output power ~78 kW at 94 GHz for the gyrating beam of 65 kV and 6 A with 4% velocity spread. The half power bandwidth has been calculated as ~ 2.6 GHz, which is approximately 1.5 times more than that of a conventional design. The saturated gain and conversion efficiency of the amplifier have been calculated as ~36 dB and ~20 %, respectively.

articleTitle: Millimeter Wave SIW Fed Linearly Tapered Slot Filtenna for 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A Substrate Integrated Waveguide (SIW) Fed linearly tapered slot Filtenna for millimeter-wave 5G applications is demonstrated in this paper. It functions fundamentally as an antipodal linearly tapered slot antenna (ALTSF) provided by a SIW feed. This study also describes the design and analysis of the SIW to Microstrip transition for mm-wave applications. The ALTSFA's recommended design has been simulated using MATLAB Antenna Toolbox software. The proposed design has a maximum gain of 10.32 dBi and a bandwidth of 23.8 GHz to 45.2GHz. The same was fabricated and the simulated and measured results are found to be in good agreement. For 5G applications, this Filtenna might be a serious competitor.

articleTitle: Design of 70W GaN Based Power Efficient Amplifier for Software Defined Radio Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, high power amplifier is designed and developed in 225 MHz to 400 MHz for software defined radio communication. A GaN based high electron mobility transistor is used in printed circuit technology to analyze the structure. A detail design procedure is described including input, output matching and load pull analysis for optimum output power of the transistor. A prototypes is fabricated to validate the proposed design. The measured small signal input return loss is better than 13.2 dB and gain 22.95 dB with a gain variation of ±0.95 dB over the band. Similarly, the measured efficiency is better than 60% over the output power of 48.5 dBm. The proposed design achieves EVM performances of less than 3.5% for QPSK modulation having a symbol rate of 250 kS/sec at an average output power of 47.0 dBm over the entire bandwidth. Also, the adjacent channel power ratio is better than −50 dBc across the frequency band.

articleTitle: CSRR and Stub Loaded Miniaturised Tri-band Patch Antenna for 5G Base Station Application
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, a complementary split ring resonator (CSRR) and stub-loaded miniaturized tri-band microstrip patch antenna is proposed for sub-6 GHz 5G base-station application. First, a CSRR loading is used on a square microstrip patch antenna to achieve dual-band response and antenna miniaturization simultaneously. Next, the tri-band response is achieved by adding two differently sized stubs. The proposed tri-band antenna works at 3.59 GHz, 3.85 GHz and 4.44 GHz, sub-6 GHz operating frequencies having peak gains of 4.8 dBi, 5.5 dBi and 6.7 dBi respectively. In order to reduce the cross-polarization levels at the operating frequencies, a rectangular slot is etched from the ground plane. The proposed antenna exhibits co-polarization to the cross-polarization separation of 20 dB, 11 dB and 17 dB at 3.59 GHz, 3.85 GHz and 4.44 GHz respectively. A prototype of the antenna is fabricated and measured results are compared with the simulated ones.

articleTitle: Near-Field Inductive Wireless Power Transfer at ISM Bands for Biomedical Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: The paper demonstrates a novel setup for near-field inductive wireless power transfer (WPT) working at two ISM (industrial, scientific and medical) bands (868-868.6 MHz and 902–928 MHz). The designed WPT setup consists of modified loop antennas at the transmitting and receiving front-end, a voltage doubler circuit acting as a power detector, and a homogeneous phantom mimicking the human body. The setup is capable of supplying maximum DC power of about 350 µW at the output for an input radio frequency (RF) power of 30 dBm. The DC output power can be used in driving implanted sensors for pacemaker and glucose monitoring systems.

articleTitle: A New Design Approach for FMCW Radar using Multiple PPL for Better Range Resolution
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A new design approach for FMCW radar using multiple PLLs is proposed for better range resolution. Design and simulation of the proposed scheme is presented in this paper. Simulation has been carried out with multiple PLLs in such a way that the PLLs combined together in precise and easy manner to produce a transmitting signal which has a triangular waveform for frequency variation with a much larger bandwidth than the PLLs individually. To achieve a range resolution of 3m with a target at 5532m distance a transmitter is designed signal with 77GHz carrier frequency and 50MHz of chirp bandwidth using a single PLL and then same transmitter is design with two PLLs as proposed. The achieved results are same which establishes the proof of the concept.

articleTitle: Microstrip Antenna with A New Kind of External Loading for Improved Backside Radiation and Enhanced Polarization Purity
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Two coax-fed stub loaded microstrip antennas have been designed and studied here. The idea has been evolved in need of developing a planar improved polarization purity and low backside radiation patch compared to a non-planar configuration published in a recent article by the same author. The proposed structures show 10dB enhanced co-to-cross isolation. One of them shows low backside radiation. An X-band prototype has been fabricated and examined using an in-house measurement facility. 15dB isolation has been achieved in the H-plane following 25dB in the E-plane. Also, a trace of suppressing backside radiation has been identified.

articleTitle: Efficient Rectifier for Ambient RF Energy Harvesting at 2.4-GHz WLAN Frequency Band
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This work presents the design of an efficient rectifier that can be used for RF energy harvesting from 2.4 GHz WLAN frequency band (IEEE 802.11). Since the ambient RF power available is very low (-30 dBm), the designed rectifier circuit focuses on obtaining high power conversion efficiency (PCE) at low input power. At 2.45 GHz, the rectifier circuit gives PCE of 8.9% at -25 dBm and 60.2% at -3 dBm. A load resistor of 1540Ω is connected at the rectifier's output for optimum performance. The circuit is designed in ADS using SMS7630-079LF diode from Skyworks Solutions and fabricated on Rogers RT/duroid 5880 substrate with a thickness of 0.79 mm. At low input power of -25 dBm, power conversion efficiency of the design is reduced with PCE of 8.9% and the conversion efficiency reaches 44% at input power of -10 dBm. This efficient rectifier can be used in rectenna design for RF energy harvesting for application to low power IoT sensors.

articleTitle: Stub-Loaded Uniplanar Monopole Antenna for Circular Polarization
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents a circularly polarized stub-loaded inverted L-shaped planar monopole antenna. Circular polarization (CP) is achieved with the help of stubs attached to the inverted L-shaped radiator. The proposed antenna provides circular polarization with good impedance matching over a broad frequency range of (7.8 - 8.5 GHz). Further, the antenna shows right hand circular polarization (RHCP) with a cross-polar difference (XPD) of more than 20 dB, slightly directional radiation pattern, peak realized gain of 3.7 dBi, and radiation efficiency of more than 90 % over coinciding impedance bandwidth (IMBW) and axial ratio bandwidth (ARBW) of 8.6 % which makes antenna useful for X-band applications. The proposed antenna has very simple geometry and is excited with coplanar waveguide (CPW) feed which makes it uniplanar, low-profile, and cost-effective. In addition, the sense of CP can be changed from RHCP to LHCP by the mirror-image configuration of the proposed antenna.

articleTitle: 3-D Triple Band and Wideband Antenna for V2X Communications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents a triple band and wideband antenna for the vehicular to everything (V2X) communications. The proposed antenna is a 3-dimensional (D) structure operating in industrial scientific and medical (ISM) bands like 2.12-2.25 GHz, 2.4-2.5 GHz, and 3.5-6.5 GHz covering vehicle to everything (V2X) 5.8-5.9 GHz bands with a -10 dB impedance bandwidth criterion. It is a low-cost, low payload structure with the overall dimensions of <tex>$\mathbf{60}\mathbf{mm}\times \mathbf{25}\mathbf{mm}\times \mathbf{5}\mathbf{mm}$</tex>. The antenna has been placed on a 90mm radius circular ground plane for the vehicular mount. The peak realized gain values of the antenna at 2.2 GHz, 2.45 GHz, and 5.9 GHz are 8.2 dBi, 8.4 dBi, and 7.8 dBi, respectively. The simulated total antenna efficiency is better than 89.9% making it suitable for the intended applications. The antenna has promising results and can find a wide range of applications in the V2X communication. The multiple-input-multiple-output (MIMO) implementation and other results would be presented during the conference.

articleTitle: Low Profile Triple Band Metasurface Based ME-Dipole Antenna
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A triple band, low profile, metasurface based ME-dipole antenna is proposed in this work. The composite antenna structure has one ME-dipole antenna topped by a suitable dual-band metasurface, which resulted in triple band response. The electric dipole was constructed by employing four quasi-square patches and fed with an L-probe. The magnetic dipole was obtained by introducing four sets of closely spaced via holes located at the inner corners of the quasi-square patches. The metasurface has two concentric split squares as unit cell. The three bands were reported at 11.3-12.51GHz, 13.78-14.3GHz and 16.11-17.88GHz, with fractional bandwidths of 20%, 7.42% and 21.85% respectively, with a peak gain of 7.57dBi. The profile of the antenna was found to be only 0.04λ<inf>0</inf>.

articleTitle: Broadband High-Gain SIW based H-Plane Horn Antenna for 5G mmWave Communications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, a high-gain substrate integrated waveguide (SIW)-based H-plane sectoral horn antenna is presented with multi-layer multi-dielectric extended slab and additional vias. The proposed SIW horn antenna has 21.32% 10-dB impedance bandwidth (24.9 - 31 GHz) with improved front-to-back ratio as compared with conventional horn antenna. The proposed antenna has the average gain of 13 dBi throughout the entire operating frequency band of the antenna. This antenna can be used in 5G mmWave wireless communications.

articleTitle: 5G Compact Planar Antenna for Multiple Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A 5G antenna for multiple applications is presented in the following paper. The presented geometry is capable of radiating the large frequency band from 2.6 to 20GHz, which covers the 5G-(I) Sub-6GHz band, X-Band/Ku-Band Communication with high efficiency. The impedance bandwidth of the radiator is 153%, with an electrical size of. 13λx.13λx0.030λ in lambda. The antenna is simulated with an FR4 substrate using CST Simulator. 04-stages evolution process is also investigated by simulations, and corresponding S-parameter results are presented. The proposed structure also demonstrates stable radiation patterns across the operating bandwidth. The proposed radiator has a high gain of 3.7 dBi, and an efficiency of 85%. Therefore, it is useful for 5G-(I) Sub-6GHz band, X-band, and Ku-band applications, including Mobile, Radar, Space, Terrestrial, and Satellite microwave communication.

articleTitle: Multilayer Cross-Coupled SIW Filter With Next Harmonic Suppression
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) filters with multilayer configuration are presented. Such configurations reduce circuit footprint area without compromising the passband loss. Here it is shown that a metallic post can provide magnetic as well as electric coupling. Further, it is shown that proper placement of the slots, used here to obtain coupling between two adjacent layers, can provide next harmonic suppression. Finally, a four-pole prototype is designed which provides symmetrically placed transmission zeros. The filter offers a measured insertion loss of 1.55 dB at <tex>$\boldsymbol{f}_{0}=2.20$</tex> GHz. The stopband rejections are at least 40 dB at <tex>$(\boldsymbol{f}_{0}\pm 0.2)$</tex> GHz and the next harmonic is suppressed at least by 28 dB.

articleTitle: Gain and Isolation Enhancement of MIMO Antenna for WLAN Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper frequency selective surface (FSS) and defected ground structure (DGS) is used in Multiple input and multiple output (MIMO) Microstrip patch antenna for gain and isolation enhancement for WLAN applications. The FSS structure is used to enhance the isolation from -16dB to -24 dB by utilising its filtering characteristics. The edge-to-edge distance between the antenna element is taken as 0.14 <tex>$\boldsymbol{\lambda}_{\mathbf{o}}$</tex>. The gain is improved by 32% and isolation by 50% by using a simple DGS structure. The material used in the design is low-cost FR-4 with dimension <tex>$\mathbf{40}\times \mathbf{35}\times\mathbf{1.6}\mathbf{mm}^{\mathbf{3}}$</tex>. The diversity parameters of the designed MIMO like ECC and DG are calculated as <.0001 and >9.99 which proves the design to be the better candidate for WLAN applications.

articleTitle: Matching, Scanning and Radiation Characteristics of Wide-Scanning Angle Phased Array with Printed Dipole Antenna with Parasitic Elements at Ku-band
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents a wide-scanning angle phased array with printed dipole antenna with parasitic elements at Ku-band. Printed dipole antenna is designed with a parasitic strip and a parasitic director to control active matching results in E-and H-planes respectively. Active matching in E-plane can be controlled by optimizing the length of parasitic strip and in H-plane by introducing a parasitic director. Introducing parasitic director to improve active matching in H-plane is the novelty of this work. Active matching results of printed dipole in an infinite array environment are presented. Matching, scanning and radiation characteristics of finite circular 164-element array are also presented. Design of antenna array shows a scan volume of ± 60 degrees, with active scan reflection coefficient (ARC) of better than -12 dB in E-plane and better than -15 dB in H-plane. A linear array of 1x14 is realized for validation of simulation results. Comparison of measurement and simulation results of 1x14 linear array are presented.

articleTitle: Analysis of Protective Coating for Optically Transparent Microwave Metamaterial Absorber
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: The Indium Tin Oxide (ITO) coated Polyethylene Terephthalate (PET) sheets are potentially used to fabricate the transparent microwave metamaterial absorbers (MMA). However, the fragile ITO coatings easily get scratched during vigorous handling which deteriorate their electrical conductivity. Consequently, electromagnetic performance of such MMA structures changes over time. This can be controlled by packaging the MMA using polymer protective coating. Simulations are performed to investigate the EM response of ITO-PET sheets within X-band, before and after a thin layer of protective coating (dielectric constant between 2 and 3). Microwave absorption of ITO with sheet resistance equal to 10 <tex>$\Omega/\square$</tex> (ITO (10)) and 100 <tex>$\Omega/\square$</tex> (ITO (100)) found to be 9.6% and 45.3% before as well as after the coating of thickness ranging between 10 to 30 µm, After these protective coating, the MMA employed with ITO (10) and ITO (100) also yield approximately similar microwave absorption within broad frequency range of 4–18 GHz and the angular response is also maintained. Hence, service life of MMA can be increased by using polymer protective coatings without any deterioration in their electromagnetic response.

articleTitle: FM Based Passive Radar Tracking of Targets Under Poor Waveforms
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Passive Radars do not have their own transmitters. The performance of FM based Passive Radar depends heavily on the type of program being played. Rich bandwidth program results in fewer false detections owing to better cancellation of reference signals. At the same time a low bandwidth system impedes the proper clutter cancellation. Hence, the performance of Passive Radars intermittently spoils during poor waveforms. Tracking under high clutter scenario results in lots of false tracks. This paper provides an approach for bistatic tracking and a simple but effective scheme to alleviate false tracks without greatly impacting tracking of targets during poor waveform intervals. The paper also provides the comparison with and without the scheme on real-time data collected from the deployed sensors.

articleTitle: On the CSRR Loaded Microstrip Patch Antennas: A Class of Metamaterial-inspired Radiators
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, we critically examine the impedance matching, far-field radiation performance and near-field reactive energy density for a class of metamaterial-inspired compact multi-band antennas, namely microstrip patch antennas loaded with CSRRs (complementary split ring resonators). Using full-wave simulation via MoM (Method of Moments) based MATLAB Antenna Toolbox, we demonstrate dual-band and triple-band operation of the microstrip patch antenna close to its fundamental mode, by simply altering the rotational orientation of the embedded CSRR. The proposed triple band CSRR loaded patch exhibits broadside radiation in all the working frequencies, with different polarization states. Furthermore, using the nearzone electric and magnetic field intensities, we compute the EM Lagrangian density above the top surface of the microstrip patch to investigate the non-propagating energy distribution around such meta-resonator loaded miniaturized multi-band antennas.

articleTitle: Metamaterial - Based Mushroom Array Antenna With Complementary Split Ring Resonator
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents a compact wide band, high gain superstrate loaded meta material mushroom array antenna. It uses a microstrip line aperture coupled feeding structure A complimentary split ring resonator (CSRR) is used as superstate in this proposed antenna. Compact and wide band nature is achieved by loading the meta material mushroom array with shorting walls on either side of radiating edges. High gain is achieved by placing a CSRR superstate array at a height of <tex>$\lambda/4$</tex> above the mushroom array. The mushroom array antenna achieves -10dB impedance bandwidth of 5–6 GHz and Peak boresight gain of 7.3 dB. The array antenna achieves a bandwidth of 5.8-6.6 GHz and a gain of 8.3 dB. Good simulation results with respect to impedance matching, gain & radiation pattern characteristics are observed in the mushroom array antenna and later produces more gain in superstate loaded mushroom array antenna.

articleTitle: Design and Development of RADAR for detection of Drones and UAVs
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In recent years, certain nonstandard drone operations have caused many safety concerns to defense and civil aviation operations. This paper demonstrates a radar designed using USRP B210 with custom code for detecting a drone. The radar has been tested under various scenarios with a small drone in an outdoor environment. The present configuration has a range of 40m for a small drone made of carbon fiber composite. The range can be improved by incorporating RF gain stages in the transmit and receive directions.

articleTitle: A Compact Rectangular Ring Antenna with Meander Line for UHF Band Communications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This article describes the design of a low profile compact antenna operating on the ultra-high-frequency (UHF) range for wireless communication. The proposed design contains a probe through which rectangular ring excited, served as an antenna. The electrical size of this proposed design is 0.18λ<inf>0</inf>× 0.17λ<inf>0</inf>× 0.05λ<inf>0</inf> at resonating frequency of 405 MHz. The feeding probe has a length of 47 mm. Here, the antenna compactness is due to meander line inserted on the rectangular ring structure at this frequency. The proposed antenna design provides an omnidirectional radiation pattern with a bandwidth of 3.84 MHz. Radiation efficiency is more than 90%, and the average gain in the working band is 1.98 dBi at a resonating frequency of 405 MHz. Here, a low cost dielectric substrate of FR-4 is used for the antenna design. The advantages of the suggested design are low cost, low-profile, easy fabrication, high radiation efficiency and omnidirectional radiation pattern. The proposed design can be suitable for the underground mines communication.

articleTitle: Dual Mode On-Body Off-Body Microstrip Antenna Franklin for Wearable Device over 5G Application
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents a Franklin dual-mode (on-body and off-body) microstrip antenna for a wearable device for 5G application. The on-body mode adds three-layer structures, skin, fat, and muscle, into the antenna, while the off-body mode does not add a body layer. Design results at the 28 GHz show that the proposed antenna has 8.54 GHz wide impedance bandwidth, a gain of 10.4 dBi, and a compact size with a length of 68 mm and a width of 22 mm. The proposed Franklin microstrip antenna exhibits performance when placed on the human body due to good bandwidth, gain, and radiation pattern. This Franklin antenna makes it a good candidate for wearable applications.

articleTitle: Orientation-Independent Flower-Shaped Chipless RFID Tag for ISM Band Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: The Chipless RFID technology is one of the fastest growing technologies for identification of objects, tracking applications, biomedical and packaging applications as well because of its low cost, planar structure and ease of fabrication convenience. The chipless RFID is considered to be the replacement of the barcode technology with the advantages that it provides like non-line of sight detection, low power usage and implementation of sensor functionality into the tags. One of the challenges to design a Chipless RFID tag is to read tag's ID independent of its orientation. The reader should read the tags ID and information regardless of the environmental structures on which the tags are placed. To ensure that Orientation independent tags are designed in this paper. So, an Orientation independent flower-shaped tag is presented in the paper which produces the co-polar and cross-polar Radar Cross Section information. The proposed resonator resonates at 5.8 GHz frequency that can be suitable for ISM band applications.

articleTitle: A Compact Design and Analysis of Ultra-Wide Band Frequency Selective Surface With Three Closely Spaced Bands
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, A design with a single-layer Tri-band Frequency Selective Surface (FSS) is proposed. The Novelty of the proposed FSS is in its three strictly spaced bands at 3.27 GHz, 6.81 GHz and 9.01 GHz and achieves angular stability up to 40° for both transverse electric (TE) and transverse magnetic (TM) polarizations. Any resonance frequency may be obtained by varying the length of the unit cell, making the design extremely adaptable. This design has Swastik engulfed in an inner circle within an outer circle inside a Square that has a compact lattice periodicity of order <tex>$\mathbf{0.21}{\lambda} \mathbf{0} \times\ \ \mathbf{0.21}{\lambda}\mathbf{0}$</tex>. The design can be used for a range of Ultra-Wideband Band applications like medical monitoring and imaging, wireless body area networks, etc.

articleTitle: A Novel Electromagnetically Coupled Dual Band Microstrip Planar Antenna for Ku/Ka Band Wireless Communications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This work proposes a novel 10 GHz / 40 GHz dual-band antenna designed for Ka-band for 5G, military, and space applications and Ku band for satellite applications. The proposed antenna has been made on Rogers RO 3003 (lossy) substrate with a thickness of 0.762 mm. The proposed antenna has been EM coupled at various levels to improve the parameters of the antenna, such as S-Parameters, efficiency, gain, and directivity far-field. The proposed antenna has three layers of patches which are Electro-magnetically coupled with each other in which one of the patches is connected to the feed line of the antenna and the rest of the two layers are Electro-magnetically with a compact footprint of 40 mm x 30 mm which makes the antenna highly compact to be used in handheld devices. The ground of the antenna is a Half Ground Structure with an elliptical shape and a DGS that has been incorporated to improve various characteristics of the antenna such as gain, efficiency, S-Parameter, and VSWR. The proposed antenna can be used for wireless devices which demand low profile, high directivity, gain, efficiency, low attenuation levels, and excellent radiation characteristics.

articleTitle: Implementation of Noncoherent Media-Based Modulation With a Reconfigurable Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Media-based modulation (MBM) has been proposed recently as an energy and bandwidth-efficient communication scheme where the channel-fading coefficients represent the symbols in an alphabet. Conventional MBM requires the measurement of both magnitude and phase of channel-fading coefficients to determine symbols; which is difficult without using a vector network analyzer. In this work, a noncoherent variant of MBM, called dual frequency-shift media-based modulation (DFS-MBM) is proposed, where only the magnitudes of the channel-fading coefficients are required to constitute symbols. This opens the door for a software-defined radio-based cost-effective receiver for a potentially deployable realization of MBM.

articleTitle: Dual Band On-chip Terahertz Antenna for Short-range Wireless Communications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents a simple terahertz (THz) on-chip antenna (OCA) based on the concepts of Substrate Integrated Waveguide (SIW) and Metamaterials (MTM) resonating at a dual frequency of 628 GHz and 759 GHz. The antenna is designed with a planar structure consisting of a three-layer, copper- polyimide-copper. A 100-μm polyimide substrate is used in between the two copper plates along with a series of vias on the edges connecting the top and bottom layer. In addition to that, the top layer is etched with six rectangular patches on which further linear micro-slots are etched to achieve MTM properties. A microstrip to SIW transition feedline is used as excitation. Simulation is performed in Ansys High-Frequency Structure Simulator (HFSS), where the S-parameter, voltage standing wave ratio (VSWR), gain, and radiation pattern are analyzed. The dimension of the antenna is 1160 × 360 × 100.8 μm<sup>3</sup> which provides a bandwidth of 18 GHz and 20 GHz with a maximum gain of 4.2 dBi and 4.9 dBi, respectively. The dual resonating nature of the proposed OCA makes it promising for emerging short-range wireless communications.

articleTitle: Gradient Descent ANN Modelling of RF MEMS Switch for Defense Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Radio Frequency Micro Electro Mechanical System (RF MEMS) are progressing as an enabling technology for designing low loss, high performance, power-efficient switches which are essential in designing modern miniaturized phase shifters for defense radar applications. In this paper, an equivalent circuit modelling of RF MEMS shunt switches based on Artificial Neural Network (ANN) method is presented. The RF performance of MEMS based shunt switch are predicted for different Resistance, Inductance, Capacitance (RLC) combinations. The proposed ANN-based circuit modeling to determine better RF performance overcomes the disadvantages of the time-consuming optimization processes involved in EM and circuit simulators. In this work, the proposed Gradient Descent ANN model minimizes the design time of the equivalent circuit model by 88.8% in comparison with circuit simulator that takes nearly 45 minutes. The validation of the proposed ANN model is done by comparing the obtained results with the Advanced Design System (ADS) model and good agreement is achieved.

articleTitle: A Simple Frequency Selective Surface Based Reflector for UWB Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: The paper introduces a new simple type of frequency selective surface (FSS) which is made up of a square loop with a plus shaped metallic structure on the top side of the substrate and a square loop structure on the bottom side of the substrate. The proposed FSS provides very wide transmission bandwidth i.e., S21 < -10dB from 5 GHz-14.2 GHz and the size of the unit cell is 0.16λ<inf>o</inf>x 0.16λ<inf>o</inf>x 0.013 λ<inf>o</inf> where λ<inf>o</inf> is the wavelength corresponding to the lowest operating frequency. The proposed FSS provides polarization stability as well as reasonable angular stability. The transmission line modelling has also been provided. The parametric optimization for different parameters has also been provided. The proposed FSS can be used as a reflector for C, X and Ku (partial) band applications.

articleTitle: High Rejection Miniaturized Bandpass Filter with Controllable Transmission Zero using LTCC Technology
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A miniaturized and high rejection band pass filter (BPF) realized by low-temperature cofired ceramic technology are presented in this paper. The design consists of conducting patterns distributed on different dielectric layers. Grounded combline resonators loaded with capacitors are used as a basic topology for the design of the proposed filter. The capacitor has been realized using metal-insulator-metal concept in LTCC technology. To achieve the rejection in the BPF, a transmission zero has been realized by introducing a non-adjacent coupling. The location of transmission zeros can be controlled using the length of this U-shaped coupling transmission line. An extra coupling pad has been introduced to maintain the coupling coefficients between the resonators. A filter has been designed and simulated for Ku-band (12.7-13.0) GHz with 1-dB absolute bandwidth of 310 MHz. A rejection of 80 dB has been achieved at 16.10 GHz. The overall size of the filter is 6.5 mm x 2.58 mm x 0.48 mm.

articleTitle: A Circular Element Log Periodic Microstrip Patch Antenna for Sub-6 GHz Frequency Bands
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: The goal of this paper is to design a circular element log periodic microstrip array antenna targeting 5G mobile applications that operates at sub-6 GHz. Because of sub-6 GHz and simple technique, the microstrip patch antenna is considered for the improvement of communication systems. The proposed 5G multiband antenna is light weight, small in size, inexpensive, and has a good radiation pattern. The primary goal of this paper is to design a circular element log periodic microstrip array for 5G applications, and the second goal is to design this antenna for lower frequency bands (N78, N66, N40, N28 and N3). This antenna has the ability to adjust the channel in the specified bands. Lower frequency 5G bands have been assigned. Here, in this paper, the frequency bands of 5G for Sub-6GHz.

articleTitle: MIMO Dielectric Resonator Antenna with Multiple Diversity Techniques
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this article, a five-port multiple-input-multiple-output (MIMO) dielectric resonator antenna (DRA) is investigated for WLAN applications. Four cylindrical dielectric resonator antennas (CDRAs) are positioned at the four different arms of a plus shaped substrate. The coaxial feed excites <tex>$HE_{11\delta}$</tex> mode in each CDRA. The antennas are arranged in such a manner that polarization and space diversity are established in between the antenna elements to improve the isolation between the ports. Pattern diversity is created in the proposed geometry by exciting another mode <tex>$(\mathbf{TM}_{\mathbf{01}{\delta}})$</tex> in the ring DRA. The ring DRA is placed at the center of the substrate. With this multiple diversity technique, more than 24 dB of isolation is achieved among the ports. The proposed antenna structure offers 10.16% of bandwidth covering band from 5.51 to 6.10 GHz. Based on the presented results, the proposed MIMO antenna may be suitable for WLAN 5.8GHz applications.

articleTitle: A Single-Stage Power Efficient MMIC Based Frequency Multiplier at the W-Band
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this work, a frequency doubler is presented using a single pHEMT with 0.1 μm gate-length for W-band applications. Harmonic mixing technique has been employed for properly terminating the device to enhance the required harmonic signal at the output. A comparison with other frequency multipliers using much shorter gate length shows comparable results. Superior performance has been achieved by minimalistic approach in designing the biasing, matching and filtering circuits. Power is also recovered from the harmonic frequencies that minimizes conversion loss. The fabricated MMIC doubler has achieved a minimum conversion loss of 16 dB over 88–100 GHz with 10 dBm of input power. The circuit consumes only 50 mW of DC power. Spurious rejection of the circuit is at least 50 dBc. Output spectrum obtained through testing of the fabricated MMIC based frequency multiplier is very stable and the spectral purity is also appreciably good. Therefore, the multiplier MMIC is useful for the development of high quality MMW transceivers.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of An Omnidirectional Printed Inverted-F Antenna with Quasi-Isotropic Radiation
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Based on the design of inverted-F antenna (IFA), a scheme of printed IFA (PIFA) with a bent end is presented to realize quasi-isotropic radiation in <tex>$4\pi$</tex> full-space. The traditional ground plane is transformed into a printed strip structure, and the antenna is fed with CPW. Simulation results show that the presented antenna has relative bandwidth of 2% (@605 MHz) where its VSWR is lower than 2. The nonuniformity of the antenna is 3 dB in <tex>$4\pi$</tex> full-space and the gain is −1.39 dBi. Because of its small size, low profile and light weight, the presented antenna has great potential to be used in mobile communication terminals.

articleTitle: Enhanced reliability considerations for manufacturability of space TR modules of Radar Imaging Payload
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: The key element of Radar Imaging payload of a satellite is the Synthetic Aperture Radar. Transmit Receive module forms the major module of such an active phased array system. With increased trends in miniaturization, TR modules are realised in multichannel mode and their electronic density is also increasing for enhanced performance. Each space borne SAR payload comprises of hundreds of TR modules operating in the microwave frequency bands designed for the mission. Many steps to increase the quality and reliability of space TR modules start from the design phase comprising of component selection, redundancy designs and reliability analysis. This covers thermal, structural, signal integrity, EMI, and critical packaging considerations. The quality control steps cover the compliance to traceability, workmanship standards and data pack delivery. This paper brings out the quality and reliability enhancement criteria for spaceborne TR modules at the design phase, material selection, process, and product design as part of packaging, and test and characterization phases. The manufacturability aspects to improve the reliability of the large quantity TR modules are also discussed. The C band TR modules for RISAT-1A, which is successfully launched, are considered as case study for discussions in this paper. The numerical estimation of reliability of these TR modules is 0.999018 for a 5-year life with 10% duty cycle operation.

articleTitle: Radio Wave Propagation Analysis Using a Dual Polarized Antenna with BSF Characteristics for 4G and 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A dual-band and dual slant <tex>$\pm \mathbf{45}\ \mathbf{deg}$</tex> polarized inverted omega shape loaded MIMO antenna element, operating for 4G LTE-A (2.3-2.4 GHz) and 5G (3.4-3.6 GHz) applications is presented. A dual-band is realized by introducing the inverted omega (mho) shape loaded with the planar printed dipole antenna element. Dual slant ±45 deg polarization is achieved by utilizing two such modified dipole antennas in orthogonal orientation. Unidirectional radiation for 4G and 5G simultaneous operation is achieved by concatenating the electric conductor as a ground plane. The antenna is backed by a metallic ground plane at <tex>$\boldsymbol{\lambda}/\mathbf{4}$</tex> for 4G and 5G operations. The antenna exhibits a beam width of 72 deg and 89 deg with a gain of 7.32 dB and 8.12 dB for a VSWR of 1.5 and 2.0 in the 4G and 5G frequency bands, respectively. radio network planning and wave propagation analysis have been carried out to study the antenna performance in the real-time scenario using 64 QAM and 256 QAM modulation schemes for the DPM model. The obtained downlink/uplink data rate are 3.826/2.8 Mbps respectively and the uplink/downlink throughput were 1044/800 Mbps respectively for the proposed four-stream MIMO antenna configuration at the deployed cell sites.

articleTitle: SIW Fed HEM Mode Excited Cylindrical DRA Array for Automotive Radar Application
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: The design of a Substrate Integrated Waveguide (SIW) fed Hybrid Electromagnetic Mode (HEM) cylindrical dielectric resonator antenna (CDRA) array at 24 GHz in travelling wave mode propagation is proposed in this paper. A 1:2 Y junction power divider is designed to feed the CDRA through transverse slots. Each arm of the power divider has two slots over which the CDRAs are mounted. The <tex>$\mathbf{2}\times \mathbf{2}$</tex> prototype, designed using 3D EM simulation software ANSYS HFSS, yields a maximum realized gain of 9.6 dBi with a bandwidth of 4.5 GHz. The prototype is designed as unit element for the application of collision avoidance in automotive radars.

articleTitle: A Wideband High Directional Bow - Tie Antenna for Automatic Dependent Surveillance - Broadcast
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents a design technology on wideband high directional bow-tie antenna, operating within 0.976 - 1.252 GHz band, for Automatic Dependent Surveillance - Broadcast (ADS - B) communication technologies. The proposed antenna is printed on Rogers RO3010 substrate of dimensions 90×125 mm<sup>2</sup>having a relative permittivity of 10.2 and thickness of 1.6mm. Peak gain varies between 3.33dBi - 4.61dBi within the operating region for radiating electromagnetic energy. This structure also adopts three director elements on the top and bottom planes to maintain high directional behaviour. The fabricated prototype is verified with simulation results and a good agreement is noted. Due to high directional radiating electromagnetic wave, wideband, compact size and simple structure it can be used in ADS - B systems along with GPR and other L-band applications.

articleTitle: Broadband Slot Coupled Ku-Band Orthomode Transducer for SATCOM Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents the design, simulation, development and characterization of a wideband, compact slot-coupled Ku-band Orthomode Transducer (OMT) for dual liner (horizontal and vertical) polarizations application. The designed OMT covers the frequency range of 10.5GHz- 13.5GHz for both linear polarizations. The OMT is fabricated and port to port isolation greater than 45dB is obtained in the measurement. Analogy of cavity resonance has been included in the design to achieve broadband operation for the slot-coupled polarization. Proposed analogy is useful to have dual band or wideband operation for the polarization, which is catered on coupled port. The presented OMT is compact in size and measured results shows a 25% bandwidth for 20dB Return Loss (RL).

articleTitle: A Dual-Polarized L-S-Band Frequency-Selective Rasorber With Highly Selective Transmission Response
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A L-S band frequency selective rasorber (FSR) with a highly selective transmission window in-between two absorption bands is presented. The FSR consists of lossy and lossless frequency selective surface (FSS) layers at the top and bottom substrate layers, respectively, with an air gap in the middle. The lossy FSS comprises a modified Jerusalem cross element loaded with lumped resistors. The lossless FSS layers at the bottom include a second-order bandpass filter made of a square patch and aperture. The simulated results show that the proposed FSR achieves a narrow transmission band from 2.60-2.68 GHz for the insertion loss of less than 1 dB, with an insertion loss of 0.67 dB at 2.6 GHz. The band with reflection coefficients lower than −10 dB covers a lower absorption band from 1.18-2.51 GHz (72.1%) and an upper absorption band from 2.78-3.27 GHz (16.2%). Moreover, the proposed structure is polarization-insensitive and exhibits stable performance against oblique incidences up to 30 deg. In addition, a patch antenna has been integrated with the proposed rasorber, demonstrating its capability to realize a low radar cross-section radiating system while not disturbing the electrical performances of the antenna.

articleTitle: Development of an Imaging System for Breast Cancer Detection
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents the design and development of a microwave imaging system for breast cancer detection. A microstrip patch antenna is designed and fabricated for breast cancer imaging. The measurement result of the fabricated patch antenna shows that the operating frequency band of the antenna is from 1.85 GHz to 4.5 GHz and the antenna gain is 3.1 dB throughout the operating band of frequency. Dough and soybean oil-based phantom has been used to mimic the breast phantom tissue. The Dielectric properties of dough and soybean oil have been measured using the coaxial probe method from 1 GHz to 10 GHz. The measured value of the dielectric properties shows the Relative permittivity of dough varies from 31.8-20.8 and conductivity vary from 0.352-6.52 (S/m) and relative permittivity of soybean oil vary from 2.75-2.53 and conductivity vary from 0.004-0.024 (S/m) from frequency range of 1 to 10 GHz. A microwave imaging setup is established to detect the presence of the tumor. We have focused to identify the presence of tumor in breast phantom with the soybean oil and dough-based phantom.it is found that the antenna has capability to detect the presence of tumor inside the breast phantom.

articleTitle: Preliminary Experimental Studies of the Proposed High Power RF Antenna to assist Glow Discharge Cleaning of SST-1 at Low Pressure
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: The wall conditioning system for Steady-state Superconducting tokamak (SST-1) with a high power RF antenna to assist the glow discharge cleaning (GDC) is developed to operate at the low pressure. The antenna is designed as per the SST-1 port space constraints and simulated using CST-MWS. The simulated and measured results showed that the antenna is naturally resonating at ~184.1 MHz and 173 MHz with a return loss of ~12 dB and ~18 dB respectively. The antenna is then made to resonate at 13.56 MHz with an external L-type capacitive lumped element matching network. The fixed frequency (13.56 MHz) RF source is used to feed 2.5 kW of power to the antenna under the matched condition along with the 550 V DC voltage and current ~7.5 A is applied at the GDC electrodes. The initial test experiment achieved the dense plasma discharge of helium gas at ~1.3e-4 Torr which can help in achieving the wall conditioning of SST-1 with Helium gas at the low pressure up to ~1e-5 Torr in the next campaign of SST-1.

articleTitle: Multi-band Rectenna Integrated with Solar Cells for Microwave Energy Harvesting System
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper represents a hybrid rectenna system with a multi-band solar panel integrated antenna for providing support to satellite systems in orbit at the L-band, S-band, C-band, and X-band operating frequency bands. First, the frequency bands that are primarily used for satellite communication in the Leo orbit have been identified. Then, to improve the power conversion efficiency (PCE) of the receiver at low RF input signals, develop a rectenna system based on a solar panel integrated antenna on the appropriate frequency bands, which included an impedance matching circuit and Villard voltage doubler. the output DC voltages of 0.95 V, 0.7 V, 0.91 V, and 0.77 V, and output DC powers of 0.84 mW, 0.51 mW, 0.81 mW, and 0.6 mW at 5 dBm input power and desired frequency bands.

articleTitle: An S/X band Shared Aperture Antenna
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper reports a shared aperture antenna operating in the S and X bands. The antenna comprises two patches with U-slots for the X-band antenna, and an S-band magneto-electric (ME) dipole. The X-band element is placed on the horizontal plate of the S-band element. On simulation, the −10 dB reflection coefficient bandwidth offered by the S-band element is 17.15<sup>%</sup> (2.72-3.23 GHz), and that of the X-band element is 20% (8-9.78 GHz). The measured reflection coefficient bandwidth in the S-band ranges from 3.12-3.22GHz, and that of the X band in the two ports are 8.23-11.04 GHz and 8.34-10.44 GHz, respectively. The mutual coupling between the two X-band elements is less than −20 dB, and that between the S and X-band elements is less than −18 dB. The simulated gain of the S and X band elements are 4.39 dB at 2.7 GHz and 8.4 dB at 9.5 GHz, respectively.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Radar Absorbers using Smith Chart
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In stealth applications, absorbers are specially designed structures to reduce the reflections of incident electromagnetic waves. In this paper, a Smith chart approach is detailed which enables the designer to visualize the layer-to-layer admittance and matching performance of the absorber. A conventional single-layer Salisbury screen and multi-layer Jaumann absorbers are designed and their performance is analyzed with the Smith chart. The parameters affecting the absorbers' performance are analyzed with the Smith chart and possible enhancement methods are discussed. The Jaumann absorbers with 2 to 8 layers are designed, and the impact of the layers on bandwidth enhancement is discussed. The mathematical calculations involved in the absorber design are detailed, and the calculated Smith chart results are verified with the EM solver simulated results.

articleTitle: Capacity Optimization in Coding Metasurface-Based Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface-Aided MIMO
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, the channel capacity of a reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS)-aided multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) is analyzed. A 1-blt coding metasurface is used to design the RIS. To determine the optimum channel capacity of this RIS-aided MIMO, the water filling algorithm is utilized. During the capacity optimization, it is considered that the transmitter has the full knowledge of channel state information (CSI). Moreover, the optimum channel capacity of the suggested RIS-aided MIMO for variation in the number of elements in the metasurface and signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) are presented.

articleTitle: Electro-Acoustic Scattering using Finite Difference Time Domain Method (FDTD)
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, we show the enhancement in the Radar Cross section (RCS) due to dielectric inhomogeneities caused by an acoustic disturbance using the Finite Difference Time Domain (FDTD) method. The acoustic source creates a pressure variation around the source, which leads to a dielectric variation. This dielectric variation increases the RCS around the object. We observe an average of 8dB enhancement in the RCS.

articleTitle: Open Stopband Suppressed Half-Mode Substrate Integrated Waveguide Based Leaky-Wave Antenna for Forward and Backward Beam Scanning
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this work, a novel periodic leaky-wave antenna (P-LWA) based on slot-loaded half mode substrate integrated waveguide (HMSIW) is proposed. The P-LWA unit cell contains two identical open-ended stubs spaced close to quarter wavelength apart to suppress the open stopband (OSB). The proposed leaky-wave antenna provides impedance bandwidth with <tex>$S$</tex><inf>11</inf>< −10 dB between 10.3-15.1 GHz. The antenna radiates in the broadside at 12.5 GHz with 14.7 dBi gain and has a peak gain of 17.2 dBi at 14.9 GHz.

articleTitle: Aperture Coupled Linear Array for Single and Dual Plane Monopulse Comparators at 3.5 GHz
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: The monopulse comparator (MC) is considered one of the important modules of the automated target detection and direction finding system. The present work proposes two new aperture coupled monopulse antenna arrays for single and dual plane tracking. The proposed monopulse array consists of a 4-element linear aperture coupled antenna (ACA) array and a microstrip line comparator circuit as a feeding network. The designed monopulse arrays cover the entire n78 (3.3-3.8 GHz) sub-6 GHz band with a bandwidth (BW) of > 18 %. The gain in sum patterns of single and dual plane monopulse arrays are 5.9 and 8.5 dBi at 3.5 GHz. The two arrays achieve a null depth of < -24.1 and < -25.4 dB between the sum and difference patterns.

articleTitle: Indoor Statistical Channel Modelling For Small Scale Fading Effect
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Wireless radio channel measurements per-formed in indoor environment at the frequency of 9.6GHz with bandwidth of 600MHz to estimate and model channel characteristics. Scattering parameters obtained using ex-perimental setup of vector network analyzer, low and high gain antennas. Using power profile data at various time samples, we have calculated the Probability Distribution Function (PDF) as a function of different distances between the two transmit and receive antennas. Different distribution functions were considered to best fit the measured random power profile data. From the best fit curves, we conclude that Weibull distribution functions best matches the data of indoor channel modelling.

articleTitle: Development of Low-Frequency CI/BFO Composite Microwave Absorbing Material
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A significant effort has lately been made to produce unique nanomaterial composites showing excellent microwave absorption, thin thickness, and wide bandwidth. Many radars' operating frequency ranges have been expanded to the L-band and S-band, however, the microwave absorbing materials exhibiting excellent microwave absorption in low-frequency range have been rarely reported. Thus, in this study, an attempt to develop a broadband microwave absorber working in low-frequency band has been made. For this purpose, the CI/BFO composite is prepared using a simple and scalable high-energy ball milling process; the milling of 2 wt% of barium ferrite nanoparticles and CI was carried out for 15 hours. The CI/BFO composite's complex permittivity and permeability have been measured across the frequency range of 0.5 to 14 GHz. The coaxial transmission-reflection method has been used to calculate the microwave absorption properties of the material. The enhanced microwave absorption bandwidth of 7.35 GHz (1.63-8.98) was obtained for CI/BFO 2% -15h sample with the coating thickness of 3.0 mm. Importantly, because the fabrication procedure employed here is rather simple, the as-prepared CI/BFO composite can be considered to be used as a candidate in the absorption of low-frequency microwaves.

articleTitle: Design of dual octagonal ring elements for broadband and high gain reflectarray antenna
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A single-layer reflectarray with the periodicity of γ/<inf>2</inf>(@12 GHz) is designed. An octagonal-shaped two concentric ring is designed as a unit cell which is used for better bandwidth and phase characteristics. The phase of 540 degrees is obtained by adjusting the length of the segment. The minimum space between the two cells is γ/2. The reflectarray is designed for high gain, high aperture efficiency, and broadband characteristics. A reflectarray of diameter 204mm is designed on a circular aperture. It consists of 156 elements The aperture efficiency obtained is 65.3%. The method involved for phase compensation is the variable size method. The reflector is center fed using a pyramidal horn antenna. The gain of the reflectarray in the broadside direction is 25.3 dBi. The 1-dB Gain Bandwidth obtained is 18.3% (11.2 – 13.6 GHz). Many simulations are performed for the Ku band for use in satellite communication The design is a compact size, broadband, high gain with high aperture efficiency. The side lobes are also suppressed and is 14.9 dB below the main lobe.

articleTitle: A Planar Low-Profile Endfire Antenna Based on Spoof Surface Plasmon Polaritons
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, a simplified, single-layer, simple to design endfire antenna is designed, which is implemented through a spoof surface plasmon polaritons based line.
