A coplanar waveguide (CPW), a transition structure and an SSPPs transmission line that integrates with asymmetric and irregular discontinuities serve as the radiating components of the proposed antenna. The designed antenna generates endfire radiation in the operating frequency range of 10.39-11.26 GHz with a maximum realized gain of 9.09 dBi and the maximum efficiency of radiation is 70%.

articleTitle: Experimental Realization of Dual-Polarized Cylindrical Shaped Microwave Network Cloak
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, the experimental verification on the performance of a dual-polarized microwave network based invisibility cloak is demonstrated. A microstrip slotted square patch is used as the unit cell of the cylindrical shaped cloak to achieve the invisibility effects at around 1.35 GHz and 1.67 GHz for transverse electric (TE) and transverse magnetic (TM) polarization states of the incident wave, respectively. The thickness of the proposed cloak design is <tex>$\mathbf{0.012}\lambda$</tex> and <tex>$\mathbf{0.015}\lambda$</tex> at 1.35 GHz and 1.67 GHz, respectively. The fabricated cloak consisting of <tex>$\mathbf{13} \times \mathbf{5}$</tex> unit cells of the slotted patch shows a normalized total scattering cross-section of 0.25 and 0.22 for TE and TM polarized incident waves, respectively.

articleTitle: Compact and Wideband Design of a Switched-Beam Lens Antenna for Millimeter-Wave 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A compact and wideband design of a gradient-index (GRIN) switched-beam lens antenna is presented for millimeter-wave 5G applications. Two-dimensional (2D) electronic beam-scanning is achieved to cover a wide angular range without sacrificing the antenna gain. A peak-gain of ~20 dBi is maintained over an impedance bandwidth of 43% regardless of the switching state. The proposed switched-beam technique offers continuous coverage of ± 23° for any phi plane with a negligible scan-loss. The sidelobe level remains below −12 dB regardless of the switching state.

articleTitle: 1-Bit Circular Polarization Reflectarray Antenna for Uplink Satellite Communication at Ka-Band
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents the design of a reflectarray antenna having circular polarization (CP) for satellite communication applications. The antenna operates in the frequency range of 29-30.2 GHz with an impedance bandwith percentage of 4% and an overlapping 3dB axial ratio bandwidth of 1.25% (29.3-29.67 GHz). The phase delay elements of the proposed reflectarray antenna consist of the metallic rings whose inner and outer radius dimensions are varied to obtain the phase difference between two elements. The phase distribution along the surface of the reflectarray panel is quantized into two levels (0 and π) to obtain a 1-bit reflectarray. The size of the phase delay elements is 0.29λ x 0.29λ x 0.15λ (λ is corresponding to wavelength at 29.5 GHz). A corner truncated CP patch acts as a feeding antenna. The reflectarray antenna gives gain of 20.6 dBiC at 29.5 GHz. The reflectarray is fabricated and the performance parameters are experimentally verified. The simulated and experimental results comply well with each other.

articleTitle: A Novel Design of SIW-based Phase Shifter for Electronic Beam Switching in Millimeter Wave 5G
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: An advanced design of an antenna array with electronic beam switching is proposed for millimeter-wave 5G applications. Electronically reconfigurable phase shifters are employed to control the phase difference between the array elements. Eight rectangular dielectric resonator antennas (DRAs) are excited by using the radiating slots on the surface integrated waveguide (SIW). To realize the phase shifter, a number of electronically switchable Vias, made of liquid metal (LM), are implanted within the SIW. A maximum tilt of <tex>$\pm 38^{\circ}$</tex> along the SIW guide is achieved by adjusting the phase difference between the array elements electronically. An impedance bandwidth of 16.2% is maintained for all switching states. About 13.5 dBi peak-gain is achieved from a compact SIW-fed DRA array <tex>$(5.3 \lambda \times 0.9 \lambda \times 0.2 \lambda)$</tex>, while the scan loss is kept below 3dB over the entire scanning range. Furthermore, the antenna array shows an inherent feature of frequency scanning, in which the beam tilting angle is possible to vary by controlling the operating frequency.

articleTitle: Circular Ring-Shaped Patch Antenna for Automotive Communication and DSRC Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: The proposed work presents a compact antenna which is used for automotive applications. The proposed antenna is designed using polyamide substrate which is having dielectric constant of 2.9 and having dimensions of 25 × 30 × 0.1 mm3. The proposed antenna is having Circular radiating patch which later modified to get desired band of frequencies. The proposed antenna is focused to work at 4.25-6.8 GHz (WLAN, DSRC, WAVE, V2X) bands for vehicular communications. The other antenna parameters such as gain (which varied between 3.2-4.1 at working bands) is analyzed for antenna. The antenna is placed on vehicular environment scenario and checked its reliability when it is placed on different vehicular positions. The simulated obtained results tell the antenna is suitable to use for vehicular communication and for dedicated short range communications.

articleTitle: A Printed UWB Monopole Antenna Based on Bistable Composite Laminates
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Bistable insulating dielectric materials have been widely applied to antenna design at mobile communication terminals due to their bistable composite cylindrical configurations. In this paper, a printed monopole antenna with a disc-shaped metal radiator is designed, using bistable glass fiber reinforced polymer composite materials as the PCB dielectric substrate to achieve antenna pattern reconfiguration. The antenna, fed with a microstrip line, has an ultra-wide impedance bandwidth under both steady-state configurations, and can reach a VSWR<2 at 2.4GHz-10.2GHz. Moreover, the antenna pattern under the two configurations has traditional doughnut-shaped radiation and quasi-isotropic radiation, respectively. The proposed antenna has a small size and can be applied to various mobile communication terminals.

articleTitle: GaN-HEMT Based Common-Gate LNA MMIC with Integrated Switch for Compact 5G Transceivers
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A novel two-stage GaN-HEMT low-noise amplifier with an integrated switch configuring common-gate transistors is presented in this paper. It is intended to become a key component of a transceiver front-end operating in half-duplex mode. The LNA MMIC performs in receive mode as a standard amplifier with a gain of 15 dB and a low noise figure of 1.3 dB at 5 GHz. In transmit mode, the LNA is in the OFF state, providing isolation of around 30 dB up to an input power of 20 dBm. The proposed concept of integration eliminates the requirement of an antenna switch and yields a compact, low-loss realization of the transceiver.

articleTitle: Comparative study based simple analog predistortion design with improved linearization
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Analog predistortion (APD) techniques are commonly used for linearization when the baseband information is not available. It is predominantly used in satellite communication because of its small footprint. This article divides the conventional APD structures into two categories, single-path, and multipath APD. It provides a comparative study of these designs, derives the mathematical equations involved with each design, and proposes a new APD method with a small footprint. The proposed design is a single path APD which consists of a π- network with diodes as load impedance in two branches. The equations involved with the proposed design are also derived. A two-tone test with a center frequency of 3.5 GHz and a tone spacing of 10 MHz is performed for this APD with a 10 Watt PA in the simulation environment. The linearization results are measured in terms of carrier-third-order intermodulation ratio (C/I3). PA with the proposed APD shows significant C/I3 improvement as compared to PA without APD.

articleTitle: A Compact Frequency Reconfigurable Antenna Using RSRR for Cognitive Radio Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This literature presents the design procedure and performance analysis of a frequency reconfigurable antenna using Rectangular Split Ring Resonators (RSRRs) for cognitive radio applications. The presented design is characterized by small dimensions 30×22×l.6 mm^3, simplified geometry and can be easily reconfigured to other desired frequencies by simply modifying the dimensions of the RSRRs. The design has a circular patch radiator with triangular tapered feed line for UWB mode of operation and the RSRRs are used to achieve the narrowband mode. The mode switching is done through varying the bias conditions of the P-i-N diodes. The antenna is designed on a low cost FR4 substrate to make the design cost effective for commercial applications.

articleTitle: Frequency Coded Chipless RFID Tag Design using L and U - shaped Resonators
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Chipless Radio Frequency Identification (RFID) Technology that uses electromagnetic (EM) signals as interrogating signals, is one of the most promising automatic tagging and tracking technologies that has gained prominence in the field of tracking and identification of objects in the real-time over the past few years. The tag intended to design consists of ‘L’ shaped resonators combined with ‘U’ shaped resonators. The tag design is fabricated on FR4 substrate and (tan δ=0.02), which resonates at 2.4 GHz and 5.8 GHz frequencies which fall under Industrial, Scientific and, Medical (ISM) band applications. The proposed tag is designed in CST microwave suite version 2021 and the simulated results are validated in an anechoic chamber.

articleTitle: Electrically Compact Quasi Yagi-Uda Antenna for S-Band Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A uniplanar, compact quasi-Yagi-Uda antenna for end-fire radiation in the S-band is proposed in this paper. The proposed antenna comprises one reflector (ground), one driven, and one director element. A fractional bandwidth of 13% (|S<inf>11</inf>| < -10 dB) with a peak gain of 4.1 dBi has been achieved on a compact size of 0.33 λo× 0.16λo× 0.015λo. To achieve a compact size, the antenna is synthesized using the concepts of a microstrip antenna, along with a U-Shaped ground and a meandered radiating element. The proposed quasi-Yagi-U da antenna is suitable for applications requiring radiation in the end-fire region.

articleTitle: Element Active Radiation Analysis in Multiband Shared Aperture Antenna Array
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Analysis of active element radiation pattern (AEP) in a multiband shared aperture array configuration is presented. The multiband array layout for analysis is implemented by integrating three different antenna arrays A, B, and C operating in multiple frequency bands into a common shared aperture footprint. The active element radiation pattern of a specific unit cell operating in a designated frequency band is analyzed using three independent configurations, viz. an isolated element, a unit cell in a planar array, and a unit cell in a shared aperture array. The active antenna elements of type <tex>$A$</tex>, B, and C operating at 0.225GHz, 0.450GHz, and 0.900GHz in a planar array and a shared aperture array show variation in beamwidth and gain as compared to isolated element radiation. For element type A gain and beamwidth range from 4.35-6.15dB and 102.4°-116.8°, for element type B from 5.50-7.12dB and 50.3°-105.8°, and for element type C from 5.12-6.30dB and 54.4°-110. 4° respectively.

articleTitle: Miniaturized All stop to CABW tunable bandpass switchable filter using U-shaped multi-mode resonator
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A pin diode loaded multi-mode resonator (MMR) based tunable filter has been presented in this manuscript. The filter consists of U-shaped resonator which are loaded with varactor tuned stubs at the middle. Also the resonator is loaded with PIN-diodes at the end. The proposed filter has two modes of operation based on the condition of PIN diodes - BPF mode, when the PIN diodes are ON and switch-off mode when the PIN diodes are OFF. In BPF mode, the proposed tunable filter maintains a constant bandwidth of the passband while tuning across different frequencies. A constant absolute bandwidth tunability has been achieved by controlling the first three modes - the odd mode and two even modes. The varactors have been introduced between the resonator and feed-line to maintain constant bandwidth while tuning. Additionally, the bandwidth reconfigurability at a fixed centre frequency can be achieved in the BPF mode of the proposed filter. In switch-off mode the filter will not allow to pass that particular band of frequencies. To demonstrate the concept, a filter has been designed and simulated to achieve a frequency tuning of 1.1 GHz to 1.8 GHz.

articleTitle: Millimeter-Wave Wide-Angle Beamsteerable Transmission-Type Metasurface Lens Antenna
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A low-profile high gain wide-angle beamsteerable metasurface lens (MSL) antenna with transmission-type slotted end loaded cross-dipole as unit cell is proposed for millimeter-wave applications. The proposed unit cell is highly insensitive to wider oblique angle of incidence of upto 60° and polarization. The MSL array is constructed using a 25 × 25 matrix of unit cells with an overall size of 7.7 λ0 x 7.7 λ 0 x 0.14 λ 0 • The slot coupled microstrip patch antenna is designed as the feed source placed at a focal distance of 20 mm beneath the MSL resulting in a f/D ratio of 0.24. The mechanically steered beams along 0°, ±30°, ±45° and ±60° are achieved by spatially exciting four distinct MSLs with the feed source. Hence, 3-dB spatial beam coverage of 120° (± 60°) is realized with a gain tolerance of 1.9 dB. The maximum gain of 19.5 dBi is achieved in the broadside direction with a gain enhancement of 13.4 dB.

articleTitle: An SDR-based anti-drone system with Detection, Tracking, Jamming, and Spoofing Capabilities
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Numerous cases have been reported wherein drones have been used for eavesdropping, planned attacks on vital installations, and accidental damages to defense and civil assets. This paper proposes using a low-cost Software Defined Radio based system to protect vital areas against unauthorized drones. The paper proposes the use of software defined radio as a radar for drone detection along with Jamming and spoofing of drone GPS to protect vital areas. Real-time tests of the implemented solution were carried out with varying scenarios demonstrating the proposed system's effectiveness.

articleTitle: Mathematical Analysis of Switching HBT Devices
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Developing highly efficient power amplifiers using HBT devices at mm-wave frequencies is in active research due to their high f<inf>T</inf>/f<inf>max</inf>. This paper focuses on formulating a general mathematical analysis of HBT devices for switching-mode power amplifiers (SMPAs) at mm-wave frequencies. This analysis helps identify and quantify the switching device's loss mechanisms and collector efficiency. The analysis results of the transferred-substrate InP DHBT device are presented, which are comparable to other HBT technologies. The conduction loss is the primary reason for lower collector efficiency at the W-band rather than the switching loss. The Push-Push configuration and the effects of knee voltage and f<inf>T</inf> of the switching device are studied to improve the SMPA collector efficiency.

articleTitle: Design of a 3D Printed Meta-Structure Bio-Sourced PLA Substrate Based Patch Antenna
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, a new 3D printed meta-structure substrate is developed, fabricated and tested for patch antenna applications like ISM band, which operates at 2.45 GHz. A bio-sourced Polylactic Acid (PLA) is used for 3D printing the meta-structure substrate. Ring resonator method is used for determining the dielectric constant and loss tangent of the substrate. Two 3D printed PLA substrates are fabricated, one with 100% infill density and lines as infill pattern, another with 80% infill density and Cubic-Subdivision, Concentric, Lines as infill pattern in same substrate (meta-structure) only. It has been found that the alteration in infill pattern in PLA substrate is changing the RF properties of the antenna. The meta-structure design is showing more accurate results as compared to conventional PLA and FR4 substrates. To the best of our knowledge, the meta-structure substrate is used for first time for microstrip patch antenna applications.

articleTitle: Energy Optimization in Laser Micro-machining of Transparent Metamaterial Absorber
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Radar cross section (RCS) reduction is thoroughly studied among electrical engineers so as to attain stealth capabilities of any object of interest. One particular kind of absorber which is in high demand is of the transparent and flexible kind. Transparent absorbers find their applications in various defence related applications such as in wind shield of aircraft and vehicles. Manufacturing of transparent metamaterial absorbers is a challenge as it is always a trade off between electrical performance and maintaining optical transparency. In this paper the authors present a technique of optimizing the electrical and optical performance of transparent absorber manufactured with commercially available Polyethylene Terephthalate (PET) coated Indium Tin Oxide (ITO) sheets.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis for Hybrid Beamforming Algorithm in 5G MIMO Wireless Communication System
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper compares the best suited algorithm to optimize the precoder weight vector for the hybrid beamforming in 5G MIMO wireless communication system. Analysis performs for the different antenna array of the size 16x16, 8x8, 4x4, 2x2 with the mmWave operating frequency 28 GHz. Our intrigued of investigation and performance metric are spectral efficiency and bit error rate. In this paper we show, manifold optimization (MO) algorithm outperforms as compare the Orthogonal matching pursuit (OMP) algorithm and optimize the precoder close to the accurate digital beamforming precoder. Further the size of antenna array and length of data stream, improve the spectral efficiency and bit error rate by great extent. MATLAB simulation result of bit error rate of wireless communication is reduced with the size of antenna array. We demonstrated our result for larger size of antenna array. The beam is more concentrated and steered in desired direction as well as the side levels is reduced in the other direction.

articleTitle: Two Port MIMO Antenna for Wideband Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: With the rising need for miniaturization and wideband antennas in the field of Wireless Communication, the industry always has an impulse to compact, diverse applications and cost-effective multiband antenna. The proposed design is a micro strip patch Half-moon shaped radiating patch that makes the antenna resonate with a wideband of 5.2Ghz with three resonating points at 3.9 GHz, 5.7 GHz (Wi-Fi) and 7.2 GHz (satellite TV) frequency band, obtained by etching regular DGS slot in the ground plane. It exhibits good impedance matching, stable radiation pattern, acceptable gain and appreciable radiation efficiency at the targeted frequencies. The proposed X-mas Tree-shaped design has compact dimensions of only <tex>$74\times35\times1.6\text{mm}3$</tex>, fabricated on the FR-4 substrate. The Defective Ground Structure method is used to evolve the wideband operations with high gain and efficiency. The design and simulation of the proposed antenna are carried out by HFSS.v13 software. A compact Half-moon shaped triple-band antenna stacked with DGS slots for Wi-Fi and satellite TV applications is proposed.

articleTitle: High Gain Cylindrical Dielectric Resonator Antenna Design using Aluminum Cavity for Wireless Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: a novel high gain cylindrical dielectric resonator antenna is proposed by using aluminum cavity as a gain booster and also radiations converter. Here the aluminum cavity acts as gain booster from 6dBi to 14dBi, and the broadside radiations of conventional CDRA is converted into highly directional radiations. This proposed antenna configuration is very compact and it can be easily adopted in any wireless applications. The optimum design is obtained using High Frequency Structure Simulator (HFSS). The conventional CDRA is excited with dominant HEM<inf>11</inf><inf>δ</inf> mode by the coaxial probe feed, which is resonating at 3.93GHz with broadside radiations and the peak gain of 6.73dBi. The proposed CDRA is resonating at 4.11 GHz with directional radiations and with co-polarized peak gain of 14.66dBi. The total gain of 8dBi is enhanced with an isolation of 36dB. The prototypes are fabricated and the experimental verification is under process.

articleTitle: Wideband Multifunctional Reflective Linear and Circular Polarization Converter
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A wideband linear-to-orthogonal and linear-to-circular polarization converter functioning in reflection mode is described using orthotropic structure printed on ultrathin single substrate layer (thickness of <tex>$0.079\lambda_{o}$</tex>, where <tex>$\lambda_{o}$</tex> corresponds to wavelength at center frequency of lowest operational bandwidth). The unit cell of this structure comprises a 45° rotated split-ring and cut strip in the middle. The proposed polarization converter can efficiently transform an incident wave with linear polarization to reflective cross polarization in the frequency bands: 7.63 - 12.21 GHz and 19.34 - 21.2 GHz. Furthermore, a reflected wave with circular polarization in the frequency band 13.85 - 18.50 GHz is also obtained. The behaviour of this converter for oblique angle incidences is evaluated. Furthermore, a prototype of the proposed polarization with <tex>$\mathbf{25} \times \mathbf{25}$</tex> cells of the converter is fabricated and measured. Measurement results are in consensus with their simulated counterparts. This converter could be employed in X/Ku/K frequency band applications.

articleTitle: A micromachined series-fed antenna array for WLAN applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A low-cost three-port 3-D printed series-fed antenna array is presented. The antenna is fabricated on the polylactic acid (PLA) substrate using industry-standard chemical etching. The antenna substrate is 3-D printed such that the principle of micromachining is investigated for a patch antenna and later for a series-fed antenna array. The micromachined substrate in both cases ensures higher gain and higher radiation efficiency than a conventional non-micromachined substrate. The three antennas resonate at 5.8 GHz with antenna 1 and 2 having a gain of 9.4 dBi and antenna 3 having a gain of 4.5 dBi. The series-fed array antenna can be used for Wireless local area network (WLAN) applications.

articleTitle: MLFMM Accelerated Method of Moments Analysis for the Absolute Charging of a GEO-based Satellite
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents the analysis for the absolute charging of an artificial satellite orbiting in geostationary orbit using Multilevel Fast Multipole Method (MLFMM) accelerated Method of Moments (MoM). The integral equation is formed considering a fixed potential of spacecraft body with respect to the orbital plasma environment. A 3D Green”s function has been used to relate the unknown charge distribution and the potential of the spacecraft. The set of simultaneous moment equations are solved by FMM accelerated Generalized Minimal Residual Method (GMRES). The charge density profile on the surface of the space-craft has been computed and subsequently the electrical capacitance of the spacecraft was evaluated from the charge density profile. The temporal behavior of the potential on the spacecraft has been computed considering a Maxwellian distribution applicable to plasma.

articleTitle: Capacitive Coupled Dual Band Dual Polarized Patch antenna for C Band Application
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A dual band dual polarized 6/5 GHz capacitive coupled patch antenna for communication system is presented in the proposed design. There is a pair of metallic rectangular disks connected to 50-ohm connector on the bottom of patch. These rectangular disks compensate the inductive effect generated due to probe height. Simulated results of proposed antenna show that for both linear Horizontal and linear vertical polarization return loss is less than 20dB. Proposed antenna gives linear Horizontal polarization at 5 GHz with bandwidth 21 % and linear Vertical polarization at 6 GHz with bandwidth 28%. Gain for Linear Horizontal polarization is observed as 7.762dBic and for linear vertical it is 8.3962dBic.

articleTitle: Measurement challenges for On-wafer characterization of RF devices and its remedial solutions targeting multifaceted wireless communication in modern era
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This article investigates on various measurement challenges for on-wafer RF characterization and its remedial solutions. Quintessence of on-wafer RF testing in modern day wireless communication on the high demand of known good die has been highlighted here. The types of errors, probable sources, and its mitigation techniques have been detailed here. Mathematical modelling of errors embedded with the test instrument has also been covered in the essence of calibration techniques and further de-embedding methods. Various dummy structures along with its electrical equivalent circuit have also been outlined here. For suitable on-wafer characterization, varieties of probes have been elaborated.

articleTitle: Microwave Synthetic Aperture Radar based Imaging Technique for Crevasse Identification in Glacier Terrain
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this article, a microwave imaging method based on modified synthetic aperture radar (SAR) technique is proposed for crevasse identification in glaciated terrain. The modified SAR technique proposed in this work is able to provide enhanced cross-range or the lateral resolution of the target without the rigorous requirement of the antenna with a very small beam width. A controlled laboratory setup analogous to the glacier terrain is developed here by using materials having dielectric characteristics like those of glacial entities such as ice, air cracks, etc., to evaluate the performance of the proposed methodology in the actual scenario. The experiment results suggest that the proposed methodology can be employed to precisely locate crevasses in glaciated landscape.

articleTitle: A Directional Flared Antenna with Slotted Ground for ADS-B Systems and GPR Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This work reports a broadband flared directional antenna offering -10dB impedance bandwidth within 0.967GHz - 1.27GHz band. The proposed antenna is printed on Rogers RO3010 substrate of thickness 1.6 mm and permittivity of 10.2 occupying a dimension of 60 × 80 mm <sup>2</sup>and efficiently radiates electromagnetic (EM) energy. The rectangular electromagnetic wave radiating patch is designed with an offset-feed which helps in achieving directional performance while slotted ground helps in obtaining wider impedance bandwidth. The flares on top layer, which are isolated and placed adjacent to radiating patch and on bottom layer also contribute to higher directivity in the boresight direction. The simulated radiating energy peak gain varies between 0.723 - 2.30 dBi within the operating band. The fabricated prototype is verified with simulation results and a good agreement is noted. Due to compact size, directional performance and simple structure it is suitable for numerous wireless communication technologies such as Ground Penetrating Radar (GPR) and Automatic Dependent Surveillance (ADS-B) Broadcast systems.

articleTitle: Range-Doppler Estimation for Gait-Detection with FMCW Radars in a Simulated Indoor Scenario
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper discusses a MATLAB-based simulation model to mimic an indoor scenario and detect the presence of a human target behind an obstacle to enable range and velocity computation, verification with set parameters and rudimentary clutter rejection. Simulations, based on three frequency modulated continuous wave (FMCW) radars with starting frequencies at 2, 24 and 77 GHz, are presented. The paper describes the simulation steps involved in determining the important FMCW radar parameters, the design of a three-dimensional human model as a radar target, and the data generation and signal processing steps needed to obtain the range-doppler maps for specific scenarios. A comparison of the observed range and Doppler information for all the three radars in an ideal scenario is presented. Further, non-idealities are added and their impact is studied for a 2 GHz radar in the presence of different types of obstacles. The work presented in this paper can be extended to build a complete simulation framework to study and understand the effect of the non-idealities of a radar system on human gait detection.

articleTitle: Non-sinusoidal Harmonics in Square Microstrip Antennas
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: So far square microstrip antennas have only been treated as a special case of rectangular microstrip antennas. In this work, square microstrip antennas have been presented from a new perspective and a non-sinusoidal harmonic response has been obtained. The feeding along the diagonal has been shown to excite circular harmonics in square microstrip antennas, unlike feeding along the length. Nature of harmonics in diagonal fed square microstrip antennas have been shown to be governed by various orders of Bessel functions of the first kind; instead of sinusoids. A generalized expression for their cylindrical resonance frequency based on a new mathematical model has been obtained using magnetic wall modification and axial symmetry. The accuracy of the proposed theory and expression has been validated with simulated and measured results.

articleTitle: A Compact Broadband High Order IMPATT Based Frequency Multiplier at W-Band
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Design and development of a W-band IMPact ionization Avalanche Transit-Time (IMPATT) diode based 12th order frequency multiplier circuit is presented in this paper. The 12th order multiplication is achieved in a single stage. Since no cascaded stages are used, it provides a compact solution with minimum dc power consumption. The diode is mounted in a waveguide based configuration with a coaxial Low Pass Filter (LPF) at the input and a standard WR10 waveguide port at the output of the circuit. The structure is fabricated and tested. Measured results show more than 2 dBm of output power and better than 24 dB of conversion loss at 94 GHz for an input power of 26 dBm at 7.833 GHz. RF performance has been achieved over a bandwidth of 10 GHz, while spurious and other harmonic rejection are in excess of 30 dBc and 10 dBc, respectively. Total dc power consumption of the component is only 80 mA@15V.

articleTitle: A Low Profile Bidirectional Broadside Coupled Spiral Antenna
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A low-profile twin arm broadside coupled spiral antenna is proposed, and its performance is compared to a conventional twin arm spiral of the same size. Different size reduction techniques have been examined, and their effect on impedance and far-field radiation performance is analysed. A compact spiral of <tex>$0. 28\lambda$</tex> diameter and <tex>$0. 09\lambda$</tex> height at the lowest frequency of operation is fabricated and characterised. Good performance in terms of VSWR bandwidth of 147% (<2) and an axial ratio bandwidth of 142% (largely below 3dB) has been achieved.

articleTitle: Analysis of a Multi-Octave Co-Axial Balun Cascaded With Harmonic Termination
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Wideband high efficiency power amplifiers are required in tactical communication systems. Ferrite loaded coaxial baluns are well proven impedance transformation elements used in multi-octave V/UHF push-pull power amplifiers. Differential baluns meet the multi-octave bandwidth requirement conveniently. In this paper, we explore possibility of incorporating the efficiency enhancement technique - harmonic impedance tuning into the balun. A co-axial balun encompassing a ferrite core with frequency dependent complex permeability is modeled in circuit simulator. The modeled balun is analyzed in terms of even and odd mode impedances to draw inference on harmonic impedances presented to a non-linear push-pull transistor. Third harmonic impedance tuning through balun has been demonstrated by reactively loading (filter) the unbalanced port of balun appropriately. With this harmonic tuning method it is possible to maintain fundamental impedance unaltered by the harmonic impedance network.

articleTitle: Antenna System for Telemetry & Telecommand RF Systems for Re-entry Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, design and analysis of antenna system for telemetry and telecommand RF Systems is presented for Re-entry vehicle. Since re-entry vehicle outer body is being covered with thermal protection system, the antenna system should be of non-protruding type, which is a major constraint in antenna design. Hence, Conventional inverted F-Monopole Antenna and Quadrifillar helix antenna cannot be used for this application. Microstrip Patch Antenna is the best choice for this mission because it is of low profile, light in weight and conformal to mounting surface. These antennas are embedded beneath Thermal Protection System (TPS) (Silica Tile/Flexible External Insulation) in re-entry Vehicle. Towards this, a Wideband U-Shaped air-dielectric microstrip patch antenna is proposed. Wideband U-Shaped air-dielectric microstrip patch has been designed, simulated, fabricated and tested. The simulation and experimental results are covered in this paper. It shows a wide impedance bandwidth of 13.9 %, and peak gain more than 7.0 dBi in the frequency band 2.0-2.3 GHz. Since, Antenna elements are planned to be used in re-entry vehicle, RF Characterization (Frequency shift and RF Attenuation) is carried out due to thermal bonding of TPS on antenna elements.

articleTitle: Design of a Circularly Polarized High Gain Antenna for Cubesat/SmallSat Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents the design of a Partially Reflecting Surface (PRS)-Artificial Magnetic Conductor (AMC) based compact high gain Fabry-Perot Cavity antenna for CubeSat/SmallSat applications. The proposed antenna resonates at 10 GHz and produces Left Hand Circularly Polarized waves. The AMC ground is used to reduce the height of the antenna. Its compact size and high gain make it suitable for small satellite applications.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Scattering and RCS Analysis of a 3D BoR Reference Object
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A low RCS 3D BoR reference platform is presented for analysis of conformal antennas. The proposed platform is created by rotating a plane section that is made by intersecting two parabolic curves. Multiple EM computational methods are employed to analyze and ascertain the RCS of the 3D BoR reference platform. When illuminated with a vertically and horizontally polarized plane wave, the 3D BoR platform exhibits very low RCS in the azimuthal plane, with a maximum value of - 34.23 dBm<sup>2</sup> and -21.39 dBm<sup>2</sup> respectively.

articleTitle: Multiple Resonance Dual-Layer Antenna using Fixed Feed Point Concept and Offset Technique with Stacked-Circular Patches and Appropriate Impedance Matching
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, a multiple resonance antenna is presented using the novel concept of fixation of signal excitation point with appropriate impedance matching in a dual-stacked microstrip antenna system using the offset technique, and the primary resonant antenna (Layer-I) serves as an effective active (signature) ground plane to the atop stacked offset secondary resonant antenna (Layer-II). Multiple resonances happen at frequencies of 2.251 GHz, 3.898 GHz, 5.536 GHz, 6.697 GHz, and 6.967 GHz, respectively. Layer-I antenna consists of an etched circular patch (CP-I, primary resonance patch) atop the retained (or unetched) ground plane, while the Layer-II patch consists of just a single side etched circular patch (CP-II, secondary resonance patch) pattern. CP-I resonates at 2.45 GHz and CP-II resonates at 4.9 GHz. The signal feeding point is common (fixed) to both the antennas, primary and secondary, which share them. In essence, the antenna system consists of two offset stacked-circular patches, with the primary patch serving as the active ground plane to the secondary patch. The standard microwave-grade FR4 substrate material is utilized to fabricate the antennas. The performance of the antennas is verified by testing the fabricated prototypes. The simulated and measured results are found to be in fair agreement.

articleTitle: A Minima-oriented Pedagogy Based on Modified Chebyshev Impedance Matching Transformers
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, a minima-oriented technique using a proposed modified Chebyshev impedance transformer is discussed, which is intended to provide a more basic, clearer understanding of the working of multi-section impedance matching transformers to students pursuing a course in RF and microwave engineering. By extending the conventional quarter-wave transformer theory, it is shown that the matching analysis simplifies greatly which would help a student better understand how multiple sections contribute to improved bandwidth. A generalized solution for the section impedances of this transformer is also proposed. The theoretical analysis is supported by an experimental approach as well, which are in good agreement.

articleTitle: A single layer dual band Reflectarray antenna for millimeter-wave application
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A single layer, dual-band Reflectarray antenna is presented. The proposed reflectarray consist of two different elements, cross-dipole at 28 GHz and, the square ring with inner patch at 38 GHz on the same aperture. By varying the size of these elements, the required phase shift at these bands is obtained independently. The simulated realized gain is 26.3 dBi at 28 GHz and 28.8 dBi at 38 GHz and aperture efficiency are 25% at 28 GHz and 24% at 38 GHz. The side lobe level is −15dB at 28GHz and −22.5dB at 38GHz. The proposed antenna can be a good candidate in Ka band for 5G applications.

articleTitle: A Series Fed Antenna Array at X-Band for Monopulse Operation
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A Series-Fed Microstrip Antenna Array for X-Band Monopulse Applications was designed and analyzed. To make a proof of concept, first a series fed antenna with 6 elements has been designed and optimized. By arranging this series fed antenna with respect to Taylor distribution coefficients we have successfully developed a single quarter, with a gain of 18.5dB. The model was realized on Roggers-5880 with a height of 30mil (0.7874mm). The performance of the array was verified in simulation software and the prototype was fabricated for testing. The measured and simulated results are comparable with less than -10dB return loss over a band of 9.34 GHz to 11.22 GHz. By stretching this work for wide enough to set and accommodate into four quadrants along with the branch line coupler, a full-fledged antenna for monopulse operation can be achieved.

articleTitle: A Compact Circular Patch Antenna for 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi and Other WLAN Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: The following paper is aimed at developing a 2.4 GHz application specific circular patch antenna with multiple rectangular slots, circular parasitic element in the ground plane along with a simple rectangular ground patch. The dimensions of the antenna are 25mm*20mm*1.5mm with Annealed copper used as conductor of 0.018 mm thickness along with FR-4 substrate having electrical permittivity of 4.3 and loss tangent of 0.025. The compact size of the antenna and its operation frequency of 2.4 GHz make it suitable for Wi-Fi, WiMAX, Bluetooth and ISM Radio band applications. The details about design and its simulated results are discussed in the paper.

articleTitle: Broadband and Efficient Doherty Power Amplifier by Influencing Output Impedance of Auxiliary Power Amplifier and Optimizing Impedance of Quarter-Wave Transmission Line
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, a novel Doherty Power Amplifier configuration with broadband and highly efficient characteristics is proposed. It is based on the synthesis of key approaches such as non-infinite output impedance of auxiliary power amplifier and optimizing the impedance of λ/4 transmission line. A detailed analytical analysis of drain efficiency at peak power level and at 6-dB output power back-off level is performed. The proposed methodology has yielded the peak power efficiency as well as the 6-dB output power back-off efficiency always greater than 70% in the entire frequency range. Thus, a highly efficient Doherty Power Amplifier with a very wide fractional bandwidth of 80% is obtained.

articleTitle: Dual Band EBG with low SAR for wearable applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Design of wearable textile antenna in variety of applications needs novel approaches to achieve objectives of compactness and acceptable Specific Absorption Rate (SAR). Various methods to reduce SAR using various types of EBG structures have been reported in recent past for both single and dual band antenna. Modeling of antenna for dual band 2.4 GHz and 5.8 GHz is carried out for wireless local area network application. In this paper, authors propose compact dual band gap EBG structure. It consists of double concentric ring with slot along with inner patch. Important design performance parameters like reflection phase, reflection coefficient, etc are obtained by simulations. SAR values with this antenna integrated with EBG are computed in HFSS on human arm & male torso model. Simulations results show that proposed EBG array structure is effective for reduction of SAR values to acceptable values.

articleTitle: High-Sensitivity Transceiver for Airborne Ultra-Wideband Radio Echo Sounding of Polar Regions
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents the design and development of a high-sensitivity ultra-wideband radar for sounding and imaging 5-km thick polar ice. The design is optimized to detect internal layers in ice from the surface to the bed with fine resolution. The radar consists of 8 transmitters and 16 receivers. Each transmit/receive module is designed to operate either as a standalone system or as a channel of multi-channel radar. Each subsystem is designed and optimized, and then integrated. Each transmitter's output power is 53 dBm and operates over the frequency band of 170 - 470 MHz. A push-pull amplifier configuration is used in the transmitter chain to reduce the second harmonic distortion of the transmitted chirp. A high-power, high-speed PIN diode transmit/receive switch is also designed to operate the radar with a single antenna array. The High-power switch cascaded with a low-power CMOS switch provides 80 dB isolation between the transmitter and receiver. The receiver subsection is designed to provide optimal performance with the digital subsystem. The receiver offers a 20-dB gain over the frequency of operation. Based on laboratory tests, the radar will have a loop sensitivity of about 250 dB for airborne measurements.

articleTitle: High Power Ratio Waveguide Power Divider
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: this paper describes the design and comparison of two Rectangular hollow waveguide power dividers. Power dividers are designed in H plane tee with a straight/slant septum in the tee junction. The design objective is to achieve high power ratio of the order of 1:11.6 where it can be useful for realizing feed network for antenna arrays with low sidelobe level.

articleTitle: Millimeter-wave High-Gain and Highly Isolated Diversity MIMO Array Antenna for 5G Wireless Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: The design of a wideband millimeter wave two-port multiple-input-multiple-output (MIMO) array antenna appropriate for 5G applications is presented in this work. The intended antenna wider impedance bandwidth (IBW), circular polarization radiation, and higher gain response are obtained due to the loading of a staircase-shaped circular polarization converter-based metasurface (MS). Using this concept, a two-port MIMO antenna is designed. The intended MIMO antenna provides a wider IBW of 34.1% (23.61 GHz to 33.3 GHz), a higher gain of 11 dBi at 26.1 GHz, and isolation is more than 30 dB due to the placement of modified mushroom-based MS. Furthermore, the antenna provides polarization diversity mechanism, with antenna-1 provides right-handed circular polarization (RHCP) and antenna-2 provides left-handed circular polarization (LHCP) radiation.

articleTitle: Sub-6 GHz supported Dual-Band Folded MIMO Antenna For Mobile Handset
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A compact dual-band folded Multiple Input Multiple Output (MIMO) Antenna is proposed for 5G mobile terminal. The proposed configuration has four identical folded antenna elements positioned on the sides of long vertical edges of main board of mobile handset. The placement of antennas on the vertical corners of the main board offers extra space in horizontal surface for the arrangement of other circuital components of mobile handset. The combined arrangement of two-folded structure and the open-slots in the vertical ground plane helps to reduce size of antenna and allows two operating frequency bands. A defective ground structure (DGS) is created to increase the isolation between elements. The proposed system provides good impedance matching, isolation as well as MIMO performance over operating bands of 3.5 and 5.2 GHz which is useful for 5G-supported Mobile Communication and WLAN.

articleTitle: Multi Octave Band Spiral Antenna Using Hybrid Loading for Phase Comparison Direction Finding System
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper discusses a Hybrid loaded low profile multi octave band spiral Antenna for phase comparison direction finding (PDF) applications. Designed an archimedian spiral antenna covering frequency range from D to J band, simulated and optimised the parameters using simulation software. Inductive and tapered dielectric loadings were incorporated for miniaturisation of antenna. The antenna was fabricated, assembled and achieved 41% miniaturisation with minimum gain of -10 dBic at lowest frequency of operation. This antenna finds application in PDF systems for airborne platforms.

articleTitle: Realization and Characterization of RF Modules for X-band Phased Array Antenna Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Phased array antenna consists of several components which are integrated to achieve the desired specifications. The antenna performance is governed by the individual components namely phase shifter, amplifier and power distribution network. MMIC based amplifiers and phase shifters are cost effective compared to other technologies. Performance of the microwave components are based on the design as well as assembly process and overall packaging. Also, substrate effect and selection of the package are important to achieve the desired performance. Various process challenges, characterization and related analysis, selection of materials is presented in this article. Further design aspects associated with driver amplifier, power amplifier and switching network are also detailed in this article.

articleTitle: A Wideband X-band Phase Shifter in SIW Technology
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents a wideband phase shifter based on substrate-integrated waveguide (SIW) technology. Most of the SIW-based phase shifters are of narrow bandwidth because of their high dispersive characteristics. Here, a linear variation of the phase constant is targeted by using different tapering profiles. Thus, a wideband phase shifter is designed. An X-band phase shifter with a relative phase shift of 270 degrees is designed and implemented. The results show that it covers the whole X-band with a maximum insertion loss of 0.71 dB. Guidelines are provided for other phase shift values and also other frequency ranges.

articleTitle: Effect of Feed Line Bend on the Performance of Spiral Antenna
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents the basic design of cavity backed spiral (CBS) antenna and its feeding structure. It provides details on how bending in the feed structure will affect the characteristics of the spiral Antenna, i.e. Radiation pattern, circular polarization (CP) purity, CP Beam width and Pattern squint.

articleTitle: Design and PIC Simulation of Klystron like RBWO at Lower Guiding Magnetic Field
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: An X-band Klystron like RBWO with a single extraction cavity has been designed and simulated for its beam-wave interaction behavior at lower guiding magnetic field using FDTD based electromagnetic code. The present simulation predicted a maximum RF output power ~1.1 GW with some stability at 9.48 GHz for an applied input DC voltage of 660 kV, beam current of 4.059 kA, and 0.58 T. The power conversion efficiency has been calculated as ~40%.

Author Keywords: Klystron like relativistic backward wave oscillator

articleTitle: Design of Cavity Backed Slot Array Antenna for Radar Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper describes the design of a Cavity Backed Slot Array Antenna (CBSA) for Radar applications. The antenna array is required to operate in the X-band and to form a very low side lobe (Average SLL <-35dB), HPBW 1.9 deg in the Az plane and minimum 26dBi gain over the whole frequency band of 400MHz (4% bandwidth). The main objective of this work is to enhance the impedance and pattern bandwidth and gain of the array antenna. The proposed antenna has been designed and optimised for its electrical performance and dimensions by 3D EM solvers. To meet all the functional and mechanical requirements, an antenna leads to a linear array of a total of 96 radiating elements.

articleTitle: Design of an Omnidirectional Slotted Waveguide Antenna for Side Lobe Blanking
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Design of slotted waveguide antenna (SWA) with omni-directional radiation patterns is discussed. The antenna mainly consists of slot doublet radiating element and waveguide to coaxial adapter. In this, slot offset and length are design and optimized using 3D software based on the finite integration method. The resonant and radiation properties of the antennas have been examined. The simulated results are in good agreement with measured results. The gain of the antenna is better than 3.5 dBi over omni beam coverage (i.e., 360°) in azimuth plane. The paper presents the simple method to design a slotted array antenna with omni-directional pattern.

articleTitle: A Compact Dual Band Millimeter-Wave CSRR Loaded MIMO Antenna Array System for 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, a compact two-element multiple input multiple output (MIMO) antenna array system is presented in millimeter-wave (mm-wave) spectrum having dual-band functionality, high gain, good isolation, and broadside radiation pattern. Firstly, a single antenna is designed by loading a complementary split ring resonator (CSRR) unit cell on a conventional patch. An array structure, consisting of 2 antenna elements, is then realized using a dual-band T-junction power divider. Finally, the 1 x 2 MIMO antenna array system is designed by intelligently placing the array units to achieve a compact topology with an overall dimension of 47 mm x 25.25 mm. The proposed geometry exhibits broadside radiation at 28 GHz as well as 38.8 GHz with peak gains of 10.48 dBi and 11.21 dBi, respectively, and good isolation values (> 15 dB) over the operating bands. The suggested antenna system is appropriate for 5G applications in the mm-wave frequency range.

articleTitle: Design of the Multiband Substrate Integrated Waveguide Filter using Coupling Matrix based on Frequency Transformation
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents the design of substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) based multi-band filter using the frequency transformation approach. The steps involved in the extraction of coupling matrix elements and the equivalent circuit model for the generalized multi-band filter design are briefly explained. To validate the synthesis method presented in this paper a second-order dual-band bandpass filter is designed with the Chebyshev response. The two passbands are designated at 10.1 – 10.2 GHz and 10.4 – 10.5 GHz with fractional bandwidth (FBW) of 0.985% and 0.957% respectively. The maximum return loss for each passband is 20 dB. Very good agreements are achieved between theoretical responses and full-wave simulations.

articleTitle: A Novel Approach for Thermal Simulation of Mesh Reflector Space Antenna
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: The Space Antenna is an external payload on satellite which faces harsh environment. The performance of Antenna depends upon the stability and surface accuracy of reflector. The reflector is made up of metallic thin wire diameter of 30 micron. A novel approach is evolved in present work to analyze the effect of solar radiation, albedo and Infrared Radiation on Reflector mesh. The result obtained from this study is used as input for estimation of surface accuracy of reflector mesh. The results obtained from this analysis are compared with the analytical solution for verification.
